title: สธ.ยืนยันยังไม่พบโรคระบาดพื้นที่ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พร้อมดูแลประชาชนเต็มที่
titleEn: Ministry of Public Health Confirms No Epidemic Found in Thai-Cambodia Border Area, Ready to Provide Full Care

source: สยามนิวส์ (Siam News) / LINE TODAY
summary: China’s Foreign Ministry Spokesperson addressed the Thailand-Cambodia conflict, stating that as a friend, China is closely communicating with both sides to mediate, promote dialogue, and support direct negotiation and ASEAN's role. This marks the second time China has called for a constructive end to the conflict.
title: รอบนี้เอาจริง! จีนประกาศถึงไทย-กัมพูชา ชี้ 1 ทางออก ในฐานะมิตร
titleEn: This time it's serious! China announces to Thailand-Cambodia, points to one solution as a friend

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) sent a formal letter to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, condemning Cambodian missile attacks on civilian areas in Si Sa Ket that killed one Thai civilian. Thailand condemned the attacks as violations of international humanitarian law and invoked its inherent right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, with military operations targeting only Cambodian military objectives.
title: Thailand submits letter to UN over Cambodian missile attacks on civilians

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense reported that Thai military forces continued attacks in Military Zone 5 (Banteay Meanchey and Pursat provinces) on December 15, including shelling, F-16 airstrikes, and the use of drones to allegedly spray toxic fumes along the border in Pursat province.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 13.30 15/12/25: Thai drones spray toxic gas in Cambodia

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura, announced three conditions for a ceasefire with Cambodia: 1. Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first; 2. The ceasefire must be implemented in practice; 3. Cambodia must genuinely and sincerely cooperate in clearing landmines. The article cites Thai media 'The Nation' from December 15, 2025.
title: ក្រសួងការបរទេសថៃ បង្ហាញលក្ខខណ្ឌចំនួន3 សម្រាប់បទឈប់បាញ់តាមព្រំដែនថៃ-កម្ពុជា (Video inside)
titleEn: Thai Foreign Ministry Presents 3 Conditions for Ceasefire on Thai-Cambodia Border

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim stated that Malaysia is coordinating diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions along the Thailand-Cambodia border. When questioned about Thailand's consideration of blocking fuel exports to Cambodia, Anwar responded that negotiations are currently taking place, while also calling for a complete stop to the fighting.
title: លោក អាន់វ៉ា៖ ម៉ាឡេស៊ីកំពុងសម្របសម្រួលកិច្ចប្រឹងប្រែង ដើម្បីបន្ធូរបន្ថយភាពតានតឹងព្រំដែនថៃ-កម្ពុជា
titleEn: Anwar: Malaysia is Coordinating Efforts to De-escalate Thailand-Cambodia Border Tensions

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Interior rejected Thailand's accusation that Cambodia's decision to suspend border crossings was a violation of international law and human rights principles. The Ministry asserted that Cambodia's decision was made to ensure the safety of civilians, including Thai nationals, from the 'brutal attacks' by the Thai military along the border.
title: ក្រសួងមហាផ្ទៃព្រលះថៃរឿងចោទកម្ពុជាផ្អាកដំណើរការច្រកព្រំដែន គឺរំលោភច្បាប់អន្តរជាតិ ខណៈថៃខ្លួនឯងកំពុងវាយប្រហារដ៏សាហាវលើកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Ministry of Interior Slams Thailand for Accusing Cambodia of Violating International Law by Suspending Border Crossings, While Thailand Itself Is Brutally Attacking Cambodia

summary: Cambodia has condemned Thai airstrikes that reportedly targeted civilian areas, including near a displaced civilians camp in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province—more than 70km from the border. The strikes allegedly forced hundreds of already displaced families to flee again, and Cambodia is calling for international intervention.
title: Cambodia Condemns Thai Airstrikes Near Displacement Camps, Calls for International Intervention

summary: The Spokeswoman for Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence stated that Cambodian armed forces remain strong and vigilant against Thai aggression, which she claims is intensifying with the use of cluster bombs, artillery, and toxic gas in several provinces. She called on the international community to condemn Thailand's actions and demand an immediate cessation of hostile activities and withdrawal of forces.
title: Defence Ministry: Cambodian forces stand strong in defending national territory
titleEn: Defence Ministry: Cambodian Forces Stand Strong in Defending National Territory

summary: As of 4:50 PM on December 15, 2025, the Thai military is reported to be continuing shelling Cambodian territory in the Preah Vihear Temple direction (An Ses and in front of the Temple), utilizing various heavy weapons, including F16 aircraft and drones. Cambodian forces are reportedly standing firm and returning fire in defense of their territory.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 17.15pm 15/12/25: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 5:15 PM, 15/12/25: Thailand Continues to Shell Cambodia

summary: The Russian Embassy in Bangkok denied Thai media reports suggesting Russian citizens were involved as mercenaries in the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. The embassy stated these reports were untrue and risked damaging long-standing Russian-Thai relations, reaffirming Russia's support for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.
title: ស្ថានទូតរុស្ស៊ីប្រចាំនៅទីក្រុងបាងកកថា ការចោទថា ពលរដ្ឋរុស្ស៊ីជាប់ពាក់ព័ន្ធ ជាទាហានស៊ីឈ្នួល ក្នុងជម្លោះព្រំដែនថៃ-កម្ពុជា គឺអាចប្រឈមនឹងហានិភ័យបំផ្លាញ ទំនាក់ទំនងយូរអង្វែង រវាងរុស្ស៊ី និងថៃ
titleEn: Russian Embassy in Bangkok says accusation of Russian citizens being involved as mercenaries in the Thai-Cambodia border conflict risks damaging long-standing relations between Russia and Thailand

summary: Cambodia's Defense Ministry reported that a Thai fighter jet bombed an area near a displaced civilians camp in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province. The Information Minister noted this was the first time Thailand had bombed Siem Reap and was the furthest strike (over 70km from the border) during the renewed clashes, forcing hundreds of displaced families to flee the evacuation site.
title: Cambodia says Thai airstrikes hit Siem Reap, home province of heritage temples

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Monday that a special meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers, scheduled for Tuesday to address the Thailand-Cambodia conflict, had been postponed at the request of Thailand and Cambodia. Anwar stated that Malaysia continues to appeal to both sides to stop the fighting while maintaining daily contact.
title: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar says ASEAN foreign ministers’ meeting postponed as Thailand-Cambodia dispute heats up

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim revealed that both the Thai and Cambodian governments requested a postponement of the upcoming ASEAN meeting. He also stated that negotiations are still in progress regarding the news of Thailand closing off the Gulf of Thailand (to maritime traffic).
title: 'อันวาร์' เผยไทย-เขมร ต่างขอเลื่อนถกอาเซียน ชี้ข่าวปิดอ่าวไทย ยังมีการเจรจากันอยู่
titleEn: Anwar reveals Thailand and Cambodia requested ASEAN meeting postponement; says negotiations on Gulf of Thailand closure are ongoing

summary: Thailand has stopped fuel shipments passing through a key border checkpoint with Laos, citing intelligence that the supplies were being diverted to support Cambodian forces. The conflict, which has displaced over half a million people, has led to the postponement of a planned special meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers, further highlighting the struggle for diplomatic solutions within the region.
title: Thailand Halts Fuel Transit to Laos as Cambodia Border War Escalates

summary: Cambodia reported that its civilian casualties from Thai attacks have increased to 12 killed and 74 injured. The report also claimed the arrest of a "mole" (spy/insider) who allegedly provided targeting information to Thailand, leading to the destruction of a bridge. (Note: Claims about casualty numbers and espionage are unilateral and unverified by Thailand).
title: กัมพูชา เผยยอดพลเรือนเขมร เซ่นไทยโจมตี พุ่ง 12 เจ็บ 74 อ้างจับไส้ศึก ชี้เป้าไทยถล่มสะพาน
titleEn: Cambodia reports its civilian casualties from Thai attacks rose to 12 killed, 74 injured, and claims to have arrested a mole who pointed out the bridge that Thailand destroyed

summary: Heavy combat between Thailand and Cambodia entered a second week. Cambodia claims that Thai F-16 fighter jets dropped two bombs near camps for displaced persons, with one incident targeting a bridge over 70km inside Cambodian territory near Siem Reap. Thailand did not comment, and independent verification is difficult. More than two dozen people have been officially reported killed and over half a million displaced.
title: Cambodia claims Thai bombing is hitting deeper into its territory near shelters for displaced people

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra reported that as of 6:00 PM on December 15, 2025, a total of 126,204 families, equivalent to 421,853 people, have been displaced across seven provinces due to Thailand's armed aggression along the border, seeking safety away from their homes.
title: Updated: More Than 421,000 Cambodians Displaced Following Thai Armed Aggression in Seven Provinces

summary: Citing the Ministry of National Defense, the article reports that at 12:56 PM, the Thai military used many toxic smoke-spraying drones in Thma Da commune, Veal Veaeng district, Pursat province. The report also mentions earlier shellings of schools in other areas.
title: យោធាថៃ ប្រើដ្រូនបាញ់ផ្សែងពុល យ៉ាងច្រើននៅតំបន់ថ្មដា
titleEn: Thai military uses multiple toxic smoke-spraying drones in Thma Da area

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense stated that the Thai military continued to attack Cambodian forces in Military Region 4 (Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey provinces) on the morning of December 15, 2025, using warplanes, heavy artillery, and tanks in Thma Da, Ta Moan Temple, and Chop Kokir areas. The statement asserted that Cambodian troops and border police remain strong. It also noted that schools in 6 border provinces have been closed, affecting 1,039 schools, 9,797 teachers, and 242,881 students.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ ៖ យោធាថៃ បន្តបាញ់ប្រហារមកលើកងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជា នៅទិសយោធភូមិភាគទី4 ខណៈវីរកងទ័ព និងវីរនគរបាលកម្ពុជា កំពុងឈរជើងយ៉ាងរឹងមាំ
titleEn: Ministry of National Defense: Thai military continues to fire upon Cambodian forces in Military Region 4, while Cambodian heroic troops and police are standing firmly

summary: The article provides new details regarding the arrest of a Cambodian national accused of being a spy recruited by Thailand. It states the individual was allegedly promised a substantial cash reward to help guide Thai bombs into Cambodian territory.
title: More details revealed in case of Cambodian, recruited by Thailand as spy to guide bombs into The Kingdom

summary: The article reports that observers are urging the Cambodian government to immediately file a lawsuit against Thailand at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to stop what they view as aggressive actions, including the use of F-16 fighter jets which have been escalating the conflict for nearly 10 days, endangering civilians and ancient cultural heritage.
title: អ្នកឃ្លាំមើលឱ្យរុញសំណុំរឿងព្រំដែនទៅ (ICJ) ខណៈថៃប្រើយន្តហោះចម្បាំងឈ្លានពានជិត10ថ្ងៃ
titleEn: Observers urge pushing border case to ICJ as Thailand uses warplanes to invade for nearly 10 days

summary: A meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers to address the Thailand-Cambodia conflict was delayed until December 22 at Thailand's request, Malaysia's foreign ministry confirmed. The article cites reports of casualties and displacement figures from both Thai authorities (at least 16 soldiers and 10 civilians killed, 258,626 displaced) and Cambodia's interior ministry (at least 11 deaths, 74 injured, 394,706 displaced) since the latest clashes began.
title: ASEAN foreign ministers’ meeting on Thai–Cambodian conflict delayed to December 22

summary: Lt. Gen. 'Serm. Maew' (a former military officer/columnist) advises the government to use Thailand's own strategy and international law to solve the border conflict, cautioning against becoming a victim of great power pressure. He specifically suggests China reconsider selling GAM-102LR rockets to Cambodia and expresses serious concern over Thai citizens allegedly being held hostage in Cambodia, stating it may violate international law.
title: “เสธ.แมว”เตือนแก้ปัญหาชายแดนอย่าตกเป็นเหยื่อแรงกดดันมหาอำนาจ-แนะจีนทบทวนขาย GAM-102LR ให้กัมพูชา
titleEn: Lt. Gen. 'Serm. Maew' warns against being a victim of great power pressure in border conflict resolution, advises China to reconsider selling GAM-102LR to Cambodia

summary: The Defense Ministry's spokesman announced that one more Thai soldier was killed on Dec 15 due to an attack by Cambodian forces at Chong Krang, Surin province, bringing the total military fatalities to 17. He also warned the public to be cautious about information, as Cambodia has hired foreign 'lobbyists' to create a favorable image internationally.
title: ปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชาวันที่ 9 ทหารไทยพลีชีพอีก 1
titleEn: Thai-Cambodian Border Clashes on Day 9: Another Thai Soldier Killed

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra praised the presence of international journalists for reporting the 'truth' about the Thai military 'invasion' and helping to counter fake news, reaffirming the government's official framing of the conflict.
title: Cambodia welcomes accurate media reports on Thai invasion

summary: Thai police have intensified screening of foreigners, particularly in Nakhon Ratchasima's Phol Krang area, following intelligence reports suggesting possible infiltration by foreign mercenaries to target strategic locations. Hotel/resort operators and residents are urged to report suspicious foreign guests. The Russian Embassy in Thailand denied reports of Russian nationals being hired as mercenaries for the Cambodian side.
title: Border checks tightened

summary: This analysis piece argues that the renewed border fighting between Thailand and Cambodia, the most serious since July, exposes the fragility of ceasefire diplomacy and the volatility of colonial-era disputes. It notes that the collapse of the US-brokered ceasefire was due to its failure to resolve the core issue—competing interpretations of the 1907 colonial map—and the lack of a robust monitoring or enforcement mechanism.
title: Thailand, Cambodia escalate conflict, demonstrating limits of diplomacy

summary: Cambodia’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Keo Chea, addressed an open discussion at the UN Security Council, emphasizing Cambodia’s support for strengthening leadership for peace. He detailed the loss of civilian lives and damage to civilian infrastructure caused by the 'invasion' of the Thai military, stressing that the Thai attacks reaching 90 km into civilian areas are clear acts of aggression, not self-defense or mere border disputes.
title: កម្ពុជាគាំទ្រ ការពង្រឹងភាពជាអ្នកដឹកនាំ ដើម្បីសន្តិភាព ក្នុងកាលៈទេសៈ ដែលកម្ពុជា ទទួលរងការឈ្លានពាន ពីប្រទេសថៃ
titleEn: Cambodia Supports Strengthening Leadership for Peace Amidst Invasion by Thailand

summary: Cambodia has intensified its diplomatic efforts regarding the border dispute, with its representative to the United Nations denouncing what was described as 'Thai aggression' during a Security Council debate on peace, urging the UN to intervene in the conflict.
title: UN urged to intervene in Cambodian-Thai border dispute

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence summarized the situation along the border, stating Thai military forces are continuing to fire upon Cambodian forces in Military Regions 4 and 5, which cover Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat provinces.
title: យោធាថៃ បន្តការបាញ់ប្រហារ មកលើកងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជា នៅយោធភូមិភាគទី4 និងយោធភូមិភាគទី5
titleEn: Thai Military Continues Firing on Cambodian Forces in Military Regions 4 and 5

summary: As of 7 am on December 16, 2025, Thailand continues to shell Cambodian positions in Thmorda (Pursat), O3 Chon (Banteay Meanchey), and towards Takrabey (Oddar Meanchey). The report claims that the continuous firing by the Thai military could not affect the Cambodian forces, who are standing firm and firing back in defense of national territory.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 8am 16/12/25: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia on multiple fronts

summary: An analysis piece discussing how the heightened border tensions between Thailand and Cambodia, alongside other global conflicts, challenge the effectiveness of multilateral institutions and regional stability efforts, particularly for ASEAN. Academics comment that resolving the long-standing conflict will take time despite diplomatic efforts.
title: From Gaza to Thailand-Cambodia; 2025 conflicts test global and Asean diplomacy

summary: Government Spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Thailand is waging two wars in its invasion of Cambodia: armed conflict and "psychological warfare." He called on Cambodians to remain vigilant against the psychological warfare tactics, such as the dissemination of false information and creation of fake accounts, aimed at undermining national solidarity.
title: អ្នកនាំពាក្យរាជរដ្ឋាភិបាល ៖ ថៃកំពុងធ្វើសង្គ្រាម 2ទន្ទឹមគ្នា ដើម្បីឈ្លានពានកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Royal Government Spokesperson: Thailand is Waging Two Simultaneous Wars to Invade Cambodia

summary: Residents of Battambang province are reportedly taking refuge in pagodas (wats) to escape the shelling by the Thai military, as the border clashes continue to cause displacement for Cambodian civilians.
title: ប្រជាពលរដ្ឋខ្មែរភៀសខ្លួនម្តងហើយទៀតខណៈកម្ពុជាបន្តរងការវាយប្រហារពីថៃ
titleEn: Cambodian citizens flee again as Cambodia continues to be attacked by Thailand

summary: The Ministry of National Defence spokeswoman reported continued large-scale Thai attacks in Military Regions 4 and 5, specifically mentioning shelling of Preah Vihear and Tamone temples, and an infantry attempt to infiltrate Prey Chan village with toxic gas. The Government Spokesperson also called for citizens to remain vigilant against Thai 'psychological warfare' and uphold national unity.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10.00am 16/12/25: Thai military forces have continued large-scale aggressive attacks against Cambodia

summary: Thai Army Region 2 (Northeast) reported on the Dec 15 border situation, stating Cambodia initiated heavy firing from 2:13 AM to 10:00 PM. Thai forces destroyed a Cambodian vehicle depot and used F-16s to bomb the Cambodian 371st Support Battalion HQ and damage the 795th Border Patrol Police HQ (80% damage). Thai forces are confirmed to be controlling the key areas, despite heavy clashes at Ta Kwai and Chong An Ma.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปแนวรบ ชายแดนไทย–กัมพูชา ปะทะหนักตาควาย–ช่องอานม้า
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summarizes Thai–Cambodian Border Front: Heavy Clashes at Ta Kwai–Chong An Ma

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, intended to address the escalating Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, has been postponed from December 16 to December 22 at Thailand's request. The move is part of Malaysia's attempt to reassert ASEAN's role in resolving the crisis, amid skepticism over the bloc's efficacy after failed mediation attempts by external actors.
title: Malaysia Postpones Special ASEAN Meeting on Thailand-Cambodia Conflict

summary: This article analyzes the role of China's less prominent, quiet diplomacy in the July 2025 ceasefire, contrasting it with the high-profile pressure from the US. It argues that the Chinese approach, which focused on institutional channels and trust-building within the ASEAN framework, offered a more gradual but potentially sustainable path toward peace, highlighting the sensitivity of external involvement in regional stability.
title: Mediation with Chinese characteristics in the 2025 Thailand–Cambodia border crisis

summary: Cambodia has accused Thailand of expanding its military strikes 'deep into' its territory, specifically targeting Srei Snam district in Siem Reap province. This area is approximately a two-hour drive from the Angkor Wat temple complex. Cambodian officials claim Thai F-16s flew more than 70km into their airspace. Thailand's military operations continue as Bangkok disputes ceasefire reports.
title: Thai strikes reach Siem Reap

summary: This commentary attributes the failure of the US-brokered ceasefire to domestic political pressures in Thailand, particularly the upcoming election, which incentivizes the Prime Minister to adopt a tough stance. It also suggests that Thailand's targeting of criminal 'scam centres' in Cambodia during the fighting may elicit little international backlash, balancing diplomatic and domestic political factors.
title: Commentary: Broken Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire a lesson in limits of US leverage

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense issued a summary of the situation on the border, stating that the Thai military continued to attack Cambodian forces in Military Regions 4 (Oddar Meanchey and Preah Vihear) and 5 (Banteay Meanchey and Pursat) from 8:00 AM to 11:00 AM on December 16, 2025. The report detailed the use of tanks, heavy artillery, bomb-dropping drones, and suicide drones in the attacks, while affirming Cambodian forces remain strong and continue to fight in defense of the national territory.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ សង្ខេបស្ថានការណ៍តាមបន្ទាត់ព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ ដោយបញ្ជាក់ថា យោធាថៃ នៅតែបន្តការបាញ់ប្រហារមកលើកងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជា នៅយោធភូមិភាគទី4 និងទី5
titleEn: Defense Ministry Summarizes Situation on Cambodia-Thailand Border, Affirming Thai Military Continues to Attack Cambodian Forces in Military Regions 4 and 5

summary: The National Security Council (NSC) announced a resolution to intercept the shipment of oil and strategic materials intended for Cambodia. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is preparing to charter commercial flights to repatriate Thai citizens who are stranded in Cambodia. Furthermore, the NSC plans to propose increased compensation payments for injured and deceased individuals resulting from the conflict. The Permanent Secretary of Energy confirmed that oil exports to Laos are for economic development and are not being diverted to Cambodia.
title: สมช. มีมติสกัดส่งน้ำมัน-ยุทธปัจจัยไปกัมพูชา เผย กต.เตรียมเหมาลำเครื่องบินพาณิชย์รับคนไทยตกค้าง เตรียมเสนอจ่ายเยียวยาคนเจ็บ-เสียชีวิตเพิ่ม
titleEn: NSC Resolves to Block Oil/Strategic Material Shipments to Cambodia; Foreign Ministry to Charter Flights for Stranded Thais, Propose Increased Compensation

source: ผู้จัดการออนไลน์ (Manager Online)
summary: Thai Army Region 2 issued a summary of the Dec 15 border fighting, reporting heavy clashes at Ta Khwai and Chong An Ma. The report claims Thai forces are advancing to seize important areas and destroy Cambodian positions, including 12 vehicle garages and a Border Patrol Police outpost, which reduces Cambodia's BM-21 rocket potential. It asserts that Thai forces control the battle and that troop morale is good.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปแนวรบชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ปะทะหนักตาควาย-ช่องอานม้า ไทยรุกคุมพื้นที่สำคัญ ลดศักยภาพ BM-21 ยันไทยคุมเกมรบ ขวัญกำลังพลยังดี
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summarizes Thai-Cambodia Border Front: Heavy Clashes at Ta Khwai-Chong An Ma, Thailand Advances to Control Key Areas, Reduces BM-21 Capability, Confirms Thai Control of Battle, Morale Remains High

summary: An infographic summary of the border situation on December 16 reports clashes in several areas. It claims Thai forces successfully retook 100% control of the Chong Arn Ma pass, while Cambodian forces are strengthening defenses at Chong Bok. The Cambodian military is reportedly facing severe command problems at Chong Arn Ma and is expected to retreat to a secondary defense line. Both sides exchanged heavy fire, including Cambodia using BM-21 rockets against Ta Kwai Temple and Hill 350, prompting retaliation from Thailand.
title: สรุปสถานการณ์แนวปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา 16 ธ.ค.68 เกิดอะไรบ้าง?
titleEn: Summary of Thai-Cambodia Border Clash Situation on Dec 16, 2025: What happened?

summary: The Ministry of Commerce states that while border trade has been disrupted, the impact on overall exports is limited. They are monitoring the situation at Chong Mek (Ubon Ratchathani), which remains closed for security but may see restrictions eased soon as supply lines for fuel into Laos are confirmed for internal use only.
title: พณ.เผย ปะทะไทย-กัมพูชา กระทบการค้าชายแดนระยะสั้น ด่านช่องเม็ก ใกล้ผ่อนคลาย
titleEn: Commerce Ministry: Thai-Cambodia Clashes Affect Border Trade in Short Term; Chong Mek Border Expected to Ease Soon

summary: The Secretary-General of the Office of the Basic Education Commission (OBEC) reported that over 1,000 schools in border areas have closed due to the conflict. OBEC is accelerating welfare efforts for the children and stated that core policies will continue even if parliament is dissolved.
title: ร.ร.ชายแดนปิดเรียนกว่าพันแห่ง สพฐ.เร่งดูแลเด็ก ย้ำเดินหน้านโยบายต่อ แม้ยุบสภา
titleEn: Over a thousand border schools closed; OBEC accelerates child welfare efforts and affirms policy continuity despite possible parliament dissolution

summary: The Cabinet (Cabinet) approved a budget of over 2.2 billion baht for the Royal Thai Army and Royal Thai Navy to support operations along the Thai-Cambodia border.
title: ครม. เทงบกว่า 2.2 พันล้าน ให้ ทบ.-ทร. ใช้ในภารกิจชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Cabinet approves over 2.2 billion baht budget for Army and Navy for Thai-Cambodia border operations

summary: The article reports that Thailand is working to repatriate up to 6,000 citizens stranded at the closed Poipet border crossing in Cambodia, amidst fighting that has displaced over half a million and killed nearly 40 on both sides. The clashes, which are ongoing despite international efforts including calls from President Trump, stretch from inland areas near the Laos border to coastal provinces.
title: Thailand Works to Repatriate Thousands Stranded at Cambodia Border Crossing

summary: Thai military spokesmen (Defense Ministry, Army, Air Force) confirmed that military operations along the border are continuing at full intensity, with the goal of eroding Cambodia's warfare capabilities to pressure them into rational negotiations. They noted a reduction in Cambodian heavy weapons fire due to Thai military and air force efforts to target supply lines and command units. The number of Thai soldiers killed has reached 17.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: กองทัพยันไม่ลดความเข้มข้นปฏิบัติการทางทหาร หวังกดดันเขมรยอมเจรจา
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia: Military Insists on Maintaining Intensity of Operations to Pressure Cambodia into Negotiation

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense released a summary stating that Thai forces are heavily shelling Cambodian positions in Military Region 4, specifically in An Ses and Phnom Khmaoch (Ghost Mountain) in Preah Vihear province, using tanks, heavy artillery, and bomber drones. The ministry says the Thai 'invasion' has reached its 10th day.
title: ក្រសួងថាថៃកំពុងបាញ់សម្រុកយ៉ាងខ្លាំងនៅតំបន់អានសេះនិងភ្នំខ្មោចខេត្តព្រះវិហារ
titleEn: Ministry Says Thailand is Shelling Heavily in the An Ses and Ghost Mountain Areas of Preah Vihear Province

summary: The National Security Council (NSC) resolved to block all shipments of fuel and warfare-related supplies to Cambodia, including a seaborne blockade coordinated by the Thai Maritime Enforcement Command Center. This follows the earlier suspension of overland fuel exports to Laos via the Chong Mek border crossing due to concerns the supplies were being diverted to Cambodia.
title: Thailand steps up crackdown on Cambodia-bound fuel and arms

summary: Thailand's continued military aggression, including airstrikes that penetrate deep beyond the border, has caused nearly half a million people (over 421,000) to abandon their homes in seven Cambodian provinces, making it the worst mass displacement since the Khmer Rouge era.
title: Thai invasion triggers worst mass displacement in Cambodia since Khmer Rouge era

summary: Sergeant Major 1st Class Kritsada Harnpho, from Army Region 2, was killed on duty in the border conflict at 7:00 PM on December 15, 2025, confirmed as the 17th Thai soldier killed.
title: แนวหน้า (Naewna): Thai Forces Secure Chong Arn Ma and Ban Nong Ya Kaew

summary: The 12.7mm large-caliber sniper systems, developed by Norinco, are designed to strike material targets and have been verified in recent combat footage.
title: Cambodia uses chinese anti material rifles against thailand

summary: Called on the Cambodian government... to cease attacking civilian areas... BM-21 rockets.
title: Called on the Cambodian government

summary: FM91BKK reporting on Thai Forces Secure Chong Arn Ma and Ban Nong Ya Kaew: Thai forces seized 100% control of the pass, hoisting the national flag. Soldiers removed a damaged Cambodian equestrian statue from the area and secured strategic points at Mount 677 and Mount 500.
title: FM91BKK: Thai Forces Secure Chong Arn Ma and Ban Nong Ya Kaew

summary: Khmer Times reporting on International Observers Note Intensifying 'Propaganda War': International media reports a deepening 'propaganda war' alongside military action. On Dec 18, Thai media explicitly labeled Cambodian 'toxic gas' and hospitalization claims as a psychological operation aimed at gaining international sympathy. Both sides continue to question each other's casualty figures and use of force.
title: Cambodia amplifies media presence amid thai military attacks

summary: At the special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur today (December 22), the Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is presenting three non-negotiable conditions for a ceasefire: 1) Cambodia must officially announce and implement a genuine ceasefire first, 2) the ceasefire must be continuous and verified, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in clearing landmines. Thailand maintains it is not the aggressor and will only stop military actions if these security guarantees are met.
title: Thai MFA reaffirms 3 ceasefire conditions at Dec 22 ASEAN meeting

summary: World Vision reports an unprecedented scale of displacement in Cambodia, with over 421,000 people evacuated. According to the Ministry of Education, 1,039 schools have been closed, affecting over 242,000 students. The organization has activated emergency responses in provinces including Preah Vihear and Banteay Meanchey to provide child-friendly spaces and sanitation.
title: World Vision Cambodia urges urgent humanitarian support as hundreds of thousands displaced by Cambodia–Thailand border clashes

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
summary: Cambodia's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Keo Chhea, spoke at the UN Security Council on December 15. He briefed the council on civilian fatalities and infrastructure damage caused by Thai strikes reaching 90km into Cambodia. He accused Thailand of rejecting all peaceful solutions and the ICJ's involvement.
title: Cambodia Supports Strengthened Leadership for Peace amid Thailand's Aggression

summary: Thailand is undertaking efforts to bring home thousands of people, including Thai and foreign nationals, who are stranded at the Thailand-Cambodia border crossing. The border areas remain tense following clashes that have displaced approximately 500,000 people, as the Southeast Asian bloc (ASEAN) works to negotiate a ceasefire.
title: Thailand works to repatriate thousands stranded at Cambodia border crossing

summary: Thailand's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated three key conditions for beginning peace talks with Cambodia: 1) Cambodia must first make a public declaration of a ceasefire, 2) demonstrate a sincere and verifiable commitment to peace, and 3) cooperate on joint demining efforts along the border. Thailand expressed skepticism about Cambodia's past commitments.
title: Thailand sets three conditions for peace talks with Cambodia

summary: Brazilian Ambassador to Cambodia, Vivian Loss Sanmartin, stated that Brazil stands with Cambodia in implementing the peace agreement to end the Cambodia-Thailand border dispute peacefully, emphasizing that the two countries cannot move their borders and must resolve the conflict peacefully.
title: ប្រេស៊ីល ឈរជាមួយកម្ពុជា ក្នុងការអនុវត្តកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងសន្តិភាព ដើម្បីបញ្ចប់ជម្លោះព្រំដែន កម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: Brazil Stands with Cambodia in Implementing Peace Agreement to End Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict

summary: US President Donald Trump claimed he had intervened to help defuse renewed tensions between Cambodia and Thailand, stressing that neither side wants to see conflict erupt again and urging calm.
title: Trump says he intervened to help ease Cambodia–Thailand tensions, urges calm to avoid conflict

summary: A conflict update alleging that the Thai military fired toxic gas into Prey Chan village, with heavy fighting involving tanks, artillery, and drones continuing fiercely along the Cambodia-Thailand border.
title: យោធាថៃបានបាញ់ឧស្ម័នពុលចូលភូមិព្រៃចាន់ ខណៈការប៉ះទង្គិចគ្នាតាមព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃនៅតែក្តៅគគុក
titleEn: Thai Military Fired Toxic Gas into Prey Chan Village While Cambodia-Thailand Border Clashes Remain Intense

summary: The Ministry of Interior released a statement on impacts of Thai aggression from 6:00 PM Dec 15 to 7:00 AM Dec 16, 2025, reporting no new deaths or injuries in that period. The total casualties since December 7 stand at 15 killed and 76 injured, with 422,698 displaced people. The statement also lists the total number of civilian infrastructure destroyed since the aggression began.
title: Cambodia issues statement on impacts on civilian areas resulting from war of territorial aggression by Bangkok Government and Thai Military

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Defense's spokesperson reported that the Thai military fired heavy shelling indiscriminately from a naval vessel into the O Phluk Damrei area in Pursat province, Military Region 5, between the night of December 15 and the morning of December 16, 2025.
title: យោធាថៃ បាញ់ផ្លោងជ្រំសន្ធប់ចេញពីនាវា ទៅតំបន់អូភ្លុកដំរី
titleEn: Thai Military Fires Heavy Shelling from a Naval Vessel into O Phluk Damrei Area

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation strongly condemned Thailand's armed aggression, including the use of F-16 fighter jets and airstrikes penetrating 80-90 km into Cambodia. The statement cited civilian loss, displacement of over 400,000 people, and damage to UNESCO sites and civilian infrastructure, calling on Thailand to immediately cease all military operations.
title: Cambodian Foreign Ministry condemns Thailand's aggression

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior released a statement detailing the impact of what it calls 'Thai aggression' from December 7 to 1:00 PM on December 16, 2025. The statement reports 15 Cambodian civilians killed and 75 injured. It also states that 423,715 people (127,168 families) have been displaced across seven provinces, and lists damage to civilian infrastructure, including 48 civilian houses, one school, and four pagodas.
title: 423,000 families displaced and 15 civilians killed as result of recent Thai agression
titleEn: 423,000 Families Displaced and 15 Civilians Killed as Result of Recent Thai Aggression

summary: The Russian Embassy in Thailand denied reports in some Thai media outlets that Russian citizens are participating in the ongoing border conflict as mercenaries fighting on Cambodia's side.
title: រុស្ស៊ី ថា ព័ត៌មានមួយចំនួនរបស់ថៃ ផ្សាយមិនពិត អំពីទាហានស៊ីឈ្នួលក្នុងជម្លោះព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: Russia Says Some Thai Reports About Mercenaries in Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict Are Untrue

summary: The Spokesperson for the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, Phan Rim, stated that Cambodia is fully prepared to respond in all forms to Thailand's threat to block or restrict commercial shipping routes through the Gulf of Thailand. He emphasized that Cambodia has multiple maritime cargo gateways and that Thailand does not have unilateral authority over maritime navigation in the shared Gulf, citing UNCLOS and Cambodia's own maritime space connected to international lanes.
title: Transport Ministry Spokesperson: Cambodia fully prepared to respond to Thailand's threat to block maritime routes

summary: Real estate experts note that the conflict is causing a slowdown in property demand in border provinces like Sisaket, Surin, and Buriram. Buyers are delaying decisions on new housing projects due to the security situation and economic uncertainty.
title: กูรูมอง เหตุปะทะ ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา กับผลกระทบอสังหาฯไทย
titleEn: Experts View Thai-Cambodia Border Clashes Impacting Thai Real Estate

summary: The Thai National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) issued a statement on December 16 expressing grave concern over the safety of soldiers and civilians near the border. It specifically called on the Cambodian government and military to cease attacking civilian areas, especially mentioning the use of BM-21 rockets on communities in Kantaralak District, Si Sa Ket Province, and demanded that they stop using their own citizens as human shields.
title: กสม.แถลงการณ์ จี้รัฐบาล-ทหารกัมพูชา ยุติโจมตีพื้นที่พลเรือน เลิกใช้ประชาชนเป็นโล่มนุษย์
titleEn: NHRC Statement: Urges Cambodian Government-Military to Stop Attacking Civilian Areas, Cease Using Citizens as Human Shields

summary: Thailand issues a clarification following claims that Cambodia is disseminating false information aimed at damaging the atmosphere of an upcoming United Nations meeting. Thailand asserts its willingness to engage constructively for peace, provided that Cambodia adheres to its obligations and demonstrates genuine sincerity by ceasing all hostile and provocative actions.
title: ไทย ชี้แจง หลังกัมพูชาอ้างข้อมูลเท็จบ่อนทำลายบรรยากาศการประชุมสหประชาชาติ
titleEn: Thailand clarifies after Cambodia allegedly uses false information to undermine atmosphere at United Nations meeting

summary: The Rak Chart (Love Nation) political party released a statement in English and French on December 16, strongly condemning Cambodia's indiscriminate attacks targeting innocent Thai civilians, schools, and hospitals as 'extremely inhumane' and unacceptable. The party called on the international community to consider the facts, stating Thailand has no intention of aggression and uses only the minimum necessary force to protect its sovereignty.
title: ‘พรรครักชาติ’แถลงการณ์ประณาม‘กัมพูชา’โจมตีพลเรือน-โรงเรียน-โรงพยาบาล ไร้มนุษยธรรม
titleEn: 'Rak Chart Party' Statement Condemns 'Cambodia's' Inhumane Attacks on Civilians, Schools, and Hospitals

summary: Thai forces reported the seizure of several units of Chinese-made GAM-102LR 'fifth-generation' anti-tank guided missiles at Hill 500. The discovery of these advanced weapons, left behind by retreating Cambodian troops, has raised concerns in the Thai military about the modernization and supply chain of Cambodian hardware.
title: Thai–Cambodia border clash exposes expanding arms pipeline

summary: An interview with the mother of Sgt. Maj. 1st Class Kritsada Hansupho ("Jaa Dubai"), a Thai soldier (17th casualty) who was killed on the evening of December 15, 2025, while on duty in the border conflict. She expressed deep sadness over the loss but felt proud that her son died while performing his duty to protect the nation and its people. Local authorities in Sakon Nakhon province are preparing for the soldier's return to his hometown for a proper burial.
title: เปิดใจแม่ 'จ่าดูไบ' ทหารกล้าพลีชีพชายแดนรายที่ 17 ลั่น 'เสียใจแต่ก็ภูมิใจ'
titleEn: Mother of 'Jaa Dubai', the 17th brave soldier killed at the border, speaks out: 'Sad but proud'

summary: Thailand is working to repatriate thousands of Thai workers stranded at the Poipet border crossing after Cambodia closed the checkpoint due to the ongoing border conflict. Fighting has extended into a second week across eight border provinces, displacing more than half a million people. A Thai Defence Ministry spokesman noted the situation is 'still in flux,' and the Thai Prime Minister denied international pressure for a ceasefire.
title: Thailand works to repatriate thousands stranded at Cambodia border crossing

summary: Heavy fighting along the border has forced the closure of 1,039 schools in Cambodia across six provinces, affecting nearly 243,000 students. In Thailand, over 600 schools and hospitals have been closed. The total death toll has reached at least 40 people, including 24 civilians. Cambodian officials reported Thai F-16 airstrikes inside their territory, while Thailand has formally appealed to the UN regarding civilian casualties on its side.
title: More schools close as Thailand-Cambodia border clashes continue

summary: Thailand's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman stated on Tuesday that Cambodia must be the first to announce a truce, referring to Cambodia as "the aggressor onto Thai territory." Both nations deny targeting civilians and blame the other for initiating the week-long clashes, which have killed at least 32 people and displaced approximately 800,000 civilians.
title: Thailand says Cambodia must declare ceasefire first to stop fighting

summary: The U.S. Embassy is monitoring reports of significant conflict escalation along the Thailand-Cambodia border. The alert advises U.S. citizens to AVOID ALL TRAVEL within 50 kilometers of the border due to active hostilities and the unpredictable security situation. It notes that the U.S. government has limited ability to provide emergency services in the affected provinces.
title: Security Alert: Escalation of Armed Conflict Along the Thailand-Cambodia Border (December 16, 2025)

summary: This article summarizes international reactions to the renewed Thailand-Cambodia conflict. It notes US President Trump's claim of again helping to end the fighting; China's expression of deep concern over casualties and call for restraint; Malaysia's role as ASEAN Chair in urging a ceasefire and postponing a special meeting; France's call for both sides to honor previous agreements; and Russia's call for restraint while denying reports of Russian mercenaries fighting with Cambodian forces.
title: International Reactions to New Thai-Cambodian Border Clashes Support Negotiations and Call for Ceasefire Trump Claims Role in Ending Conflict Again

summary: The Czech Republic's Ambassador to Cambodia, Markéta Kolc Hájková, expressed deep sympathy for Cambodian citizens who have lost lives and been displaced due to the ongoing Cambodia-Thailand border conflict. She conveyed that the Czech Republic is closely following the situation and has a strong belief that the issue will be resolved peacefully through negotiation soon. The statement was made during a meeting with National Assembly President Khoun Sudary.
title: ទូតឆែកនៅកម្ពុជា សោកស្ដាយចំពោះការបាត់បង់ជីវិត និងពលរដ្ឋត្រូវភៀសសឹក ដោយសារជម្លោះព្រំដែនរវាងកម្ពុជា-ថៃ និងសង្ឃឹមថាបញ្ហាត្រូវដោះស្រាយបញ្ចប់ឆាប់ៗ
titleEn: Czech Ambassador to Cambodia Expresses Regret Over Loss of Life and Displaced Citizens Due to Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict, Hopes Problem Will Be Resolved Quickly

source: ประชาชาติธุรกิจ
summary: The Ministry of Tourism and Sports reported that the ongoing border conflict between Thailand and Cambodia has not negatively impacted international tourism figures for Thailand. They stated that the number of foreign tourists is increasing across all markets, including a continuous recovery from Malaysia following the major floods in the South.
title: ปัญหาชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ไม่สะเทือน นักท่องเที่ยวต่างชาติเพิ่มทุกตลาด
titleEn: Thai-Cambodia Border Issue Unaffected, International Tourists Increasing in All Markets

summary: This article summarizes international reactions to the renewed border conflict, noting that the US, Malaysia, and France are urging a ceasefire and a return to negotiations. It highlights President Trump's role and his alleged threat of tariffs if the fighting doesn't stop. However, the Thai Commerce Minister stated that there was no mention of tariff measures during the discussion with the US leader.
title: ท่าทีนานาชาติ เหตุปะทะชายแดนไทยกัมพูชารอบใหม่ หนุนเจรจา-เรียกร้องหยุดยิง
titleEn: International Stances on the New Round of Thai-Cambodia Border Clashes: Support for Negotiation and Calls for Ceasefire

summary: The Thai military's joint press center stated it is monitoring whether Cambodia will accept the 3 Thai ceasefire conditions, which include Cambodia having to announce a ceasefire first, a sustained cessation of violence, and cooperation in mine clearing. The military also refuted fake news claiming Thai soldiers were captured and Preah Ta Khwai temple was seized, confirming the temple is under Thai control and that the curfew in Trat province has been lifted.
title: กองทัพ จับตากัมพูชาตอบรับ 3 เงื่อนไขหยุดยิง โต้ข่าวทหารไทยถูกจับ-ปราสาทตาควายถูกยึด ไม่เป็นความจริง
titleEn: Military observes Cambodia's response to 3 ceasefire conditions; refutes fake news of Thai soldiers captured, Preah Ta Khwai temple seized

summary: Thailand's foreign ministry spokeswoman stated that Cambodia, as the aggressor onto Thai territory, must be the first to announce a truce to halt the fighting, adding that Cambodia must also sincerely cooperate in de-mining efforts. The article notes the renewed conflict has killed at least 32 people and displaced around 800,000, with both sides trading accusations of instigating the clashes.
title: Thailand says Cambodia must announce ceasefire 'first' to stop fighting

summary: A Cambodian civilization expert stated from Rome that Thailand has changed the border dispute into an 'open invasion' by rejecting the US President's ceasefire and continuing military operations, including destroying temples and civilian infrastructure up to 80km inside Cambodia. The expert called on the Khmer nation to unite to defeat the 'Siamese invaders' and urgently appealed to ASEAN, the UN, and the international community to take effective action to stop all forms of aggression.
title: អ្នកជំនាញអារ្យធម៌ខ្មែរ៖ ថៃបំបែកពីជម្លោះព្រំដែន មកជាការឈ្លានពានបើកជំហរ
titleEn: Cambodian Civilization Expert: Thailand Has Changed the Border Conflict into an Open Invasion

summary: The 1st Army Region Command (GGL. Boorapha) summarized the situation, stating Thai troops continued clashes in Sa Kaeo, successfully seizing control of an area along the claimed border at Ban Nong Ya Kaew while facing continuous counter-fire from Cambodian forces using BM-21 rockets and artillery. Thai forces report 3 soldiers killed and 53 injured, and noted that Cambodian officials continue to refuse to release Thai citizens from Poipet to return home for the 6th consecutive day.
title: ทภ.1 สรุปเหตุปะทะ ไทยยึดครองพื้นที่ตามแนวอ้างสิทธิบ้านหนองหญ้าแก้ว พบกัมพูชายิงBM-21 ต่อเนื่อง
titleEn: 1st Army Region summarizes clash: Thai forces seize claimed area at Ban Nong Ya Kaew, Cambodia continues firing BM-21

summary: The article reports that 10 days into the renewed conflict, both sides are engaged in a 'propaganda war,' with Cambodia emphasizing a severe refugee crisis and Thailand trying to project an image of normalcy despite the conflict. It notes the low official casualty figures are treated with caution. Cambodia has lodged a complaint regarding Thailand's alleged use of cluster bombs, while Thailand continues to urge Cambodia to cooperate sincerely on demining operations.
title: Propaganda war between Thailand and Cambodia

summary: Thai authorities reported that the civilian death toll linked to the border conflict has reached 16. One person died from shrapnel, while the other 15 fatalities were attributed to indirect causes like traffic accidents or inability to access medical treatment due to the fighting. The curfew in Trat province has been lifted.
title: 16 Thai civilian deaths linked to border war

summary: The Ministry of Defence spokesman stated that the conflict with Cambodia is being fought on three main fronts: diplomatic, intelligence, and military. He acknowledged that Cambodia is hiring foreign lobbyists to attack Thailand's image internationally and urged the public to use discretion when consuming information. The spokesman also confirmed that recent air operations destroyed a significant number of Cambodian BM-21 rocket launchers and other essential military equipment.
title: ทบ. แจง คลิปทหารกัมพูชา ฉกปืนทหารไทย เร่งนำกลับ รับ เนิน 350 เจอต้านหนัก
titleEn: Army clarifies clip of Cambodian soldiers snatching Thai soldier's gun, admits heavy resistance at Hill 350

summary: Thailand has moved to block fuel shipments from reaching Cambodia as the border conflict intensifies, with over 500,000 people now displaced. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul dissolved parliament to avoid a no-confidence vote, setting a snap election for February 8, 2025. Experts suggest domestic political pressure and the upcoming election may be driving the Thai government's firm stance in the conflict.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Conflict Continues to Escalate

summary: Thai forces have seized complete control of Chong Anh Ma in Ubon Ratchathani province following several days of intense fighting. Soldiers hoisted the Thai flag and cleared a damaged Cambodian equestrian statue from the area. Strategic points at Mount 677 and Mount 500 have also been captured.
title: Thai troops take full control of Chong Anh Ma

summary: As of 10:30 PM on December 16, 2025, Fresh News reported a breaking update that all battlefields along the Cambodia-Thailand border, including Pursat, Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, and Preah Vihear, are quiet. However, Cambodian armed forces remain highly vigilant to protect the territory from invasion.
title: BREAKING: គិតត្រឹមម៉ោង10៖30នាទីយប់នេះ គ្រប់សមរភូមិទាំងអស់តាមបន្ទាត់ព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ មានភាពស្ងប់ស្ងាត់, កងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជាបន្ដប្រុងប្រយ័ត្នខ្ពស់ ដើម្បីការពារទឹកដីពីការឈ្លានពាន
titleEn: BREAKING: As of 10:30 PM tonight, all battlefields along the Cambodia-Thailand border are quiet; Cambodian forces remain highly vigilant to defend the territory from invasion

summary: EuroCham Cambodia issued a statement on December 16 noting that goods transport and supply chains remain stable despite border conflict. However, they are monitoring fuel prices closely. The article also repeats MoD claims that as of December 16, 17 Cambodian civilians have died (including 1 infant) and 77 are injured due to Thai military aggression.
title: EuroCham៖ វិស័យដឹកជញ្ជូន និងខ្សែសង្វាក់ផ្គត់ផ្គង់កម្ពុជា «នៅតែដំណើរការធម្មតា» ទោះមានភាពតានតឹងព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: EuroCham: Cambodia's logistics and supply chain 'still operating normally' despite Cambodia-Thailand border tensions

summary: Heavy clashes continue along the Thai-Cambodia border on December 17, 2025, particularly at the Ta Kwai temple area in Surin province, resulting in the death of 2 Thai soldiers. Thai Army Region 2 reports that Thai forces have gained control of the Ta Kwai temple area, but intermittent skirmishes persist.
title: เกาะติดชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชาวันนี้ แนวรบปะทะเดือด ทหารพลีชีพ 2 นาย
titleEn: Tracking the Thai-Cambodia border today: bloody clashes, 2 soldiers killed in action

summary: The Thai cabinet approved an allocation of 2.44 billion baht from the central fund for the 2026 fiscal year. The funds are intended to reinforce the military and shore up border security amid ongoing fighting along the Thai-Cambodia border.
title: Funds set for border defence
titleEn: Cabinet approves 2.44 billion baht for border defence and military reinforcement

summary: Thailand's Foreign Ministry outlined three conditions for peace talks: Cambodia must publicly declare a ceasefire, demonstrate a verifiable commitment to peace, and cooperate in joint demining efforts. Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded by strongly condemning Thailand's actions as disproportionate aggression, including the use of F-16 jets.
title: Thailand lays down three conditions for ceasefire

summary: The Ministry of National Defense stated that at 6:25 AM on the morning of December 17, 2025, the Thai military used F-16 fighter jets to drop bombs into Prey Chan village. This is a claim of continued aggression despite reports of quiet battlefields the previous night.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ៖ នៅម៉ោង06៖25នាទីព្រឹកនេះ យោធាថៃបានប្រើប្រាស់យន្តហោះចម្បាំង F-16 ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែកចូលក្នុងភូមិសាស្ត្រភូមិព្រៃចាន់
titleEn: Ministry of National Defense: At 6:25 AM this morning, the Thai military used F-16 fighter jets to drop bombs into the area of Prey Chan village

summary: China's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Guo Jiakun, expressed deep sadness over the casualties and urged Thailand and Cambodia to prioritize a ceasefire, end the conflict, and protect civilians. China supports direct dialogue between the two nations and efforts by ASEAN. The article also notes Thailand's Foreign Ministry's conditions for a ceasefire and Cambodia's representative's statement at the UN, both stressing that action and peaceful resolution require mutual trust and an end to military force.
title: Actions urged for ceasefire in border clashes

summary: On the morning of Dec 17, Thai F-16 jets dropped bombs in Prey Chan village at 6:25 a.m. Shelling was also reported in Pursat province. The article claims several Thai soldiers were killed at Takrabei Temple, while Cambodian troops recovered weapons and maintained their positions.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.30 17/12/25: Thai F-16s launch new attacks on Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 8:30 AM: Thai F-16s Launch New Attacks on Cambodia

summary: Thailand insists that any move towards a ceasefire must begin with a unilateral declaration from Cambodia, according to Thai foreign ministry. Cambodia, meanwhile, claims Thai airstrikes are reaching deeper into its territory, hitting targets within 80km of the Angkor Wat tourism hotspot and taking a toll on tourism. The renewed conflict, sparked on December 7, continues with dozens killed and about 800,000 people displaced on both sides.
title: Thailand presses Cambodia for unilateral ceasefire as border conflict escalates

summary: Reporting indicates that Cambodia has significantly modernized its military with Chinese equipment, including multiple rocket launchers and 'fifth-generation' anti-tank guided missiles (GAM-102LR) recently seized by Thai forces at Hill 500. While China denies delivering new weapons since the clashes began in July 2025, Thai military officials are concerned about the sophistication of the hardware now appearing on the battlefield.
title: Thai–Cambodia border clash exposes expanding arms pipeline

summary: This neutral analysis highlights the fundamental map dispute fueling the current conflict: the 1907 French 'Annex I map' used by Cambodia versus the natural watershed line claimed by Thailand. The dispute focuses on three key Hindu temples—Preah Vihear (Khao Phra Viharn), Ta Moan Thom (Ta Muen Thom), and Ta Khwai (Prasat Ta Krabey). While the 1962 ICJ ruling awarded Preah Vihear to Cambodia, it left surrounding territory ill-defined, allowing nationalist narratives in both countries to exploit cartographic ambiguities during domestic political crises.
title: A visual guide to the historical maps and temples at the heart of the Thailand-Cambodia conflict

summary: The Ministry of National Defense reported that since Dec 7, 17 Cambodians (including a baby) have died and 77 have been injured due to Thai attacks. The ministry accused Thailand of using cluster bombs, poison gas, and F-16s, targeting civilian infrastructure and historical sites.
title: Ministry says 11th day of renewed Thai aggression has brought 17 deaths and 77 injuries to civilians
titleEn: 17 Civilians Killed, 77 Injured After 11 Days of Thai Aggression

summary: A conflict update for December 17, 2025, at 9:40 AM, reported fierce fighting in Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey province. It stated that the Cambodian army successfully repelled attempts by Thai infantry to push into Cambodian territory and noted that Thai artillery shelled Sla Kram village.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10.10am 17/12/25: Fierce fighting on Cambodian border

summary: Citing the Wall Street Journal, Thai media reports that the Royal Thai Air Force used F-16s and drones to strike at least 6 casinos and hotels in Cambodia. Thailand claims these sites were abandoned by scam syndicates and seized by the Cambodian military to use as drone and artillery bases. Cambodia's Ministry of Information denies this, stating the buildings are civilian infrastructure.
title: สื่อนอกตีข่าว สงครามชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พุ่งเป้าโจมตีแหล่งสแกมเมอร์ข้ามชาติ
titleEn: International media reports Thai-Cambodian border war targets transnational scam compounds

summary: As of 10:20 AM on December 17, Cambodian sources claim that several Thai soldiers died during an infantry attack on Ta Krabey Temple (Prasat Ta Krabey) in Oddar Meanchey Province. The article alleges that Cambodian forces captured weapons from the fallen Thai troops and maintain full control over the 11th-century temple.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10.40 17/12/25: Thai soldiers reported killed in fierce battle at Takrabei Temple
titleEn: Conflict Update 10:40 AM Dec 17, 2025: Thai soldiers reported killed in fierce battle at Ta Krabey Temple

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence issued an update on December 17, 2025, marking the 11th day of the conflict. The statement alleges that Thai military forces continue to fire and violate Cambodia's sovereignty and the ceasefire agreement in Military Regions 4 and 5 along the border.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ ធ្វើបច្ចុប្បន្នភាពពីស្ថានការណ៍តាមបន្ទាត់ព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ ករណីយោធាថៃ បន្តបាញ់ប្រហារ និងឈ្លានពានលើដែនអធិបតេយ្យកម្ពុជា នៅទិសយោធភូមិភាគទី4 និងយោធភ
titleEn: Ministry of National Defence updates on the situation along the Cambodia-Thailand border regarding the Thai military continuing to fire and invade Cambodian sovereignty in Military Regions 4 and 5

summary: The Malaysia-Cambodia Business Association (MCBA) states that while the Thailand-Cambodia tension has led to heightened attention, it remains confined to specific border areas and hasn't yet caused large-scale withdrawal of foreign investments. However, members are evaluating alternative ASEAN locations due to risks in cross-border logistics and trade flow redistribution.
title: ASEAN Confidence Remains Strong Despite Heightened Regional Tension

summary: The Ministry of National Defence spokesperson, Ms. Mali Socheata, stated in a conference that December 17 marks the 11th day of the Thai military's brazen armed aggression on Cambodian territory, showing no fear of international law.
title: 11ថ្ងៃហើយ ដែលយោធាថៃ បើកការវាយប្រហារកម្ពុជា
titleEn: It's been 11 days that the Thai military has launched attacks on Cambodia

summary: Military reports indicate continuous fighting along the border. Authorities are also stepping up maritime inspections to block the shipment of logistics and war supplies to Cambodia, while also addressing the issue of call center scammers operating near the border.
title: ข่าวยังมีการปะทะตลอดแนวชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Clashes Continue Along Entire Thai-Cambodian Border

summary: Army Region 2 reported that Thai forces successfully seized and secured key targets at the Chong An Ma market area, finding numerous PMN-2 mines. Clashes involving tanks, artillery, and drones continue at Pha Mo E-Daeng. Cambodian BM-21 rockets were reportedly fired into Thai territory at Chong Jom and Chong Prao, while Thai forces confirmed destroying Cambodian supply trucks and drone storage sites used by 'scammers' near Chong Sai Taku.

titleEn: Army Region 2 summarizes Thai-Khmer border situation: Thailand launches offensive, controls key areas at Chong An Ma and Ta Kwai

summary: At 12:00 PM on December 17, 2025, Cambodian forces reportedly responded to Thai 'invaders' by firing BM21 rocket launchers at the Thmar Daun battlefield. The report claims this was a retaliatory strike after Thai forces fired shells into Cambodian territory but failed to provoke the army.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 12.30pm 17/12/25: Cambodian troops repel Thai agressors
titleEn: Conflict Update 12:30 PM Dec 17, 2025: Cambodian troops repel Thai aggressors

summary: The Joint Press Center, led by Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sonjaidee, has issued three non-negotiable conditions for a ceasefire: 1) Cambodia must be the first to announce a truce, 2) The ceasefire must be genuine and continuous, and 3) Cambodia must sincerely cooperate in landmine removal.
title: แถลงการณ์ศูนย์แถลงข่าวร่วมสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย - กัมพูชา 17 ธ.ค. 68 เวลา 13.00 น.
titleEn: Joint Information Center Statement on Thai-Cambodian Border Situation, Dec 17

summary: Military engagements have entered their 11th consecutive day, with the combined death toll reaching at least 52. Thai authorities report 19 soldiers and 16 civilians killed, while Cambodia reports 17 civilian deaths. Over 700,000 people have been displaced. Despite international mediation attempts, Thailand has set a condition that Cambodia must be the first to announce a credible ceasefire.
title: Thai-Cambodia border clashes rage on with rising death toll

summary: Thailand's Defense Ministry announced on Wednesday that the latest round of conflict has left at least 19 Thai soldiers and 19 Thai civilians dead. Over 270,000 people have been displaced. The ministry's spokesperson, Surasant Kongsiri, stated that Cambodia used heavy weapons for attacks in border areas from Tuesday night into early Wednesday morning.
title: 19 Thai soldiers killed in Thailand-Cambodia clashes

summary: Cambodia's Defense Ministry reported on Wednesday that the civilian death toll from the reignited border conflict with Thailand has reached 17, with 77 others injured. Spokesperson Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated that Thai forces continued to use F-16 fighter jets, drones, and heavy artillery to strike positions in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat provinces. Official figures indicate over 438,000 individuals have been displaced since the fighting resumed on December 7.
title: Cambodian civilian death toll in border clashes rises to 17: ministry

summary: Official military update regarding the Ta Kwai - Hill 350 area. The Thai military claims to have intercepted opposing forces attempting to advance and used appropriate firepower to maintain area control and prevent the movement of reinforcements and heavy weaponry from the Cambodian side.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 2 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา 17 ธ.ค.68 (เวลา 12.00 น.)
titleEn: Second Army Region Summarizes Thai-Cambodia Border Situation, Dec 17, 2025 (12:00 PM)

summary: Thailand is restricting fuel and supplies to Cambodia to limit its military capabilities... Thailand would only agree to a ceasefire if Cambodia openly stops hostilities.
title: Thai defense minister says cambodia thai border war wont

summary: As of late December 2025, the number of displaced Cambodians has reached 422,698 people (126,508 families) across seven provinces including Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Banteay Meanchey. The Ministry of Education reports that 1,039 schools have been closed, affecting over 242,000 students. Humanitarian organizations like World Vision are calling for urgent aid to address food shortages and trauma among children, describing the scale of displacement as 'unprecedented'.
title: Cambodian evacuees top 400,000; aid groups seek more support as border clashes continue

summary: The Nation Thailand reporting on Day 11: Death Toll Rises to 57; Thailand Confirms 38 Fatalities: Thai military fatalities rose to 21 soldiers. title: The Nation Thailand: Day 11: Death Toll Rises to 57; Thailand Confirms 38 Fatalities

summary: An analysis of the reignited conflict since December 7, describing it as one of the most intense Southeast Asian confrontations in decades. The report highlights Thailand's military objectives to 'deter and destroy' Cambodian capabilities and suggests Thailand may be seeking to create buffer zones along the border. It explores how China, as a primary partner for both nations, is positioned as a critical mediator to prevent further escalation that threatens regional trade.
title: The Cambodia-Thailand Conflict: Can China’s Influence Tip the Scales?

summary: Tourism industry leaders in Northeastern Thailand are urging their government to end the fighting quickly. Major hotels in border provinces and even cities like Nakhon Ratchasima report total cancellations, with occupancy rates falling to 60-70% instead of the usual 80% during the New Year period.
title: ប្រតិបត្តិករសណ្ឋាគារថៃអំពាវនាវឲ្យបញ្ចប់សង្រ្គាម ខណៈការកក់បន្ទប់ត្រូវលុបចោលច្រើន

summary: As of 3:00 p.m. on Dec 17, Thai soldiers reportedly used drones to drop bombs and fired artillery into the O Phluok Damrey area in Pursat province. Cambodian forces are reported to be standing firm to protect national integrity and counterattacking the invasion.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE: 15.40 17/12/25: Thais use bomber drones against Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 3:40 PM: Thais Use Bomber Drones Against Cambodia

summary: The 2nd Army Region reported active clashes at Chong Sai Taku, resulting in a fire at a facility housing military drones and a scammer operation center. Thai forces seized key areas at Chong An Ma and Ta Kwai. Two Thai soldiers, Sgt. Maj. Samroeng Klangprakhon and Pvt. Panuphat Saosa, were confirmed killed in action. The military remains on high alert for drone attacks.
title: ปะทะ 'ช่องสายตะกู' ทำไฟไหม้คลังเก็บโดรนทิ้งระเบิด-ฐานสแกมเมอร์

summary: The Royal Thai Army's First Army Area Command reported intensification of clashes in Sa Kaeo province. Sgt. Phornsak Iamsaad died from injuries, bringing the casualty count to 61 Thai soldiers affected since December 8. Cambodian forces continue to use BM-21 rockets and mortars. Tensions in Poipet remain high following border closures and reports of smoke from local buildings.
title: First Army takes strong action in border clash with Cambodia, one more Thai soldier killed

summary: Thai Prime Minister states that Cambodia should return to the negotiating table if they have 'common sense.' He emphasized that Thailand must secure Hill 350 and has instructed the military to recover the bodies of fallen personnel. The military is also briefing on the tactical situation at Chong An Ma.
title: 'นายกฯ' ชี้หาก 'กัมพูชา' มีสติควรเจรจา ลั่นต้องได้เนิน 350

summary: The foreign ministries of Sweden and Denmark have issued red notices for areas within 50km of the Thai-Cambodian border. This includes popular holiday islands Koh Chang, Koh Kood, and Koh Mak. Travelers are being advised to cancel trips to these 'red zones' due to the escalating military conflict.
title: Holiday plans on hold: Nordic travelers navigate changing government guidance

summary: Fighting entered its 11th day with the death toll reaching 52. Thai forces reportedly captured the Chong Anh Ma area after heavy combat. Cambodia's Defense Ministry reported Thai artillery and drone strikes, while Cambodian forces responded with BM-21 rockets. Displacement has exceeded 700,000 people.
title: Thai-Cambodia renewed clashes enter 11th day, death toll rises to 52

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs held an international meeting with representatives from 58 countries to coordinate a crackdown on call center scammers. Notably, Cambodia did not attend the meeting despite the issue being prevalent in border areas. Mr. Sihasak Phuangketkeow confirmed that even without their attendance, Cambodia must eventually cooperate in these regional efforts.
title: กต.ประชุม 58 ประเทศ ถกปราบสแกมเมอร์
titleEn: MFA meets with 58 nations to discuss scammer crackdown; Cambodia absent

summary: The Ministry of National Defence issued a report stating that Thai forces continued to violate Cambodian sovereignty from December 16 to 17. In Military Region 4 (Oddar Meanchey/Preah Vihear), Thai forces used F-16 jets and artillery to strike Takrabei Temple and Mount 333. In Military Region 5 (Banteay Meanchey/Pursat), Thai infantry supported by tanks attempted to advance into Jock Chey and Prey Chan villages, accompanied by drone strikes and reports of 'toxic smoke'.
title: យោធាថៃ បន្តបាញ់ប្រហារ និងឈ្លានពានមកលើកម្ពុជា នៅទិសយោធភូមិភាគទី4 និងយោធភូមិភាគទី5
titleEn: Thai military continues shelling and invasion of Cambodia in Military Regions 4 and 5

summary: Capt. Thammanoon Wanna of the Trat Marine Task Force stated that after 9 days of operation 'Trat Prab Porapak,' Thai forces have fully seized the 'Ban Sam Lang' area. He claimed Cambodian forces have been neutralized and no longer offer resistance. Current stats for the Trat area show 5 Thai soldiers injured, no deaths, and over 4,500 evacuees currently in shelters.
title: ผบ.ฉก.นย.ตราด ยันคุมชายแดนได้เบ็ดเสร็จ ลั่นลิดรอนกำลังฝ่ายตรงข้ามจนสิ้นสภาพ รออีกนิดได้กลับบ้าน
titleEn: Trat Marine Task Force Commander confirms total border control, claims opposing forces neutralized

summary: Dr. Sok Touch, President of the Royal Academy of Cambodia, and other political scientists have criticized ASEAN's inability to manage the conflict. They argue the 'non-interference' policy has failed, and instead point toward major powers like China to facilitate a solution as Thailand rejects ceasefire calls from the US and Malaysia.
title: ខណៈការឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃលើកម្ពុជាបន្តអូសបន្លាយ អ្នកជំនាញ រិះគន់អាស៊ានថា គ្មានយន្តការដោះស្រាយ
titleEn: As Thai invasion of Cambodia continues, experts criticize ASEAN for lack of resolution mechanism

summary: The 1st Army Region summarized the border situation in Sa Kaeo as of December 17. Heavy fighting occurred at Ban Khlong Phang and Ban Nong Ya Kaew. One Thai soldier, Sgt. Phornsak Iamsaad, was killed, and 8 others were injured. The report noted Cambodian military presence in Poipet after the border crossing was closed to Thai citizens.
title: ทภ.1 สรุปแนวรบชายแดนสระแก้ว ปะทะหนักต่อเนื่อง ตรวจพบทหารกัมพูชาพร้อมอาวุธที่ฝั่งปอยเปต

summary: Soldiers and police in Cambodia’s Banteay Meanchey province claim they experienced severe respiratory distress after Thai aircraft dropped what they described as 'poisonous water' or 'toxic gas.' Cambodia's Ministry of Defence has repeatedly accused Thailand of using gas in violation of international law. Reuters, which conducted the interviews, stated they could not independently verify the claims, and Thai officials have not provided fresh comments on these specific accusations.
title: From hospital beds, Cambodian soldiers describe 'toxic gas'

summary: Air Marshal Prapas Sonjaidee, Director of the Joint Press Information Center, stated Thailand's 3 requirements for peace: 1) Cambodia must announce a ceasefire first, 2) The ceasefire must be genuine and continuous, and 3) Cambodia must sincerely cooperate in landmine clearance along the border.
title: ผอ.ศูนย์แถลงข่าวร่วมสถานการณ์ไทย-กัมพูชา ย้ำ 3 เงื่อนไข ยันกัมพูชาต้องหยุดยิงก่อน
titleEn: Director of Joint Press Center insists on 3 conditions, maintains Cambodia must ceasefire first

summary: On the evening of December 17, 2025, Thai forces reportedly shelled Samraong town, the capital of Oddar Meanchey Province. The attack, which occurred around 8:00 PM, caused a fire at a market near the Kok Mon roundabout. Early reports indicate that one civilian has died and at least two others were injured in the assault.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 20.40 17/12/25: Civilian killed, market on fire as result of latest Thai aggression this evening
titleEn: Conflict Update 8:40 PM Dec 17, 2025: Civilian killed and market on fire from Thai shelling this evening

summary: A special envoy from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs in charge of Asian affairs is scheduled to visit Cambodia and Thailand on December 18, 2025. The visit is part of China's diplomatic efforts to facilitate communication between the two sides and restore peace following the ongoing border conflict. China has expressed deep concern and aims to help reduce tensions as a close neighbor to both nations.
title: BREAKING: មន្រ្តីជាន់ខ្ពស់ក្រសួងការបរទេសចិន នឹងធ្វើដំណើរទស្សនកិច្ចមកកាន់កម្ពុជា និងថៃ ដើម្បីប្រឹងប្រែងស្តារសន្តិភាពឡើងវិញឲ្យបានឆាប់
titleEn: BREAKING: Senior Chinese Foreign Ministry official to visit Cambodia and Thailand to restore peace quickly

summary: The Thai-Cambodia People Alliance for Peace has called for an immediate ceasefire, accusing both governments of using the border dispute to fuel 'ultranationalism' and distract from internal political failures. The group claims the conflict serves the interests of ruling elites while harming border communities and low-ranking soldiers. The article also mentions a Thai airstrike that damaged a primary school in Thmar Pouk district on December 17.
title: Alliance Urges Immediate Thai–Cambodian Ceasefire, Warns Border Conflict Serves Elites Only

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra stated on social media that major international outlets like CNN, AP, and AFP have accurately reported on Thai military attacks against Cambodian territory. He argued that these reports allow the international community to see that Cambodia is exercising restraint while Thailand uses disproportionate force. He specifically cited reports of Thai bombs falling near refugee camps.
title: Information Minister: International Media Expose Thai Military Attacks as Cambodia Exercises Restraint

summary: Thai Navy's Marine Task Force in Trat reports that Cambodian forces have been 'incapacitated' after 8 days of the 'Trat Prab Porapak' operation. Following heavy naval and air strikes, Thai troops have recaptured Ban Sam Lang and are currently in full control of the situation with no counter-attacks reported.

summary: Defense Ministry spokesperson Maly Socheata stated in a press conference that the Thai military has continuously used heavy weaponry since Dec 7. She listed the weapons used as DK guns, 100mm tank guns, 105mm and 155mm artillery, toxic gas drones, fire drones, and suicide drones. Attacks targeted Prasat Ta Moan Thom and areas near Preah Vihear Temple. Cambodia called on the international community to condemn these actions as 'illegal war crimes.'
title: លោកស្រី ម៉ាលី សុជាតា ៖ យោធាថៃ នៅតែបន្តប្រើសព្វាវុធ ធុនធ្ងន់គ្រប់ប្រភេទ លើកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Ms. Maly Socheata: Thai military continues to use all types of heavy weapons against Cambodia

summary: As of 7 AM on Dec 18, the border frontlines were described as relatively calm compared to previous days. However, the report notes that on the night of Dec 17, Thai forces used drones and artillery to strike positions in Pursat (O Phluok Damrei) and Oddar Meanchey (Ta Moan and Chub Ka Kir). Cambodian forces remain on high alert and have reportedly fired back to defend territorial integrity.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.10 18/12/25: Situation ‘calm’ but Cambodian troops ready for attacks
