He assured the public that the government is working urgently to resolve the crisis and emphasized that the safety of Thai citizens is the top priority. He asked residents to remain patient while the military handles the security threats.
title: นายกฯ เยี่ยมศูนย์พักพิงผู้ป่วยติดเตียงจันทบุรี ยันเร่งแก้ไขสถานการณ์โดยยึดความปลอดภัย
titleEn: PM visits bedridden patient shelter in Chanthaburi, vows to resolve situation prioritizing safety

summary: Tens of thousands of Cambodians participated in a massive peace march in Phnom Penh on the 12th day of the border conflict with Thailand. Organized by the Union of Youth Federations of Cambodia (UYFC) and led by Hun Many, the rally called for an end to hostilities and respect for a ceasefire. Official reports indicate the conflict has claimed at least 55 lives so far, including 18 Cambodian civilians and 16 Thai civilians, along with numerous military casualties on both sides.
title: Tens of thousands rally for peace in Cambodia amid deadly border conflict

summary: China's Ministry of National Defense called on both nations to remain calm and reach a ceasefire immediately. A spokesperson rejected speculation regarding the use of Chinese weapons in the conflict, stating that China's defense cooperation with both sides is not targeted at any third party and complies with international law.
title: China urges Cambodia, Thailand to exercise calm and restraint, come to ceasefire

summary: Students at Hun Sen Klakon High School in Serey Sophorn, Banteay Meanchey province, were forced to run for safety after Thai airstrikes hit areas near the school. The strikes occurred near the Provincial Department of Education, causing panic among students and teachers.
title: Students Flee for Safety After Thai Airstrikes

summary: Thai F-16 fighter jets conducted airstrikes on Thursday, targeting a warehouse in the Cambodian border town of Poipet that Thailand claims was used to store rockets. The conflict, which reignited on December 8 after a skirmish the previous day, has seen thousands of rockets fired by Cambodia and heavy artillery and air operations by Thailand. Both nations are fighting over disputed frontier territory containing ancient temple ruins.
title: Thailand carries out more airstrikes on Cambodia as deadly border conflict flares

summary: Report citing the Joint Press Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Border Situation stating that Thailand has set three conditions for a ceasefire: Cambodia must officially declare the ceasefire first, the ceasefire must be strictly followed and sustained, and Cambodia must show sincere cooperation in joint demining operations. The article also mentions Thai military shelling of a Tela gas station in Banteay Chhmar commune, Banteay Meanchey province, which affected civilian areas.
title: ថៃ កំណត់លក្ខខណ្ឌចំនួន 3 សម្រាប់បទឈប់បាញ់ មុនកិច្ចប្រជុំរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសអាស៊ាន នៅថ្ងៃទី22 ខែធ្នូ
titleEn: Thailand sets 3 conditions for ceasefire before ASEAN Foreign Ministers meeting on Dec 22

summary: China has intensified mediation efforts, with Foreign Minister Wang Yi holding separate calls with Thai and Cambodian counterparts. Beijing reports both nations are willing to de-escalate. China has also dispatched a special envoy for shuttle diplomacy to facilitate a ceasefire following heavy fighting that has killed approximately 40 people and displaced 750,000 across both sides.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Willing to Deescalate Border Conflict, Chinese FM Says

summary: Strategic analysis indicates that the Thai-Cambodian tension is no longer a manageable bilateral issue but a indicator of the future security order in Southeast Asia. The conflict highlights ASEAN's decreasing relevance as it lacks the tools for arbitration. The dispute is becoming a state of 'militarized coexistence' where permanent insecurity is normalized, further complicated by the involvement of great powers like China and the U.S.
title: Why the Thai–Cambodian Dispute is a Strategic Problem

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that since the start of Thai military operations on December 7, 18 civilians have been killed and 498,328 people (151,655 families) have been displaced across Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. Significant damage was reported to civilian infrastructure including schools, health centers, and pagodas. The government called for international intervention to compel Thailand to return to the ceasefire agreement.
title: Interior Ministry: Thai Military Attack Kills 18 Civilians, Displaces Nearly 500,000 Cambodians as of December 19

summary: The Ministry of National Defense accused the Thai military of firing 'toxic smoke' into Banteay Meanchey province at 08:48 on December 19. The statement claims Cambodian forces are monitoring the situation closely and remain ready to defend territorial integrity against what they describe as Thai aggression.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 09.00 19/12/25: Thais fire toxic gas into Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 09:00 19/12/25: Thais fire toxic gas into Cambodia

summary: At 07:42 on December 19, the Thai military reportedly fired 5 artillery shells into civilian homes in Banteay Mean Rith village, Kok Romiet commune, Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province. The Ministry of National Defense condemned the attack as a violation of international humanitarian law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10.00 19/12/25: Thailand shells civilian homes in Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 10:00 19/12/25: Thailand shells civilian homes in Cambodia

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) reported that Thailand has submitted a letter to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights regarding Cambodia's closure of land borders, which prevents 5,000-6,000 Thai nationals in Poipet from returning home. The MFA reaffirmed its 3 conditions for a ceasefire: Cambodia must announce it first, the ceasefire must be real and continuous, and Cambodia must cooperate in demining. The Foreign Minister is set to attend a special ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 to discuss the situation.
title: Summary of the Weekly Press Briefing by the Director-General of the Department of Information and MFA Spokesperson on 19 December 2025
titleEn: Summary of the Weekly Press Briefing by the MFA Spokesperson on 19 December 2025

summary: The Second Army Area provided an update on the border conflict as of December 19, 2025. In Buriram province, specifically at Chong Sai Taku, both sides are reinforcing troops and exchanging artillery and mortar fire. The military warns citizens to be careful with social media posts to prevent leaking operational secrets. In Sisaket, the situation remains tense at Hill 350 where efforts to recover fallen Thai soldiers continue under heavy fire.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Army Region 2 summarizes the Thai-Cambodian border situation

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) stated that Thailand is ready for the special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting on December 22 in Kuala Lumpur. Deputy spokesperson Maratee Nalita Andamo emphasized that Thailand has three non-negotiable conditions for a ceasefire: 1) Cambodia must declare a ceasefire as the party that encroached on Thai territory, 2) the ceasefire must be real and continuous, and 3) Cambodia must show sincerity in demining operations. Foreign Minister Sihasak has briefed top diplomats from the EU, China, and the US on these positions.
title: กต. ย้ำ ไทย ไม่ปิดกั้นเจรจา ชี้ กัมพูชา ต้องรับ 3 เงื่อนไข หยุดยิง
titleEn: MFA: Thailand doesn't block talks; Cambodia must accept 3 ceasefire conditions

summary: The Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives (BAAC) announced a 20 billion baht relief package for farmers in seven border provinces affected by the conflict. Measures include debt cancellation for deceased or missing persons, 1-year payment extensions, and low-interest emergency loans up to 500,000 baht for recovery.
title: ธ.ก.ส. เยียวยาชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ยกหนี้-ขยายเวลาชำระ สูงสุด 1 ปี
titleEn: BAAC aids Thailand-Cambodia border residents: Debt cancellation and payment extensions up to 1 year

summary: A coalition of 39 non-governmental organizations from both Cambodia and Thailand, known as the Thai-Cambodian People's Alliance for Peace, issued a joint statement on December 19 calling for an immediate end to border hostilities. The groups emphasized that the conflict is causing severe hardship for local villagers, farmers, and workers who have long lived in peace. They urged both governments to respect previous peace agreements and restore normalcy for people living along the border.
title: អង្គការកម្ពុជា-ថៃ ចំនួន39 ចេញសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍រួម អំពាវនាវឲ្យបញ្ចប់សង្គ្រាម
titleEn: 39 Cambodian-Thai organizations issue joint statement calling for an end to the war

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has called for a ceasefire... Special Envoy for Asian Affairs, Deng Xijun, has embarked on a 'shuttle-diplomacy' trip.
title: WS6944a70fa310d6866eb2f6f5

summary: The UN has condemned the increased hostilities. Locally, Cambodian officials reported that Thai artillery hit a Tela gas station in Banteay Meanchey province, which is a civilian residential area. The report claims total deaths across both sides since July have reached 35,000, though this number is likely an exaggeration compared to other official reports.
title: UN ថ្កោលទោស ការបង្កើនអរិភាព ក្នុងជម្លោះព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ និងបង្ហាញការតក់ស្លុតពេលថៃ ប្រើយន្តហោះចម្បាំង វាយប្រហារទីតាំងវប្បធម៌
titleEn: UN condemns escalation of hostilities in Cambodia-Thailand border conflict and expresses shock at Thai airstrikes on cultural sites

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released an update on Dec 19, stating that Thai forces are continuing to violate the Oct 26 peace agreement. In Military Zone 4 (Oddar Meanchey), Thai artillery allegedly fired on Ta Moan Temple and the surrounding 'Royal Palace' area between 8 PM on Dec 18 and 7 AM on Dec 19. In Military Zone 5 (Banteay Meanchey/Pursat), reports include Thai drone strikes in Thma Da and artillery fire from a warship in the same area. The ministry claims Thai forces fired shells into civilian homes in Banteay Mean Rith.
title: Ministry of National Defense: For 13 days, Thai army’s aggression against Cambodia has been brutal and has caused a high level of damage to civilians

summary: border situation is reported as relatively calm following heavy shelling from the Thai side at approximately 4:00 a.m.
title: Conflict update 08 00 19 12 25 situation calmer after early morning shelling

summary: A Thai warship fired warning shots to deter a Cambodian vessel that attempted to intrude into Thai territorial waters near Mondol Seima district (Koh Kong) and Hat Lek, Trat province on December 19. The situation returned to normal after the intervention.
title: เรือรบไทย ยิงเตือนเรือกัมพูชา พยายามลุกล้ำ อาณาเขตไทย
titleEn: Thai warship fires warning shots at Cambodian boat attempting to intrude into Thai waters

summary: Casualties are reported on both sides as fighting continues across four border provinces. The Thai Army is attempting to recover the bodies of two soldiers from Hill 350. There are reports that Cambodia refused to accept the bodies of their own fallen soldiers found in Thai territory, leading the Thai Army to use quicklime for sanitation. Additionally, Thai F-16s reportedly struck a Cambodian military weapons depot in Poipet, which the military insists was a verified military target.
title: Border clashes leave casualties as humanitarian aid efforts continue

summary: Cambodian forces launched BM-21 rockets and heavy artillery at Pha Mo E-Daeng, Sisaket. In response, the Royal Thai Air Force deployed F-16 fighter jets to bomb Cambodian military positions on Pia Sabaek hill, which were identified as storage sites for rocket launchers. Fighting is also reported in the Chong Jom and Ta Muen Thom areas.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปศึกชายแดนเดือด! กัมพูชาระดมปืนใหญ่–BM-21 ถล่มผามออีแดง ไทยส่ง F-16 โต้ฐานทหารทันที
titleEn: Army Region 2 summarizes border war: Cambodia uses BM-21 rockets on Pha Mo E-Daeng; Thailand deploys F-16s against military bases

summary: In Phnom Penh, Hun Mani (brother of PM Hun Manet) and famous rapper VannDa joined a massive crowd of students and citizens to protest for peace. This follows the escalation of the Thai-Cambodian border conflict. VannDa urged media to report from both sides fairly. The protest reflects the growing internal pressure and public sentiment in Cambodia regarding the ongoing military confrontation.
title: ฮุน มานี - แวนด้า นำมวลชนเขมร ลงถนนพนมเปญ ร้องสันติภาพ เหตุปะทะชายแดนไทยกัมพูชา
titleEn: Hun Mani and VannDa lead Cambodian crowds in Phnom Penh to call for peace following border clashes

summary: Army Region 2 reports that heavy fighting continues at Prasat Ta Kway and Hill 350. Two Thai soldiers, Sgt. Samroeng Klangprakhon and Pvt. Phanuphat Saosa, were killed in action. The military accused Cambodia of using illegal landmines and stated that a Thai surveillance drone lost contact near the border in Sisaket on December 18.
title: ทบ. เผยชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ปะทะเดือด 'ปราสาทตาควาย-เนิน 350' ยังสู้หนัก
titleEn: Army reveals heavy Thailand-Cambodia border clashes at 'Prasat Ta Kway-Hill 350' remain intense

summary: Ongoing border clashes have displaced hundreds of thousands of civilians on both sides. In Thailand's Buriram province, about 15,000 residents from frontline villages are sheltering at the Chang International Circuit. Similar scenes are reported in Cambodia's Oddar Meanchey and Siem Reap provinces, where villagers are fleeing to relief centers as fighting intensifies and hits civilian areas. The total number of displaced persons is estimated at up to 800,000.
title: Hundreds of thousands displaced along Thailand-Cambodia border as fierce fighting continues

summary: Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit admitted on December 19 that Cambodian forces successfully shot down a Thai military DP-20 surveillance drone. He described the loss as 'regrettable but unavoidable' during military operations. He acknowledged Cambodia's air defense capabilities and stated that security has been tightened across all armed forces units following the incident and the discovery of drones near oil rigs in the Gulf of Thailand.
title: រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការពារជាតិថៃ សារភាពថា កម្ពុជាពិតជាមានសមត្ថភាពបាញ់ទម្លាក់ដ្រូនរបស់ខ្លួនមែន
titleEn: Thai Defense Minister admits Cambodia really has the capability to shoot down its drones

summary: Official government website reported that on December 19 at 15:30, the Thai military deployed F-16 fighter jets to bomb the Peak Sbeak geography in Preah Vihear province. The statement emphasized that Cambodian forces remain firmly positioned to defend the territory.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ៖ នៅម៉ោង15:30នាទី យោធាថៃ បានប្រើប្រាស់យន្តហោះ F-16 ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែក នៅភូមិសាស្ត្រពាក់ស្បែក ខេត្តព្រះវិហារ
titleEn: Ministry of National Defense: At 15:30, the Thai military used F-16 fighter jets to drop bombs in Peak Sbeak, Preah Vihear province

summary: China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi held telephone calls with his Cambodian and Thai counterparts, Prak Sokhonn and Sihasak Phuangketkeow, on Thursday. China is acting as a mediator, urging both sides to reach a ceasefire before the situation undermines ASEAN unity. Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense also issued a statement condemning Thailand for using F-16s and heavy artillery against schools and civilian areas, insisting that Cambodian military moves are purely defensive. ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn warned that the bloc cannot ignore the fighting which has displaced over 500,000 people.
title: Beijing Steps In to Mediate as Cambodia, Thailand Seek to Defuse Border Conflict

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that Thai F-16 fighter jets conducted airstrikes in the Pangthong area and Choam Khsant District of Preah Vihear province at 3:30 p.m. and 3:45 p.m. on December 19. The report also claims that F-16s targeted civilian infrastructure in the cities of Poipet and Serei Saophoan in Banteay Meanchey province, which Cambodia labels as a violation of international law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 16.00 19/12/25: Thai F16s strike Cambodia again
titleEn: Conflict Update 16:00 19/12/25: Thai F16s strike Cambodia again

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held separate phone calls with his Cambodian and Thai counterparts on December 18. Both nations expressed a willingness to de-escalate tensions and move toward a ceasefire. China has dispatched a special envoy for 'shuttle-diplomacy' to both countries. Additionally, foreign ministers from both sides have agreed to meet in person in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 for an ASEAN-led meeting aimed at resolving the conflict.
title: Cambodia & Thailand willing to reach ceasefire after Chinese mediation: China

summary: According to the Ministry of National Defense, between 6:30 p.m. and 6:55 p.m. on December 19, the Thai military fired between 10 to 20 artillery shells from a warship. The shells reportedly landed in the water in the Cham Yeam gateway area, Mondol Seima district, Koh Kong province.
title: យោធាថៃ បានបាញ់កាំភ្លើងធំ ចេញពីនាវាចម្បាំង ធ្លាក់ចូលក្នុងទឹកប្រមាណ 10ទៅ 20គ្រាប់ ក្នុងស្រុកមណ្ឌលសីមា
titleEn: Thai military fired 10 to 20 artillery shells from warships into the water in Mondol Seima district

summary: Internal political observers are urging the ruling Hun family to arrest high-level 'criminal masterminds' within Cambodia. This is seen as a move to strip Thailand of its international diplomatic justification for the border conflict, which Thailand claims is partly about addressing cross-border crime and scam hubs. The article highlights that unless the Cambodian government takes action against these figures, Thailand will continue to use the narrative of law enforcement to justify its military presence and 'invasion' of Khmer territory.
title: អ្នកតាមដានឱ្យគ្រួសារហ៊ុនចាប់មេឧក្រិដ្ឋជនដើម្បីកុំឱ្យថៃយករឿងនេះបំភាន់អន្តរជាតិឈ្លានពានខ្មែរ
titleEn: Observers tell Hun family to arrest criminal masterminds so Thailand cannot use this story to mislead international community

summary: China has initiated 'shuttle diplomacy' to mediate the escalating border conflict between Thailand and Cambodia, which the editorial describes as one of the most severe armed confrontations between ASEAN states since the Cold War. Beijing emphasizes that the conflict disrupts regional economic integration and mechanisms like the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation. China urges an immediate halt to the fighting to protect the shared interests of the region and create conditions for a political solution.
title: In mediating the Cambodia-Thailand conflict, China demonstrates a constructive role: Global Times editorial

summary: Cambodian analysts and legal experts rejected Thailand's claims that its military operations were intended to suppress online scam gangs. Lawyer Sok Sam Oeun stated that bombing ancient temples and bridges with F-16s has nothing to do with fighting criminals and is instead an attempt to destroy Cambodia's military capacity. Experts accused Thailand of using these narratives to distract from violations of international law and to cover up internal issues.
title: ថៃ កំពុងព្យាយាមបង្វែរស្ថានការណ៍ដើម្បីគេចពីការទទួលខុសចំពោះសង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានលើកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Thailand is trying to divert the situation to avoid responsibility for the war of aggression against Cambodia

summary: The Thai government, through its Joint Information Center for the Thai-Cambodian Situation, has expressed hope for a ceasefire before December 25. However, Bangkok insists that Cambodia must first accept three unilateral conditions: 1) Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first, 2) The ceasefire must be subject to physical and continuous investigation, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in joint demining operations. Cambodian analysts have called these conditions 'unacceptable,' arguing that Thailand is the aggressor and should be the one to implement such measures. This development comes as ASEAN Foreign Ministers prepare to meet on December 22 to discuss the conflict.
title: ថៃ ចង់មានបទឈប់បាញ់នៅមុនបុណ្យណូអែល ប៉ុន្ដែនៅតែទទូចឱ្យកម្ពុជា ទទួលយកលក្ខខណ្ឌ 3ចំណុច ដែលខ្លួនបានកំណត់
titleEn: Thailand wants a ceasefire before Christmas but still insists Cambodia accepts 3 conditions it has set

summary: On the morning of December 20, a large Thai military drone reportedly violated Cambodian sovereignty by flying deep into Veal Veng District, Pursat Province, reaching the 1500 Mountain area. The report characterizes this as a serious territorial violation.
title: យោធាថៃ ប្រើដ្រូនខ្នាតធំ ហោះរំលោភ ដល់ជើងភ្នំ1500
titleEn: Thai military uses large drone to violate airspace as far as the foot of 1500 Mountain

summary: Groups of Cambodian-Americans gathered at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on December 19 to submit a petition against Thai military actions. Protesters from various U.S. states accused Thailand of violating Cambodia's sovereignty and the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord, calling for international intervention to protect Cambodian civilians.
title: Cambodian-Americans Rally Outside UN Headquarters to Condemn Thailand's Invasion of Cambodia

summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has engaged in talks with Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow, expressing optimism that a ceasefire could be reached as early as Tuesday (Dec 23). This comes ahead of an ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting scheduled for December 22 in Kuala Lumpur, where the border crisis will be a primary focus. Thailand maintains it will not be pressured into a disadvantaged position but remains open to resolving the issue through established diplomatic frameworks.
title: สหรัฐฯ คาดไทย-กัมพูชาบรรลุหยุดยิงต้นสัปดาห์หน้า เดินหน้าเจรจาคลี่คลายความตึงเครียด
titleEn: US Expects Thai-Cambodian Ceasefire by Early Next Week; Diplomatic Push to Defuse Tension

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) spokesperson, Maj. Gen. Winthai Suvaree, issued a statement condemning Cambodian forces for using BM-21 rocket launchers against civilian communities and housing near the border, calling it a violation of international humanitarian law. The conflict has reportedly affected 400,000 Thai civilians, with 23 deaths (mostly indirect) and 6 injuries. Additionally, the Burapha Task Force conducted a raid in Ban Nong Chan, seizing numerous 'mule' bank accounts and mobile phones used by cross-border scammer networks, which Thailand views as a military strategic target.
title: ทบ. ประณามกัมพูชาโจมตีชุมชนพลเรือน ใช้กำลังไม่เลือกเป้าหมาย ค้นบ้านหนองจาน ยึดบัญชีม้า-มือถือเกลื่อน
titleEn: Thai Army condemns Cambodia for indiscriminate civilian attacks; raids Ban Nong Chan, seizes mule accounts and phones

summary: On the night of December 19, 2025, Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly dropped three bombs on the O’Chik Bridge along National Road 68 in Oddar Meanchey Province. The bridge, located 70km from the border, was a vital lifeline for civilians and trade. Cambodian authorities have condemned the strike as a war crime targeting civilian infrastructure despite ongoing international mediation efforts.
title: F-16 Airstrikes Destroy O’Chik Bridge Despite U.S. and Chinese Intervention (VIDEO)
titleEn: F-16 Airstrikes Destroy O'Chik Bridge Despite U.S. and Chinese Intervention (VIDEO)

summary: Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly conducted an airstrike on a casino building in Thmo Da, Pursat province, Cambodia, on December 20 at 11:20 AM. The building was allegedly used by Cambodian forces as an ammunition depot and a launch site for drones. While the Royal Thai Air Force has not officially confirmed the strike, reports suggest the operation was a response to escalating border tensions. The summary also notes that a Thai sailor was injured by a landmine in Trat recently.
title: กองทัพอากาศไทยส่ง F-16 โจมตีอาคารกาสิโนในกัมพูชา หลังถูกใช้เป็นคลังอาวุธ–ฐานปล่อยโดรน
titleEn: Thai Air Force sends F-16s to attack casino building in Cambodia after use as arms cache and drone base

summary: Rear Admiral Paratch Rattanachaiphan, Navy spokesperson, denied rumors that the Navy Commander-in-Chief was shot. However, he confirmed that a Cambodian sniper did target a local unit commander on the border before 'Operation Trat Prab Porapak' began. He described the act as a clear provocation and a violation of peaceful coexistence principles.
title: ทร. แจงเหตุ "กัมพูชา" ลอบยิงผู้นำหน่วยทหารในระดับพื้นที่ เข้าข่ายยั่วยุ-คุกคามชัดเจน
titleEn: Navy explains 'Cambodia' sniped local military unit leader, clearly provocative and threatening

summary: China’s Special Envoy for Asian Affairs, Deng Xijun, visited Phnom Penh to meet with Prime Minister Hun Manet and other high-ranking officials. The discussions focused on de-escalating the ongoing armed conflict with Thailand and pushing for an immediate ceasefire. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution while China pledged to play a constructive role in facilitating dialogue between the two nations.
title: China Reinforces Ceasefire Push as Special Envoy Meets Cambodian Leadership

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn held a telephone conversation with China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi on December 18. Both ministers reaffirmed their 'all-weather' strategic partnership amid the crisis.

Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to existing bilateral frameworks and international law, while thanking President Xi Jinping for China's mediation efforts. The envoy is conducting shuttle diplomacy between Phnom Penh and Bangkok to restore peace after renewed fighting broke out on December 7.

The article also mentions that Cambodian communities, workers, and students in Japan and South Korea organized protests to condemn what they described as Thai aggression and indiscriminate attacks on Cambodian sovereignty.
title: ថៃ ប្រើកាំភ្លើធំបាញ់ផ្លោង9គ្រាប់ ចូលក្នុងភូមិសាស្រ្ត ឃុំនិមិត្ត ស្រុកអូជ្រៅ ខេត្តបន្ទាយមានជ័យ
titleEn: Thai military fires 9 artillery shells into Nimit commune, O'Chrov district, Banteay Meanchey

summary: As the conflict enters its 14th day, Second Army Region Commander Lt. Gen. Weerayut Raksilp announced that Thai forces have successfully seized and established control over 'Hill 350,' a strategic area near Prasat Ta Kwai in Surin province. Meanwhile, heavy artillery fire from the Thai side continues to support operations in the Preah Vihear sector (Kantharalak, Sisaket), where air activity and smoke plumes were observed near the mountain ridges. Residents remain in bunkers and are not yet allowed to return to their homes.
title: “เกาะติดสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา” วันที่ 21 ธ.ค. 68 เข้าสู่การปะทะวันที่ 14 ทหารไทยเข้ายึดพื้นที่ปราสาทตาควาย และเนิน 350 คืนได้สำเร็จ
titleEn: Thai-Cambodian Border Monitoring Dec 21: Day 14 of Clashes, Thai Army Successfully Recaptures Prasat Ta Kwai and Hill 350

summary: Renewed fighting along the 800-kilometer border has displaced approximately 518,611 people in Cambodia and around 400,000 in Thailand. The Royal Thai Air Force has reportedly deployed F-16 fighter jets for airstrikes against military installations. Both nations trade accusations over the instigation of fighting, which centers on colonial-era border demarcations and ancient temple ruins.
title: Thai border clashes displace over half a million in Cambodia

summary: Cambodia has started dismantling a controversial 300-meter breakwater built in Koh Kong province near the Trat border. The move followed a Thai ultimatum threatening to cut off access to the Koh Kong bridge, a key supply route. Although the Royal Thai Navy officially denied issuing a direct threat, security sources confirmed the pressure led to the removal. The structure was criticized for encroaching on maritime territory and causing coastal erosion in Thailand.
title: Cambodia begins dismantling coastal barrier in Koh Kong

summary: At 13:35 and 14:00 on Dec 21, Thai forces launched artillery shells into the outskirts of Poipet and Nimit commune. Some shells fell near or beyond Road 58. By 15:00, the shelling expanded toward Ta Moan Temple in Oddar Meanchey after a brief lull. The report describes these as indiscriminate attacks violating international law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15.10 21/12/25: Thailand shells civilian areas, including border town of Poipet

summary: Ahead of the ASEAN meeting on Dec 22, the Thai MFA reiterated three conditions for a ceasefire: 1) Cambodia must declare it first as the aggressor, 2) it must be continuous and real, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in landmine removal. The ministry stressed that these steps are required to reduce tension and allow military-to-military talks.
title: กต. ประกาศจุดยืนเดิม รอดูท่าทีกัมพูชา ตอบรับ 3 เงื่อนไข 22 ธ.ค. ลั่น หยุดยิงต้องเกิดขึ้นจริง
titleEn: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Stands Firm: Waiting for Cambodia's Response to 3 Conditions Today, Ceasefire Must Be Real

summary: The 1st Army Region and Burapha Force issued an urgent evacuation notice for residents in Ta Phraya, Khok Sung, Aranyaprathet, and Khlong Hat districts. Cambodian forces reportedly used BM-21 multiple rocket launchers targeting civilian areas. Residents are told to stay in designated shelters until the situation stabilizes.
title: ชายแดนเดือดหนัก! สระแก้วสั่งอพยพ 4 อำเภอ หลังกัมพูชาใช้ BM-21 โจมตีพื้นที่พลเรือน
titleEn: Border Conflict Intensifies: Sa Kaeo Orders Evacuation of 4 Districts After Cambodia Uses BM-21 Rockets Against Civilian Areas

summary: Rear Adm Surasant Kongsiri, spokesman for the Thai Defence Ministry, stated that while Cambodian troops continued to fire rockets from BM-21 launchers at the Chub Ta Mok border pass in Surin early Sunday, the overall intensity of attacks has dropped significantly. However, a Thai marine lost a foot after stepping on a newly planted PMN-2 landmine in the Ban Nong Ree area of Trat province while on duty.
title: Cambodian attacks continue but decline significantly: Thai defence ministry

summary: The Second Army Region reported active drone activity and artillery exchanges across multiple sectors including Chong Bok and Prasat Ta Kway. Cambodian forces reportedly used surveillance and FPV suicide drones to monitor and attack Thai positions. Thai forces remain in defensive postures, holding high ground and responding with artillery as necessary.
title: 'ทภ.2' สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทยกัมพูชา วางกำลังตั้งรับ-คุมพื้นที่สำคัญ
titleEn: 2nd Army Region Summarizes Thai-Cambodia Border Situation: Defensive Positions Held in Key Areas

summary: More than 518,000 Cambodians have been displaced due to two weeks of deadly border clashes with Thailand involving tanks, drones, and artillery. The conflict has killed at least 22 people in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia. Southeast Asian foreign ministers are scheduled to meet in Kuala Lumpur on December 22 to attempt to de-escalate tensions, though Thailand has demanded that Cambodia announce a truce first.
title: Cambodia says Thai border clashes displace over half a million

summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Thailand and Cambodia to return to the peace agreement signed in October. The US expects both sides to reach a ceasefire by December 22 or 23. This push comes as the ASEAN Foreign Ministers held a special meeting in Malaysia. Meanwhile, the Thai military (TMAC) condemned Cambodia for laying new landmines, calling it a serious violation of international humanitarian law. Thai FM Sihasak reiterated Thailand's 3-point principle for any ceasefire to be effective.
title: สหรัฐฯ จี้ "ไทย-กัมพูชา" ยุติสู้รบ-ถอนอาวุธ-หยุดวางทุ่นระเบิด
titleEn: US Urges Thailand-Cambodia to End Hostilities, Withdraw Weapons, and Stop Laying Mines

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul reported that Thai forces have taken control of nearly all target areas and are compelling Cambodian forces to withdraw. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the conflict has resulted in the deaths of 34 Thai civilians. Despite declining intensity, shellings were still reported in Sa Kaeo province on Sunday afternoon, and a Thai marine was injured by a landmine in Trat province.
title: Thai PM says military controls nearly all target areas

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has called on the media to practice 'responsible reporting' during the ongoing border conflict. He urged editors and journalists to ensure their coverage does not undermine military morale, expose security risks, or disrupt frontline operations. The PM emphasized that while press freedom is respected, national security and the safety of troops must come first during this period of active hostilities.
title: PM urges responsible reporting for sake of national security

summary: As of late December, humanitarian groups report that approximately 498,242 people (over 151,000 families) have been evacuated in Cambodia due to the border conflict. Nearly 200 displacement sites have been established to accommodate those fleeing airstrikes and heavy artillery fire that have reached multiple provinces including Banteay Meanchey and Siem Reap.
title: World Vision Situation Report #18: Displacement Caused by Cambodia -Thailand Border Conflict (Updated 19 December 2025)

summary: Following high-level talks in Malaysia on December 22, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow announced that Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to hold a General Border Committee (GBC) meeting on December 24, 2025. The meeting aims to negotiate a formal ceasefire. This diplomatic breakthrough comes as the conflict enters its third week, with the death toll of Cambodian civilians standing at 19 and over 518,000 people displaced from their homes.
title: Thailand, Cambodia to Hold GBC Meeting Over Possible Ceasefire On Dec 24

summary: More than 500,000 people in Cambodia and 400,000 in Thailand have been displaced by two weeks of deadly border clashes. Fighting involving tanks, drones, and F-16 airstrikes has killed at least 22 people in Thailand and 19 in Cambodia. The conflict, rooted in colonial-era border disputes, continues daily despite international mediation efforts from the US and China. ASEAN foreign ministers are meeting in Kuala Lumpur today to find a diplomatic solution.
title: Thailand clashes displace half a million in Cambodia

summary: As of December 22, the conflict enters its 14th day. Army Regions 1 and 2 report continuous use of heavy artillery and drones by Cambodia. In Sa Kaeo, 4 districts have been evacuated to safe zones. Heavy clashes are concentrated around the Pha Mor E-Daeng and Phu Ma Khuea areas.
title: กองทัพภาค 1-2 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดน ล่าสุด ยังปะทะหนัก
titleEn: Army Regions 1 and 2 Summarize Border Clashes; Heavy Fighting Continues

summary: On the morning of December 22, 2025, Thai F-16 fighter jets dropped four bombs on the Boeung Trakuan area in Banteay Meanchey at 5:02 AM. Later, at 7:03 AM, toxic fumes were reported in Prey Chan village following Thai fire. Cambodian forces are reportedly fighting back to protect territorial integrity.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.10 22/12/25: Thai F-16s bomb Cambodian border village
titleEn: Conflict Update 08:10 Dec 22, 2025: Thai F-16s bomb Cambodian border village

summary: Army Region 2 released a summary of the situation on Dec 21, reporting continuous clashes in the Pha Mo E-Daeng, Huai Ta Maria, and Phu Makhuea areas. The military asserted that Thailand is exercising its right to self-defense under international law. It accused Cambodian forces of using historic sites as military bases and launch points for attacks, emphasizing that ancient monuments should not be used as battlegrounds.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 2 สรุปเหตุปะทะชายแดน ชี้ กัมพูชาละเมิดหลักสากล ย้ำโบราณสถานไม่ใช่สนามรบ
titleEn: Army Region 2 summarizes border clashes, claims Cambodia violated international standards by using ruins as battlefields

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand 'will act in the way we deem appropriate' and will not be pressured by foreign powers during the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur. The Thai army has expressed intentions to degrade Cambodia's military capabilities to ensure they no longer pose a long-term threat. Meanwhile, Cambodia has reaffirmed its commitment to 'ASEAN Centrality' and the U.N. Charter as it enters negotiations.
title: Thailand Says It Will Not Be Pressured on Border Conflict Ahead of ASEAN Meeting

summary: At 11:32 AM on December 22, 2025, the Thai military reportedly fired three M79 grenades into civilian houses in the Tuol Pongro area of Poipet City, Banteay Meanchey province. This incident is part of ongoing reported aggression along the border.
title: យោធាថៃបាញ់ផ្លោងកាំភ្លើង M79 ចំនួន3គ្រាប់ ចូលភូមិសាស្ត្រទួលពង្រ សង្កាត់អូរឬស្សី
titleEn: Thai military shells 3 M79 grenades into Tuol Pongro area, Ou Ruessei commune

summary: Reports suggest that the Cambodian government plans to use the special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting to criticize Thailand. The allegations include claims that the Royal Thai Air Force used F-16 fighter jets to target non-military locations such as temples, historic sites, and schools, causing civilian casualties. Meanwhile, Thai officials like Anutin Charnvirakul have countered by stating Cambodia is the one spreading misinformation to the international community.
title: จับตา "กัมพูชา" เตรียมใช้เวทีประชุมอาเซียน โจมตีไทยรอบใหม่ กล่าวหาใช้ F-16 ทิ้งบอมบ์ วัด โบราณสถาน โรงเรียน
titleEn: Watch: Cambodia prepares to use ASEAN stage to attack Thailand again, alleging F-16 bombings of temples and schools

summary: Thai military forces reportedly targeted civilian areas in Battambang province on the morning of December 22. Heavy artillery was fired into Phnum Proek and Sampov Loun districts, resulting in at least one civilian injury and damage to local infrastructure.
title: យោធាថៃ បន្តធ្វើសកម្មភាព បាញ់ប្រហារចូលទីតាំង ប្រជាជនស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា និងហេដ្ឋារចនាសម្ព័ន្ធស៊ីវិល ក្នុងភូមិសាស្រ្ត ខេត្តបាត់ដំបង
titleEn: Thai military continues firing at Cambodian civilian locations and infrastructure in Battambang province

summary: At an urgent meeting in Kuala Lumpur, ASEAN foreign ministers expressed 'deep sadness' over rising civilian deaths and called for the full implementation of the October peace accord. Thailand’s Foreign Minister announced that senior military officials from both nations are scheduled to meet on Dec 24 under the Bilateral Border Committee framework to discuss de-escalation.
title: ASEAN ministers urge ceasefire as Thailand-Cambodia border clashes continue

summary: Chatchai Bangchuad, Secretary-General of the National Security Council (NSC), stated following an NSC meeting chaired by Anutin Charnvirakul that Thailand maintains its stance regarding the ASEAN Special Foreign Ministers' meeting in Malaysia. While Thailand views the multi-party involvement as a positive step for de-escalation, it insists that the final resolution must be achieved through bilateral negotiations between Thailand and Cambodia.
title: สมช.รับทราบ รมต.กต.อาเซียน ถกชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ยันหลักการเดิม ยึดคุยทวิภาคี 2 ปท.
titleEn: NSC acknowledges ASEAN FM meeting on Thai-Cambodia border, insists on bilateral talks principle

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn met with Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan in Kuala Lumpur on December 22, 2025. During the ASEAN special meeting, Sokhonn emphasized the urgent necessity of a ceasefire and peaceful negotiations to resolve the current border conflict with Thailand.
title: ប្រមុខការទូតកម្ពុជា ប្រាប់រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសសឹង្ហបុរី ពីស្ថានភាពថ្មីៗ ដោយសង្កត់ធ្ងន់ពីតម្រូវការបន្ទាន់ឲ្យមានបទឈប់បាញ់រវាង កម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: Cambodian FM tells Singapore FM about latest situation, emphasizing urgent need for Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire

summary: Tensions are high in Sa Kaeo province as Cambodian soldiers have taken positions on high-rise buildings near Ban Wang Mon in Aranyaprathet, just 1 kilometer from the Khlong Luek border crossing. Reports state that Cambodian troops have been firing intermittently from these buildings into Thai territory to create pressure. Thai security forces have tightened surveillance to protect the local economy and residents.
title: ทหารกัมพูชายึดตึกสูง บ้านวังมน ห่างด่านคลองลึกไม่ถึง 1 กม. ยิงป่วนฝั่งไทย
titleEn: Cambodian troops occupy high-rise buildings at Ban Wang Mon, less than 1km from Khlong Luek, fire at Thai side

summary: A Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur ended without a ceasefire agreement. Thailand demanded Cambodia admit to initiating aggression and cooperate on demining, while Cambodia's Foreign Minister demanded an immediate ceasefire by midnight. Both sides agreed to convene the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 24 to discuss ceasefire implementation.
title: Special ASEAN meeting failed to reach a Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire, followed by a tripartite meeting

summary: Army Region 2 reports continued clashes at Pha Mo I Daeng and Huay Ta Maria. Cambodian forces utilized FPV suicide drones and heavy mortars. In response, the Royal Thai Air Force carried out airstrikes against enemy positions. The report confirms that a total of 22 Thai soldiers have now been lost in the conflict, with the most recent fatality identified as SFC Kampanat Thongsaeng in the Ta Phraya sector.
title: สถานการณ์ชายแดนวันนี้ 22 ธ.ค. กัมพูชาโจมตีต่อเนื่อง ไทยเดินหน้าลุยแผนเชิงรุก
titleEn: Border Situation Dec 22: Cambodia Continues Attacks, Thailand Proceeds with Offensive Plan

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow reported that the special ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur concluded without a ceasefire agreement. Thailand insists on addressing landmines, scam centers, and troop reductions. Both sides agreed to use the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, with Defense Ministers scheduled to meet in Chanthaburi on December 24.
title: ผลประชุม รมว.กต.อาเซียนไร้ข้อตกลงหยุดยิง โยนใช้เวที GBC รมว.กลาโหมไทย-กัมพูชาคุยกันที่จันทบุรี 24 ธ.ค.นี้
titleEn: ASEAN FM Meeting Ends Without Ceasefire; Defense Ministers to Meet in Chanthaburi Dec 24

summary: As of Dec 21, border clashes have reportedly claimed 53 civilian lives from both nations. Cambodia reports 19 civilian deaths and 510,000 displaced, while Thailand reports 34 civilian fatalities. Thailand's military has taken control of strategic highland areas while China and ASEAN intensify mediation efforts.
title: Thailand-Cambodia clashes kill 53 civilians; China, ASEAN mediate

summary: The ASEAN Foreign Ministers held a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur to address the escalating hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand. The Chair urged both nations to cease hostilities immediately and fully implement the Kuala Lumpur Joint Declaration signed in October 2025. The meeting reaffirmed ASEAN's centrality in ensuring regional peace and supported the deployment of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to verify any ceasefire arrangements.
title: ASEAN Chair’s Statement on the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on the Current Situation Between Cambodia and Thailand

summary: ASEAN foreign ministers have issued a collective call for 'maximum restraint' between Thailand and Cambodia. Analysts cited in the report suggest that trust between the two neighbors has fallen to a 'freezing point.' The upcoming December 24 meeting is viewed as a critical opportunity to de-escalate hostilities that have seen both sides exchange heavy artillery fire. China has expressed interest in continuing its role as a mediator alongside ASEAN.
title: ASEAN urges restraint from Cambodia, Thailand as GBC to convene on December 24

summary: Following a special ministerial meeting, ASEAN members issued a call for the 'cessation of all forms of hostilities' between Thailand and Cambodia. The statement emphasized restoring mutual trust and returning to dialogue through bilateral mechanisms. The regional grouping seeks to promote immediate steps toward peace, with a follow-up military-level meeting scheduled for later this week to verify ceasefire implementation.
title: ASEAN members urge restraint, de-escalation following special meeting on Thai-Cambodia clash

summary: Official data released on Monday indicates significant casualties: Thailand reports 22 soldiers and 38 civilians killed. Heavy gunfire and artillery strikes were reported in Sa Kaeo and other border zones early Monday morning. Cambodia's Ministry of Interior also reported Thai use of artillery, tanks, and F-16 fighter jets, while both nations continue to blame each other for initiating the conflict that reignited on Dec 7.
title: Dozens killed in Thailand-Cambodia border clashes

summary: Fighting intensified in Sa Kaeo province on December 22. Cambodian forces reportedly fired mortars into civilian areas in Khok Sung district, damaging a granary. At 11:30 AM, heavy weapons fire in Ta Phraya district resulted in the death of one Thai soldier. Over 167,000 civilians from four border districts (Aranyaprathet, Khlong Hat, Ta Phraya, and Khok Sung) have been evacuated to 848 temporary shelters. The Royal Thai Navy also confirmed control over the 'Thomoda' casino area in Trat province.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: สระแก้วปะทะเดือด! เขมรยิงอาวุธหนักลงตาพระยา ทหารไทยพลีชีพอีก 1 ราย
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia: Intense Clashes in Sa Kaeo! Cambodia Fires Heavy Weapons into Ta Phraya, 1 More Thai Soldier Killed

summary: The special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur ended on December 22 without a ceasefire agreement between Thailand and Cambodia. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow stated that Cambodia must initiate the ceasefire as the aggressor. Thailand set three conditions: a real and continuous ceasefire, sincerity in joint demining, and Cambodia taking responsibility for initial attacks. Both nations agreed to hold direct bilateral talks through the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 24 without a third-party mediator.
title: เปิดผลประชุมรมต.อาเซียน ไทย-กัมพูชา วันนี้ ชัดนะ!
titleEn: Revealing the Results of Today's ASEAN Foreign Ministers Meeting on Thailand-Cambodia Conflict!

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul refuted claims by US President-elect Donald Trump that Thailand initiated the conflict with Cambodia. The Thai Cabinet also approved guidelines for compensating victims of foreign military action, covering over 460,000 households in 7 border provinces. Additionally, a meeting between Thai and Cambodian defense officials is scheduled for December 24 to discuss the withdrawal of forces and a return to the Peace Declaration.
title: นายกฯโต้ ‘ทรัมป์’ กล่าวหาไทยเริ่มสงครามก่อน - ครม. อนุมัติงบ 8.9 พันล้าน หนุน กกต.จัดเลือกตั้ง-ประชามติ
titleEn: PM rejects Trump's accusation that Thailand started the war; Cabinet approves 8.9 billion baht budget

summary: Malaysian Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, acting as ASEAN Chair, convened a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur to address the border situation. The ministers urged both nations to exercise maximum restraint and utilize the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) for military de-escalation. The meeting highlighted the need to revive cooperation on humanitarian demining and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on Dec 24 to discuss ceasefire verification.
title: ASEAN Urges Cambodia, Thailand To Halt Hostilities, Return To Dialogue - Mohamad

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defense reported that despite the diplomatic meeting in Kuala Lumpur, Thai forces continued to attack Cambodian territory on the morning of December 22. At approximately 10:50 AM, Thai military forces allegedly fired about 30 rounds of small arms at civilian homes in Kbal Koh, Poipet. Additionally, heavy shelling involving artillery, tanks, and drones was reported in the Preah Vihear and Ta Moan temple areas between 5:00 AM and 12:00 PM.
title: កម្ពុជាអះអាងថា យោធាថៃបន្តទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែក ត្រឹមតែប៉ុន្មានម៉ោងមុនកិច្ចប្រជុំពិសេសរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសអាស៊ាន
titleEn: Cambodia claims Thai military continued bombing just hours before special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting

summary: Burapha Force reports on the 15th day of the conflict in Sa Kaeo Province. Cambodian forces used heavy artillery, mortars, and BM-21 rockets (over 120 rounds in Ta Phraya district) to target Thai positions. The military confirmed the death of one Thai soldier, Sergeant First Class Kampanat Thongsaeng, during clashes at Ban Khlong Phaeng. Currently, 17,441 Thai civilians are sheltered in 40 evacuation centers across 4 border districts.
title: ศูนย์ปฏิบัติการกองทัพภาคที่ 1 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พื้นที่ จ.สระแก้ว ประจำวัน 22 ธันวาคม 2568 เวลา 18.00 น.
titleEn: 1st Army Region Summary of Thailand-Cambodia Border Situation in Sa Kaeo, Dec 22, 2025

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs highlighted the humanitarian crisis of landmines after an 8th Thai soldier was seriously injured. Thailand claims there is undeniable evidence that Cambodia has intentionally laid new mines recently, violating humanitarian laws and peace agreements.
title: กต.ย้ำไทยให้ความสำคัญทุ่นระเบิด หลังทหารเสียขาที่ 8 พบหลักฐานเขมรมีเจตนา
titleEn: MFA Stresses Landmine Concern After 8th Soldier Loses Leg; Evidence Suggests Intentional Acts

summary: A Chinese national was injured on Monday morning during intense shelling by Thai forces in the Phnom Prek and Sampov Loun districts of Battambang province. The Ministry of National Defence confirmed the injury, noting that the strikes appeared indiscriminate and targeted areas inhabited by civilians. This development highlights the expanding geographic scope of the conflict beyond the traditional flashpoints of Preah Vihear and Banteay Meanchey.
title: Chinese National Injured in Battambang as Border Shelling Intensifies

summary: An analysis by the Strategic Policy Institute (ISP) suggests the ongoing conflict has cost Cambodia between $450 million and $650 million, leading to a GDP contraction of 1.3% to 1.6%. The report notes that investors are withdrawing, tourism is slumping, and the loss of remittances from 1.2 million Cambodian workers in Thailand is adding further strain. The World Bank warns of long-term economic consequences into next year.
title: ISP วิเคราะห์ปะทะชายแดน "กัมพูชา" เศรษฐกิจเสียหายหนัก 650 ล้านดอลลาร์ GDP หดตัวชัด
titleEn: ISP Analyzes Border Clash: Cambodia's Economy Hit Hard with $650 Million Loss, GDP Shrinks

summary: Fighting in Sa Kaeo province has entered its 15th day. Cambodian forces reportedly fired over 180 BM-21 rockets into three areas, including civilian locations in Khlong Phaeng. In response, the Royal Thai Air Force (RTAF) sent F-16 fighter jets to strike two specific military targets across the border. Over 17,000 Thai civilians have been evacuated to 40 temporary shelters across four districts in Sa Kaeo.
title: เดือด ชายแดนสระแก้ว กัมพูชา ยิงถล่ม BM-21 กว่า 180 นัด 3 พื้นที่ ทอ.ส่ง F-16 ทิ้งบอมบ์
titleEn: Sa Kaeo Border Flares: Cambodia Fires 180+ BM-21 Rockets; RTAF Scrambles F-16s for Airstrikes

summary: The Thai Foreign Ministry stated that the October ceasefire was pushed too quickly by Washington to coincide with a presidential visit, contributing to its eventual collapse. Cambodia has accused Thailand of attacking civilians and ancient structures, which Thailand denies.

The Thai military stated it was responding to rocket fire from Cambodia. Reported casualties have reached at least 23 in Thailand and 20 in Cambodia this month, with over 900,000 people displaced overall. Despite the clashes, both sides have scheduled a bilateral border committee meeting for Wednesday.

He also addressed international claims, specifically countering President Donald Trump's allegations that Thailand was the aggressor, insisting that Thailand was the one invaded.

titleEn: PM Interviews on Thai-Cambodian Border: Confirms China's Neutral Stance, No Pressure on Thailand

The ministers welcomed discussions on a ceasefire and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on December 24, 2025, to discuss implementation and verification of the truce.

summary: Kandal Provincial Governor Kuoch Chamroeun has appealed to Cambodians with spacious homes to provide temporary shelter for those fleeing the border violence. Officials report that over 525,000 Cambodians have been displaced due to Thai airstrikes and shelling, with thousands already seeking refuge in Kandal province. The governor emphasized that many fled with almost nothing and urgently need food and basic support.

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow revealed that the previous October ceasefire, witnessed by US President Donald Trump, failed because it was 'rushed' by Washington for political ceremony and lacked technical details for verification. Defense officials will now meet on December 24 to establish a 'true ceasefire' with a detailed implementation plan. Thailand emphasized that de-mining the border is essential for any progress, as recent landmine explosions have fueled mistrust between the two militaries.
title: Cambodia, Thailand to discuss new truce

summary: Poipet City, a major trade and logistics hub on the border, has become a direct target of heavy military strikes on December 23. The escalation has forced thousands of foreign residents and Thai businesses into a state of uncertainty as the city center faces continued shelling and infrastructure damage.
title: Poipet City under heavy attack

summary: Environment Minister Eang Sophalleth led a government delegation to Siem Reap province to deliver food supplies and essential goods to hundreds of families displaced by the border fighting. The humanitarian mission targets civilians who fled from Banteay Meanchey and other border zones following what the government describes as 'Thai armed aggression'.
title: Minister brings aid to displaced families in Siem Reap

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) issued a statement following the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur on Dec 22. Thailand laid out three essential conditions for a ceasefire: 1) Cambodia must declare the ceasefire first, 2) the ceasefire must be verifiable by military personnel on the ground, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in joint demining. The MFA also confirmed that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on December 24, 2025, to discuss implementation details.

summary: Cambodia's defense ministry reported that Thai fighter jets bombed areas in Siem Reap and Preah Vihear provinces on Monday night, just hours after regional crisis talks ended in Malaysia. The Thai military stated it was responding to dozens of rockets fired from the Cambodian side. To date, the renewed December fighting has killed at least 23 people in Thailand and 20 in Cambodia, with over 900,000 civilians displaced on both sides of the border.
title: Cambodia says Thailand attacks after ASEAN meet on border clashes

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow announced that both nations have agreed to hold bilateral talks through the Joint Boundary Committee (JBC) on Wednesday in Chanthaburi, Thailand. Despite the agreement to talk, Sihasak noted that a ceasefire would depend on actions rather than announcements, as existing truces brokered by ASEAN and US President Donald Trump have failed to hold.
title: Thailand and Cambodia to hold border talks amid deadly clashes

summary: The Chinese Embassy in Bangkok released a statement from China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson regarding the border situation. China's Special Envoy for Asian Affairs, Deng Xijun, is currently traveling between Thailand and Cambodia to mediate the conflict. China expressed support for ASEAN's peace efforts and emphasized its own role in promoting reconciliation and dialogue to restore stability along the border.

summary: Defense officials from Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to meet on Wednesday, December 24, to discuss a possible ceasefire. While Thailand's Foreign Minister Sihasak initially suggested Chanthaburi as the venue, Cambodia's Defense Minister Tea Seiha has requested the meeting be moved to Malaysia for 'security reasons' due to ongoing border combat.
title: Cambodia and Thailand to hold talks on resuming Trump's truce

He also called for the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers currently detained by Thailand.

summary: The General Border Committee (GBC) meeting between Thailand and Cambodia is scheduled for Dec 24-27 at the Ban Phakkard border crossing in Chanthaburi. Thailand's key conditions for the talks include an immediate and verifiable ceasefire and sincere cooperation in demining efforts.

summary: Chinese Special Envoy for Asian Affairs Deng Xijun visited Thailand and Cambodia from Dec 18-23 to mediate the border conflict. Deng met with top leaders in both nations, including Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian PM Hun Manet. China expressed deep concern over casualties and displacement, urging an immediate ceasefire and supporting ASEAN's mediation and observer roles to restore regional stability.

Thirteen people were injured yesterday in Srakaew due to BM-21 rocket fire. For safety, the MOPH has ordered the closure of 18 hospitals in the border zone.

Both nations are looking toward the ASEAN-supported GBC meeting on Dec 24 for a potential ceasefire.

This move reflects the deepening diplomatic rift following the resumption of hostilities along the border, with Cambodia encouraging travelers to find alternative routes to Phnom Penh that bypass Thai territory.
