title: យោធាថៃ ចោទកម្ពុជាដាក់មីនថ្មី គឺពឹងផ្អែកលើការអះអាងជាឯកតោភាគី
titleEn: Thai military's accusation of Cambodia laying new mines is a unilateral claim

summary: Recent combat involving airstrikes and rocket fire has displaced over half a million people. Thailand has accused Cambodia of violating previous agreements by planting new landmines, citing an incident where a Thai marine lost a leg on December 21. International pressure from the US and ASEAN is mounting to restore the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords.
title: Thailand, Cambodia to resume ceasefire talks after deadly border clashes

summary: China is pushing for both Thailand and Cambodia to 'meet halfway' to resolve their border disputes peacefully. This follows reports that South Korea also joined calls for a peaceful resolution. Meanwhile, local reports highlight the negative impact of the conflict on Cambodian tourism, specifically around Angkor Wat, following Thai air strikes in the region.
title: ปักกิ่งลุยเต็มที่! จีนหวังไทย-กัมพูชาพบกันครึ่งทาง ขอสร้างบรรยากาศการเจรจาระหว่าง 2 ฝ่าย
titleEn: Beijing pushes hard! China hopes Thailand-Cambodia meet halfway, asks to create atmosphere for talks

summary: A planned General Border Committee (GBC) meeting to negotiate an end to border clashes is in doubt as both sides disagree on a venue. Cambodia requested to hold the talks in a neutral third country (Kuala Lumpur), citing security concerns, while Thailand insists the bilateral meeting should proceed in Thailand's Chanthaburi province. Over 80 people have reportedly died since fighting resumed in early December.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border meeting in doubt over venue row

summary: On December 23, the Thai military reportedly intensified its assault by firing over 300 artillery shells into Cambodian territory, specifically targeting areas in Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. Specific incidents included shelling in Sampov Loun district and moving tanks and armored vehicles into the Chai Chumneah border pass area.
title: យោធាថៃសន្ធប់បាញ់គ្រាប់ផ្លោងចូលកម្ពុជា ជាង300គ្រាប់ នៅថ្ងៃ23 ធ្នូនេះ
titleEn: Thai military fired more than 300 shells into Cambodia on December 23

summary: Military and defense officials from Cambodia and Thailand are scheduled to meet on December 24, 2025, for a General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The talks will focus on ceasefire implementation and verification. The EU has reportedly offered satellite imagery to assist in monitoring the ceasefire. The meeting is expected to take place in Chanthaburi, Thailand.
title: កម្ពុជា-ថៃ នឹងបើកកិច្ចប្រជុំ GBC នៅថ្ងៃស្អែក
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand to hold GBC meeting tomorrow

summary: A planned General Border Committee (GBC) meeting to negotiate a ceasefire is in doubt after Thailand rejected Cambodia's request to hold the talks in a neutral country like Malaysia. Thailand's Defense Ministry insists the meeting should proceed in Chanthaburi province from Wednesday (Dec 24), arguing the venue is safe and it is Thailand's turn to host. Cambodia cited security reasons for wanting a neutral venue.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border meeting in doubt over venue row

summary: Thai military forces successfully retook strategic positions at Prasat Ta Kwai in Surin province following intense clashes that began in the early hours of December 23. Reports indicate Thai troops prevented Cambodian reinforcements from entering the area. Some local residents have begun returning to their homes as the military secured the site, though tensions remain high with calls for the government to take a firm stance in upcoming ceasefire talks.
title: ไทยยึดคืน 'ปราสาทตาควาย'! สยบทัพเขมรเสริมกำลัง หลังปะทะเดือดเช้ามืดที่สุรินทร์
titleEn: Thailand retakes 'Prasat Ta Kwai'! Suppressing Cambodian reinforcements after fierce pre-dawn clashes in Surin

summary: Military officials from Thailand and Cambodia are scheduled to meet on December 24 to discuss reviving a ceasefire as the border conflict enters its third week. According to the report, at least 41 people have been killed and nearly one million civilians have been displaced since fighting resumed on December 7. The conflict is being described as the worst between ASEAN members since the bloc's founding in 1967. Thailand's Foreign Minister noted that previous ceasefire efforts were 'rushed' due to international pressure and emphasized the need for a deal that reflects the actual situation on the ground.
title: Thailand, Cambodia agree to talks in bid to end deadly conflict – Minister

summary: A planned bilateral meeting on Dec 24 to negotiate an end to border clashes is in doubt after Thailand rejected Cambodia's request to hold talks in a neutral country (Malaysia). Thailand insists on hosting the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting in Chanthaburi Province, asserting the area is safe. The conflict has killed over 40 people and displaced 900,000 since Dec 7.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border meeting in doubt

summary: Officials from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training released a formal petition on December 24 strongly condemning the 'inhumane' actions of the Thai military. The petition accuses Thailand of repeatedly violating ceasefire agreements signed under international witnesses and calls on the international community to hold Thailand accountable for civilian casualties and displacement.
title: ក្រសួងការងារចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោសសង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃ មកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាពនៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Ministry of Labour issues petition condemning Thailand's war of aggression against Cambodia's sovereignty

summary: As of 7:30 AM on Wednesday, Thai forces continued to shell several sectors including Prey Chan, Preah Vihear Temple, and Mount Kham. Shelling was specifically reported around 5:00 AM at Ta Moan and Chubkakir temples. While Pursat province remained quiet, active fire was maintained in the northern and northwestern military regions.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.00 24/12/25: Sporadic shelling on Cambodian border
titleEn: Conflict Update 08:00 24/12/25: Sporadic shelling on Cambodian border

summary: The General Border Committee (GBC) meeting is scheduled to take place from Dec 24-27 at Ban Pakard, Chanthaburi. Thailand has proposed three core conditions: 1) Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first, 2) The ceasefire must be real, continuous, and monitored, and 3) Cambodia must sincerely cooperate in landmine clearance. The Thai government emphasizes that any agreement depends on Cambodia's sincerity.
title: จับตา! เริ่มวันนี้ การประชุม GBC ไทย-กัมพูชา ที่จังหวัดจันทบุรี
titleEn: Watch closely! Thai-Cambodia GBC meeting starts today in Chanthaburi

summary: New reports indicate Thai F-16 fighter jets conducted a raid approximately 60km inside Cambodian territory near Phnom Sampov in Battambang. The Ministry of Defence confirmed that 6 bombs were dropped during this mission at around 10:00 AM on Wednesday.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10:40 24/12/25: Thai F-16s attack Cambodia again in raid 60km into The Kingdom

summary: Fighting continued on the morning of December 24 as the General Border Committee (GBC) secretariat prepared to meet. The Defense Ministry reported that Thai T-50 aircraft dropped four bombs in Banan district, leading to the closure of 241 schools. Military spokesperson Maly Socheata claimed Thai forces used toxic gas drones near Preah Vihear. Displaced Cambodian civilians now exceed 600,000.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Clash Continues Ahead of GBC Meeting, Cambodian Defense Ministry States

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that at 10:00 AM on December 24, Thai forces used South Korean-made T-50 fighter jets to drop bombs in the Phnom Sampov area of Banan district, approximately 100km from the border. The ministry condemned the act as a 'brutal war crime' and indiscriminate attack on civilians.
title: ថៃយកយន្តហោះចម្បាំង T-50 របស់កូរ៉េខាងត្បូង ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែក4គ្រាប់ក្បែរសាលារៀនក្នុងខេត្តបាត់ដំបង
titleEn: Thailand uses South Korean T-50 fighter jets to drop 4 bombs near school in Battambang

summary: Defense Ministry spokesperson Mali Socheata confirmed that as of Wednesday, the 18th day of conflict, 21 Cambodian civilians have died and 83 are injured. Shelling continued this morning in Poipet (near Roundabout 58) and O'Chrov district, injuring two more civilians just hours before the GBC meeting in Chanthaburi.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិកម្ពុជាអះអាងថា ការប៉ះទង្គិចគ្នាតាមព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ នៅតែបន្តមុនកិច្ចប្រជុំគណៈកម្មាធិការព្រំដែនទូទៅ
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand border clash continues ahead of GBC meeting, Cambodian Defense Ministry states

summary: The Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Lin Jian, called for an immediate ceasefire and dialogue. Separately, the Cambodian Ministry of Defense accused Thailand of dropping 'cluster bombs' in Svay Chek district, Banteay Meanchey, between 12:15 PM and 12:26 PM today, further complicating peace efforts.
title: ក្រសួងការបរទេសចិន ឆ្លើយតបចំពោះជម្លោះកម្ពុជាថៃ ៖ ប្រទេសចិន នឹងបន្តជំរុញយ៉ាងសកម្ម ឱ្យមានការចរចាសន្តិភាព
titleEn: Chinese Foreign Ministry responds to Cambodia-Thai conflict: China will continue to actively promote peace talks

summary: Cambodia has dropped its demand to meet in Malaysia and agreed to meet in Chanthaburi. Thailand will present 5 points regarding Cambodia's violations of international law: 1) use and production of landmines, 2) using historical sites as military outposts, 3) firing heavy weapons from civilian areas, 4) using civilian buildings as weapon caches, and 5) using civilians as human shields.
title: กัมพูชา ยอมแล้ว ถกจีบีซี จันทบุรี ไทย ย้ำ ไม่ลงนาม หากแนวทางหยุดยิง คลุมเครือ
titleEn: Cambodia agrees to GBC in Chanthaburi; Thailand insists no signing if ceasefire terms are vague

summary: Local reports from the border area of Ou Skach confirm that a female elephant and its newly born calf were killed by shrapnel from Thai artillery shelling. The report frames this as part of the broader destruction caused by 'Thai invaders' against Cambodian natural resources and wildlife.
title: រកឃើញដំរីញី 1ក្បាល និងកូនទើបកើត 1ក្បាល ស្លាប់ដោយសារអំបែងគ្រាប់ផ្ទុះ របស់ទាហានឈ្លានពានថៃ នៅចំណុចអូរស្កាច
titleEn: Mother elephant and newborn calf found dead due to shrapnel from Thai invaders at Ou Skach

summary: A detailed situational report indicates that between 6:00 PM on Dec 23 and early morning on Dec 24, Thai artillery targeted Koul 8, Phnom Trangol, Ta Sim, and Preah Vihear temple. At midnight, long-distance shelling was reported specifically hitting the Preah Vihear temple area. The report characterizes these as indiscriminate attacks in violation of international law.
title: Conflict Update: Situation Update on Escalating Thai Military Attacks and Violations of Cambodian Sovereignty Along the Cambodia–Thailand Border (4th and 5th Military Regions)

summary: Authorities in Banan district, Battambang, have ordered the immediate closure of 83 schools, including 3 high schools and 10 secondary schools, after Thai T-50 fighter jets reportedly dropped 4 bombs in civilian areas of Chhoeu Teal commune. The district governor, Sreng Sokha, stated the move is to ensure the safety of over 20,000 students as residents flee the area in fear.
title: អាជ្ញាធរស្រុកបាណន់សម្រេចបិទសាលា83ខ្នងភ្លាមៗ ក្រោយយន្តហោះចម្បាំងថៃទម្លាក់គ្រាប់ចូលភូមិសាស្រ្តស្រុកបាណន់
titleEn: Banan district authorities decides to close 83 schools immediately after Thai soldiers use aircraft drop bombs into Banan area

summary: Daily situation report as of Dec 24: Burapha Force has secured positions at Ban Khlong Phaeng, Sa Kaeo, and is clearing landmines planted by Cambodian forces. Since Dec 8, 7 Thai civilians have been injured, 14 houses damaged, and over 5,000 rai of farmland affected by the conflict. Thai forces continue to respond to artillery fire based on the principle of self-defense.
title: เกาะติดสถานการณ์ชายแดน "ไทย-กัมพูชา" วันที่ 24 ธ.ค. 68
titleEn: Monitoring the Thailand-Cambodia border situation - Dec 24, 2025

summary: Thailand has proposed three conditions for the GBC talks starting at 4:00 PM today in Chanthaburi. The conditions include: Cambodia must announce a genuine ceasefire, the ceasefire must be monitored by observers, and Cambodia must cooperate on landmine clearance. The ministerial meeting on Dec 27 depends on the success of these Secretariat-level talks.
title: Thailand sets conditions ahead of Cambodia–Thailand GBC talks in Chanthaburi

summary: Thai forces intensified aerial attacks on December 24 by deploying KAI T-50TH Golden Eagle jet fighters alongside F-16s. Between 12:15 PM and 2:02 PM, these aircraft reportedly dropped cluster bombs in Svay Chek district (Banteay Meanchey) and Banan district (Battambang). The report describes villagers, including women who recently gave birth, fleeing to rice fields in fear.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15:00 24/12/25: Thailand adds T-50TH jet fighters to intensify aerial bombing of Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:00 24/12/25: Thailand adds T-50TH jet fighters to intensify aerial bombing of Cambodia

summary: The Cambodian delegation, led by Maj. Gen. Yam Boraden, crossed the Ban Phakkad checkpoint at 4:25 PM for the GBC meeting. The session lasted only about 30 minutes. Thai officials stated they will not sign any agreement that is vague. The meetings are scheduled to continue from December 25–26 to prepare for the high-level meeting on Saturday.
title: "กัมพูชา" เดินทางร่วมประชุม GBC ระดับเลขาฯ
titleEn: Cambodia attends GBC secretariat-level meeting

summary: Following an ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting on December 22, the Cambodian Ministry of Defense sent an official letter to the Thai Defense Minister expressing a desire for ceasefire negotiations. The Thai military confirmed receipt and emphasized that any truce must follow the established GBC framework and involve verifiable actions on the ground.
title: กัมพูชา ส่งหนังสือทางการเจรจาขอหยุดยิง 'ไทย' ย้ำ ต้องพิสูจน์ความจริงใจ
titleEn: Cambodia sends official letter requesting ceasefire; Thailand insists on sincerity

summary: Secretariat-level officials from the General Border Committee (GBC) met at the Ban Phakkad checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The Thai side, led by Gen. Natthaphong Phraokaew, presented three core demands: Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first, the ceasefire must be continuous and verified by observers, and Cambodia must cooperate on landmine removal. The meeting is a precursor to a potential ministerial-level signing on December 27.
title: เริ่มประชุม GBC ระดับเลขาฯ ถกหยุดยิง
titleEn: GBC Secretariat-level talks begin to discuss ceasefire

summary: The 1st Army Area reported that fighting in Sa Kaeo province has entered its 17th day. Clashes occurred in three main areas: Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Ya Kaeo, and Ban Nong Chan. To counter Cambodian heavy weapons, the Thai military deployed F-16 fighter jets to strike ammunition depots located in Battambang province, Cambodia.
title: ทภ.1 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดน ปะทะต่อเนื่องวันที่ 17 ส่ง F-16 ถล่มคลังอาวุธเขมร ในจ.พระตะบอง
titleEn: 1st Army summary: Clashes continue for 17 days, F-16s strike ammo depots in Battambang

summary: Former Cambodian Information Minister Khieu Kanharith posted that on Dec 23, the remains of a mother elephant and her newborn calf were found near the Preah Vihear border. Cambodian officials claim the elephants died from wounds caused by Thai military bullets or shrapnel and that forest rangers could not reach them earlier due to active fighting.
title: กัมพูชา พบซากแม่ลูกช้างตาย โบ้ยฝีมือทหารไทย อ้างโดนกระสุน-สะเก็ดระเบิด
titleEn: Cambodia finds dead mother and baby elephants, blames Thai military shelling

summary: The first day of the GBC secretariat-level meeting concluded in just 35 minutes at Ban Phakkad. Thailand introduced a new demand for Cambodia to stop using ancient ruins and civilian sites (including buildings linked to scam operations) as military outposts. If negotiations proceed well over the next two days, the defense ministers of both nations are expected to sign a ceasefire on Saturday.
title: Thai–Cambodia GBC talks end in 35 minutes on day one; secretary-level to meet Dec 25–27

summary: As bilateral talks began in Chanthaburi, fresh fighting was reported in the border provinces of Sisaket and Surin in Thailand, and Battambang in Cambodia. Official counts suggest over 40 people have been killed and approximately 1 million displaced since Dec 7. Cambodia has accused Thai forces of destroying a religious statue, while Thailand rejected claims of using cluster munitions.
title: New clashes as Cambodia, Thailand hold first talks to end latest violence

summary: The Thai Ministry of Defence expressed strong skepticism regarding Cambodia's commitment to peace as rocket attacks hit Si Sa Ket and Sa Kaeo just hours before GBC talks began. A Thai soldier was killed and four injured in Sa Kaeo on Dec 23, bringing the total Thai military death toll to 23. Thai officials stated that while negotiations proceed, Thailand must retaliate in self-defence.
title: Thailand doubts Cambodia is sincere about truce as rocket barrages continue

summary: Thailand and Cambodia have scheduled a high-level General Border Committee (GBC) meeting for December 27 to discuss a ceasefire. From December 24 to 26, negotiations under this mechanism are taking place at the secretariat level. ASEAN foreign ministers have welcomed these discussions and urged both nations to uphold their previous commitments to peace, specifically referencing the Kuala Lumpur Joint Declaration from October 2025 and the earlier July 28 ceasefire agreement.
title: Thailand, Cambodia to hold talks on ceasefire on December 27

summary: Military delegates from both nations convened at the Ban Phak Kat permanent checkpoint for a secretariat-level meeting of the General Border Committee (GBC). The preliminary session lasted approximately 30 minutes and focused on setting the agenda for full-delegation talks scheduled for Thursday. The primary goal is to prepare for a formal defense ministers' meeting on December 27 to discuss a verifiable ceasefire.
title: Thailand, Cambodia start General Border Committee secretariat meeting

summary: Officials from Thailand and Cambodia began four days of talks at a border checkpoint in Chanthaburi on Wednesday. The meeting, which was initially at risk due to a disagreement over the venue, aims to negotiate a cessation of hostilities and restore stability. The conflict, which reignited this month, has reportedly killed over 40 people and displaced around one million individuals.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border talks proceed after venue row

summary: Military officials from both nations began four days of talks at the Ban Laem checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The initial secretary-level session on Wednesday lasted only 35 minutes. If these talks progress, defense ministers are expected to meet on Saturday (Dec 27) to finalize a ceasefire. Thailand is also raising concerns about Cambodia using ancient sites and civilian buildings for military positions.
title: Thai-Cambodian border talks open amid hopes for ceasefire

summary: Military officials from Thailand and Cambodia have commenced talks to resume a ceasefire following border clashes that have claimed dozens of lives on both sides. The three-day GBC meeting in Thailand is intended to pave the way for a formal agreement between defense ministers on December 27. The talks follow a Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur and efforts to salvage a truce previously brokered by Malaysia and the United States.
title: Thailand, Cambodia Engage in Talks for Ceasefire Resumption

summary: The Australian Government expressed deep concern over the rapid escalation in the scale and intensity of military clashes. The statement specifically highlighted the use of heavy destructive weapons and the growing humanitarian impact. Australia urged both sides to engage in good faith during the GBC meeting and welcomed mediation efforts by ASEAN, Malaysia, and the United States.
title: Statement on Cambodia–Thailand border conflict

summary: Officials from Thailand and Cambodia have begun four days of talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province aimed at ending border clashes that have killed more than 40 people and displaced around one million. The meeting was delayed due to a disagreement over the venue, with Cambodia initially requesting a neutral site. The talks, organized under the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, are expected to continue through Saturday, with Bangkok expressing hope for a positive outcome if both sides show sincerity.
title: Thailand and Cambodia begin talks to end deadly clashes after venue row

summary: The Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters shared a formal letter from the Cambodian Ministry of Defense, signed by Tea Seiha, addressed to the Thai Defense Minister. The letter expresses Cambodia's intent to negotiate a ceasefire according to the Kuala Lumpur Joint Statement and suggests utilizing the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to verify compliance. However, Thai media noted that as of the publication time, official Cambodian channels had not yet posted this letter publicly.
title: กองทัพไทยเผยจดหมาย กลาโหมกัมพูชาขอเจรจาสงบศึก ให้ยึดข้อตกลงสันติภาพ 28 ต.ค.68
titleEn: Thai military reveals letter from Cambodian Ministry of Defense requesting ceasefire talks based on Oct 28 peace deal

summary: Cambodia dropped its demand to hold border talks in a neutral third country (Malaysia) and sent representatives to Chanthaburi, Thailand. Thailand's Ministry of Defence reiterated its three core conditions: Cambodia must stop firing first, the ceasefire must be verifiable by observers, and Cambodia must cooperate in demining efforts. The atmosphere is described as rigid.
title: กัมพูชายอมถอย! เลิกตื๊อคุยมาเลย์ ยอมมาคุยจันทบุรี ไทยย้ำเงื่อนไขเหล็ก 3 ประการ
titleEn: Cambodia Backs Down! Stops Pushing for Malaysia Venue, Agrees to Talk in Chanthaburi; Thailand Reasserts 3 'Iron Conditions'

summary: Russian Ambassador Anatoly Borovik presented 2 tonnes of rice, cooking oil, noodles, and water to the Cambodian Red Cross (CRC) to support families displaced by the border conflict. The donation was received by CRC Secretary-General Pum Chantinie at their headquarters. Ambassador Borovik expressed condolences for the loss of life and reaffirmed Moscow's humanitarian commitment to Cambodia.
title: Russian Embassy donates supplies to CRC for displaced

summary: Military delegates from both nations met at the Ban Phak Kat checkpoint in Thailand's Chanthaburi province on Wednesday afternoon. Led by Major General Nhem Boraden (Cambodia) and General Nuttapong Praokaew (Thailand), the secretariat meeting aims to set the agenda for formal ministerial talks on December 27. The discussions are focused on establishing a ceasefire and monitoring mechanisms under the watch of ASEAN Observer Teams (AOT).
title: Thailand and Cambodia start the General Border Committee secretariat meeting

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defense reported that Thai fighter jets dropped cluster bombs in Banteay Meanchey and four bombs into civilian areas in Battambang on Wednesday. Thai Army spokesperson Winthai Suvaree countered that any munitions used were directed strictly at military targets and are not meant to harm civilians. He also noted that neither nation is bound by the Convention on Cluster Munitions as they are not signatories.
title: Cambodia says Thailand drops cluster bombs, Thailand claims only targets military objectives

summary: A wild elephant and her newborn calf were found dead in a pond inside the Preah Rokar-Chep Wildlife Sanctuary in Preah Vihear province on December 22. Environmental authorities and park rangers confirmed the deaths were caused by shrapnel from Thai military shelling. Environment Minister Eang Sophalleth condemned the incident, stating that the conflict is destroying Cambodia's natural resources and biodiversity in addition to human lives.
title: Shrapnel from shelling kills wild elephant, calf in Preah Vihear sanctuary

summary: Starting Wednesday, Dec 24, representatives from Thailand and Cambodia began a scheduled four-day negotiation window to resolve border clashes that have claimed at least 86 lives since Dec 7. Thailand is attending with three primary demands: a unilateral ceasefire by Cambodia, verification by observers, and cooperation in landmine clearance.
title: Thailand, Cambodia agree to four days of border conflict talks

summary: As of the evening of December 24, 2025, Cambodian Minister of Information Neth Pheaktra confirmed that 30 Cambodian civilians have been killed and 87 others wounded since the conflict reignited. The figures represent a significant increase in civilian casualties as the border situation remains volatile.
title: Cambodia's civilian death toll over border clashes with Thailand rises to 30

summary: An analysis of the political roots of the current conflict, focusing on a leaked recording of former PM Paetongtarn Shinawatra talking to Hun Sen. The leak led to accusations of compromising national interests, which critics say emboldened Cambodia. The article notes that while US-brokered truces existed, the personal rivalry between political dynasties has spiraled into the most severe border conflict in a decade.
title: Leaked recording reshapes politics, border tensions
titleEn: Leaked Recording Reshapes Politics and Border Tensions

summary: According to the Ministry of National Defense, a Cambodian civilian was killed on the morning of December 25 when Thai forces fired 155mm heavy artillery into Talei village, Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province. This latest casualty brings the total number of Cambodian civilians killed in the border conflict to 30 people.
title: ជម្លោះព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ បណ្ដាលឱ្យពលរដ្ឋស្លូតត្រង់កម្ពុជាបាត់បង់ជីវិត 30 នាក់ហើយ
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand border conflict has killed 30 innocent Cambodian civilians

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
summary: Chinese Special Envoy Deng Xijun conducted shuttle diplomacy from December 18 to 23, meeting with top leaders in Cambodia and Thailand, including Prime Ministers Hun Manet and Anutin Charnvirakul. China expressed deep sadness over casualties and emphasized that the immediate priority is achieving a ceasefire and resuming peaceful dialogue to resolve the border dispute.
title: Special Envoy for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Makes Another Shuttle-Diplomacy Trip for Peace between Cambodia and Thailand

summary: One Cambodian civilian was killed at 8:41 a.m. on December 25, 2025, due to Thai military shelling in Taley village, Kouk Romiet commune, Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province. The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense condemned the attack as a violation of international humanitarian law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 09.30 25/12/25: Cambodian civilian killed by renewed Thai shelling
titleEn: Conflict Update 09:30 Dec 25, 2025: Cambodian civilian killed by renewed Thai shelling

summary: The death toll in the border conflict has risen to 96 as the fighting enters its 18th day. Casualties include soldiers and civilians on both sides. Nearly one million people have been displaced since the escalation began on December 8. Military talks started on Wednesday in Chanthaburi, Thailand, with a high-level meeting scheduled for Saturday. Cambodia reported the death of a civilian from artillery shelling on Thursday, while Thailand reported rocket attacks hitting civilian infrastructure in Sa Kaeo.
title: Death toll reaches 96 as Thailand-Cambodia border clashes enter 18th day

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that at 8:41 a.m. on December 25, Thai military forces fired 155mm artillery shells into a civilian residential area in Ta Lei village, Kouk Romiet commune, Thmar Pouk district, Banteay Meanchey province. The attack resulted in the death of one innocent Cambodian civilian. The ministry described the actions as 'indiscriminate' and a violation of international humanitarian law.
title: Defence Ministry: Thai Military Fires 155mm Artillery into Cambodian Civilian Area, One Killed

summary: The second day of the General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat Meeting began at 9:05 a.m. at the Prom-Pak Kard border crossing between Pailin and Chanthaburi. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated that technical teams are discussing mechanisms for a cessation of hostilities. This meeting serves as preparation for the 3rd Special GBC Meeting scheduled for December 27, which will involve the Defense Ministers of both nations.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Start Second Day of GBC Secretariat Meeting

summary: General Chaiyaphruek, the Army Chief of Staff, stated that the Royal Thai Army has successfully cleared and secured 90% of the sovereign territory previously contested at the border. He maintained that Thailand will only enter into a ceasefire agreement if the Cambodian side officially declares a ceasefire first. He alleged that Cambodia continues to stockpile heavy weaponry in inland areas and that Thailand will continue its mission according to its set goals.
title: 'เสธ.ทบ.' ลั่นจุดยืนไทย 'กัมพูชา' ต้องประกาศ 'หยุดยิง' ก่อน ย้ำคุมพื้นที่อธิปไตยไทย 90% แล้ว
titleEn: Army Chief of Staff asserts Thailand's stance: Cambodia must declare ceasefire first, claims 90% of Thai sovereign area secured

summary: Thai military reports that three houses in Ban Klong Pang, Ta Phraya district, Sa Kaeo, were destroyed by Cambodian rockets early Thursday. No casualties were reported, but the 1st Army Area condemned the attack for targeting civilian areas, stating it shows Cambodia has no intention of ending the conflict.
title: Cambodian rockets destroy houses in Sa Kaeo

summary: Reports state that between 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. on December 25, Thai forces fired more than 30 artillery shells into Sampov Lun district, Battambang province. Additionally, 33 rounds of 155mm shells were reportedly fired into Talei village in Banteay Meanchey. The Cambodian side claims these areas are far from the disputed border zones, framing the shelling as a direct invasion of sovereignty.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 13.50 25/12/25: Thailand bombards Cambodian villages

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed the Indian government's protest regarding the Thai military's destruction of a Hindu statue at the Chong An Ma border pass. He emphasized that the loss of a religious statue, which was built on Thai soil by Cambodia, cannot be compared to the loss of lives and limbs suffered by Thai soldiers defending the border. He also commented on the GBC (General Border Committee) meeting in Chanthaburi, describing the 30-minute session on Dec 24 as just a preliminary greeting and that the process will take several more days.
title: "นายกฯอนุทิน" ฝากให้คิด ทหารไทยสูญเสียชีวิต อวัยวะ แขนขาขาด เท่าไร อินเดียท้วงเหตุทำลายรูปปั้นเทพเจ้าฯ กัมพูชาสร้างล้ำชายแดน
titleEn: PM Anutin urges reflection on lost lives of Thai soldiers as India protests destruction of Hindu statue built by Cambodia in Thai territory

summary: The French Embassy in Phnom Penh has expanded its travel alert for French citizens in Cambodia. An 'orange zone' (travel only if necessary) has been added, extending 30 kilometers south of the existing 'red zone' (no travel) which already covers a 50-kilometer radius from the Thai border. The warning includes Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces. This move follows reports from Cambodia claiming Thai T-50TH aircraft launched strikes in Battambang's Banan District.
title: ฝรั่งเศสขยายเตือนภัยการเดินทางในกัมพูชา
titleEn: France expands travel warnings in Cambodia due to border conflict

summary: Defense Minister Tea Seiha sent best wishes to 18 soldiers (likely wounded or on the frontlines). Additionally, Information Minister Neth Pheaktra cited reports that Thai troops destroyed a Vishnu statue in a disputed area within Cambodian territory, an act condemned as a violation of cultural property and sovereignty.
title: នាយឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ ទៀ សីហា ជូនពរវីរកងទ័ពកម្ពុជា18រូប មានសុខភាពល្អ និងឆាប់វិលមកវិញ
titleEn: General Tea Seiha wishes 18 Cambodian hero soldiers good health and safe return

summary: Electricite du Cambodge (EDC) has joined other national institutions in issuing a formal petition condemning what they term as 'vicious and inhumane' acts by the Thai military. The petition supports the Royal Government of Cambodia's stance and calls for an immediate end to the shelling of innocent civilians along the border.
title: អគ្គិសនីកម្ពុជា ប្រកាសចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោស សង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃមកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាព នៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Electricite du Cambodge Issues Petition Condemning Thai Aggressive War Against Cambodia's Sovereignty

summary: On December 25, between 7:00 AM and 10:50 AM, the Thai military reportedly fired 33 heavy artillery shells into Taly village, Thmar Puok district, Banteay Meanchey. The strike killed one civilian and injured seven others. The Cambodian government condemned the attack as a 'cruel and inhumane' violation of international humanitarian law targeting civilian infrastructure.
title: យោធាថៃ បានបាញ់ផ្លោងកាំភ្លើងប្រភេទ 155ម.ម ចំនួន 33គ្រាប់ ចូលភូមិសាស្ត្រភូមិតាឡី ដើម្បី កម្ទេចលំនៅដ្ឋានរបស់ប្រជាពលរដ្ឋស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Thai military fired 33 shells of 155mm artillery into Taly village to destroy Cambodian civilian homes

summary: The Cambodian Senate issued a formal resolution condemning Thailand for what it calls a 'brutal and illegal invasion' from December 7 to 24. The statement cites the use of heavy artillery and fighter jets against civilians and historical temples, including Preah Vihear. The Senate claims these acts violate the UN Charter, the 1962 ICJ ruling, and recent ceasefire agreements from July and October 2025.
title: ព្រឹទ្ធសភា ប្រកាសចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោស សង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃ មកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាព នៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Senate issues petition condemning Thai invasion of Cambodian sovereignty

summary: Thai military reports successful deep operations resulting in the seizure of strategic locations including Hill 225 and the closure of Khan Ma Pass. Over 18 days of fighting, 23 Thai soldiers have died. On Dec 25, another soldier lost a leg to a landmine near Ta Kwai Temple. The report frames these actions as reclaiming Thai sovereignty and effectively pressuring Cambodian leadership.
title: “ปิดช่องคานม้า-ยึดเนิน 225” เผด็จศึกกัมพูชา สถาปนาอำนาจรัฐไทย
titleEn: 'Close Khan Ma Pass - Seize Hill 225' Defeating Cambodia, establishing Thai state power

summary: The demolition of a Vishnu icon at the border has sparked international concern, including from the Hindu American Foundation, which called it a blow to sacred traditions. The Thai military's joint press center responded that the statue was installed in an area not officially registered as a religious site.
title: Thailand facing heat after statue demolition

summary: PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the removal of a Hindu statue at Chong An Ma was a bilateral security matter. Responding to India's condemnation, he emphasized that a statue cannot be compared to the lives and limbs lost by Thai soldiers in the border conflict. He urged the public to wait for the GBC results but maintained that Thailand only reacts when encroached upon.
title: “อนุทิน” ชี้ รูปปั้นเทียบไม่ได้กับชีวิตทหาร หลังอินเดียประณามไทยทำลายรูปปั้นเทพเจ้าฮินดู
titleEn: PM Anutin: Statues don't compare to soldiers' lives, following Indian condemnation of Hindu deity removal

summary: The second day of the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting in Chanthaburi was marked by tension after Cambodian Defense Minister Tea Seiha denied reports that Cambodia had sent a letter requesting a ceasefire. He attributed the confusion to incorrect translations by Thai media and AI tools. Meanwhile, Thai caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand's actions were a response to being attacked and urged patience for the GBC outcome, while Thailand has reportedly laid out three non-negotiable conditions for a lasting peace.
title: GBC day two tense as Cambodia denies ceasefire letter

summary: A World Food Programme (WFP) report indicates that market functionality has weakened sharply in December 2025 due to the border conflict. Seven markets have closed, and while basic food costs have actually fallen due to decreased demand and seasonal factors, the persistence of clashes threatens long-term food security and supply chain stability for vulnerable households and displacement camps.
title: Market Situation Update Amid Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict (December 2025)

summary: Army Region 2 announced it has successfully seized Hill 225, described as a 'key' strategic location. This maneuver has effectively cut off Cambodian logistics and supply routes leading to Preah Vihear Temple and Hill 350, strengthening the Thai defense line at Prasat Ta Kwai.
title: 'ทภ.2'เผย'ไทย'คุม'เนิน 225' ชี้ขาดสำคัญแนวชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Army Region 2 claims control over strategic 'Hill 225' at Thai-Cambodia border

summary: As of 2:30 p.m. on December 25, 2025, the Ministry of National Defense reported continued Thai shelling along the border in Banteay Meanchey (Svay Chek district), Oddar Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces (near Preah Vihear Temple and Veal Intri). In the Thamma Da area of Pursat, Thai drones reportedly dropped bombs on the Elephant River between 1:50 p.m. and 2:19 p.m.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15.30 25/12/25: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:30 Dec 25, 2025: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs has compiled evidence of heavy weapon usage and human rights violations by Cambodia to be sent to the UN Secretary-General. The military also denied reports from the Cambodian embassy claiming Thai troops harassed tourists, calling it misinformation to deter travel to Thailand.
title: ไทยยื่นหลักฐานส่ง UN กัมพูชาละเมิดมนุษยธรรม เดินหน้าประชุม GBC ดึงอาเซียนร่วมสังเกตการณ์เพื่อความโปร่งใส
titleEn: Thailand submits evidence to UN of Cambodian humanitarian violations; ASEAN to observe GBC talks

summary: Chinese Special Envoy Deng Xijun concluded a shuttle-diplomacy mission (Dec 18-23) to Cambodia and Thailand. He expressed condolences for the 30 Cambodian civilians reported killed as of the morning of Dec 25. China urged both sides to achieve an immediate ceasefire, restore trust, and support ASEAN mediation efforts.
title: China Expresses Hope for Restored Trust and Rebuilt Peace at Cambodia-Thailand Border

summary: The total death toll from the border conflict between Thailand and Cambodia has risen to 96 as of Thursday. Nearly one million people have been displaced on both sides since fighting reignited on December 8. Cambodia reported 31 civilian deaths, while Thailand reported 23 soldiers and 42 civilian deaths (including collateral effects). Military talks are ongoing in Chanthaburi province, with a high-level meeting co-chaired by defense ministers scheduled for Saturday.
title: Death toll climbs to 96 on day 18 of Thai-Cambodian border clashes

summary: A coalition of 896 Cambodian Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) submitted a petition to the international community condemning ongoing Thai military assaults. The petition highlights the use of cluster bombs and the destruction of cultural heritage, specifically the Ta Krabei Temple and damage to Preah Vihear Temple. The groups urge the UN and the international community to demand an immediate ceasefire and the withdrawal of Thai forces.
title: Cambodian Civil Society Organizations Submit Petition over Thai Military Intrusions into Cambodia's Sovereign Territory

summary: Thai Ministry of Defence spokesman Rear Adm Surasant Kongsiri reported that Cambodia fired about 40 BM-21 rockets into a village in Sa Kaeo at 5 am on Thursday. Officials also accused Cambodian embassies of spreading false accusations against Thailand, while security at Suvarnabhumi airport has been stepped up to monitor potential foreign military advisers.
title: No letup in Cambodian shelling of Thai civilian areas, army says

summary: Army Region 1 reported that on the 18th day of conflict, Cambodian forces launched 40 BM-21 rockets into civilian areas of Ban Khlong Phaeng, Sa Kaeo. Over 17,913 Thai residents are currently being sheltered across 40 evacuation centers in 4 border districts.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พื้นที่ จ.สระแก้ว ประจำวัน 25 ธันวาคม 2568
titleEn: Army Region 1 summarizes Sa Kaeo border situation: 40 BM-21 rockets fired at Thai civilians

summary: The 1st Army Region reported that on the 18th day of the conflict (Dec 25), Cambodian forces fired 40 BM-21 rockets into a civilian residential area at Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ta Phraya District, Sa Kaeo. The attack damaged houses, utilities, and farmland. Currently, 17,913 Thai civilians from four border districts have been evacuated to 40 temporary shelters. The military stated this intentional attack on civilians violates international humanitarian law.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สรุปเหตุปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พื้นที่สระแก้วล่าสุด 25 ธ.ค.68
titleEn: 1st Army Region summarizes Thai-Cambodia border clashes in Sa Kaeo, latest Dec 25, 2025

summary: Brigadier General Sopka Priab stated that Chanthaburi and Pailin are sister cities and that Thailand and Cambodia are neighbors that cannot be separated. Despite ongoing border tensions, he emphasized the goal of peace for the people but declined to provide specifics on the progress or direction of the General Border Committee (GBC) negotiations.
title: นายพลเขมร ย้ำ ไทย-กัมพูชา คือพี่น้อง ต้องพึ่งพาแยกกันไม่ได้ ไม่ตอบทิศทางถก GBC
titleEn: Cambodian General stresses Thailand-Cambodia are brothers, must rely on each other, remains silent on GBC direction

summary: The Ministry of National Defense announced that between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM on December 25, Thai forces fired 28 artillery shells into Sampov Loun district, Battambang province. Shelling also reportedly continued in Choke Chey village and Prey Chan village.
title: យោធាថៃ បាញ់ផ្លោងជិត30គ្រាប់ ចូលភូមិសាស្ត្រស្រុកសំពៅលូន
titleEn: Thai military shelled nearly 30 rounds into Sampov Loun district

summary: Cambodia requested to delay the GBC secretariat meeting to 18:00 to review Thai proposals. Capt. Yodthanong of the Border Affairs Department stated that the likelihood of a full ministerial meeting on Dec 27 is only '50-50'. Meanwhile, officials at the Chanthaburi-Pailin border confirmed the situation there remains calm despite the wider conflict.
title: เขมรขอเลื่อนถกหยุดยิงเป็น 18.00 น. ทัพไทยเผยโอกาสเจรจายัง 50-50 ยันจันทบุรีไร้ปะทะ
titleEn: Cambodia asks to delay ceasefire talks to 18:00; Thai military says 50-50 chance for success

summary: Military officials from Thailand and Cambodia met for a second day of Secretariat-level talks in Chanthaburi, Thailand. While a Thai spokesperson noted a decrease in the intensity of clashes, one Cambodian civilian was killed on Thursday and two Thai soldiers were injured by a landmine. Malaysian members of an ASEAN observer team were reportedly present at the meeting.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border talks enter second day as clashes ease

summary: As the GBC Secretariat meeting entered its second day on December 25, Thai air attacks were reported in Battambang province. The article notes that national institutions and citizens are condemning the use of F-16 and T-50 warplanes. Additionally, a mother elephant and her calf were reportedly killed by Thai shelling in a sanctuary in Preah Vihear, sparking further outrage.
title: Cambodia - Thailand Border Talks Enter Second Day as Fighting Continues

summary: The Cambodian National Assembly issued a petition late December 24 condemning Thailand's 'brutal and inhumane invasion.' The statement claims Thailand has used heavy weapons including F-16 and T-50TH jets, warships, and cluster munitions, with strikes reaching 80–90 kilometers deep into Cambodia. It also accused Thailand of using 'toxic gas' and reported that 30 Cambodian civilians have been killed and over 630,000 displaced as of December 24.
title: Cambodia’s National Assembly Issues Petition Condemning Thailand’s Armed Invasion

summary: Reports indicate that Thai forces continued heavy shelling near the Preah Vihear Temple on the morning of December 25, despite UNESCO expressing deep concern over the risk to the World Heritage site. Portions of the temple are reportedly significantly damaged by the bombardment.
title: កងទ័ពថៃបន្តវាយសន្ធាប់មកលើតំបន់ប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារក្រោមក្រសែភ្នែកយូណេស្កូ
titleEn: Thai troops continue to attack Preah Vihear temple area under UNESCO watch

summary: Civil society groups from Cambodia and some Thai citizens are calling for an immediate end to hostilities as civilian casualties mount. The Ministry of Defense provided a detailed log for December 25, reporting heavy artillery (155mm) and DTI-2 rockets hitting Preah Vihear, Ta Moan, and O'Smach, alongside ground troop movements with tanks in Banteay Meanchey's Svay Chek commune.
title: អង្គការសង្គមស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា និងពលរដ្ឋថៃទាមទារឱ្យបញ្ចប់ជម្លោះ ខណៈការស្លាប់របស់ជនស៊ីវិលកើនឡើង
titleEn: Cambodian CSOs and Thai citizens demand end to conflict as civilian deaths rise

summary: Nine more Cambodian civilians were reported killed yesterday, bringing the total death toll to 30. The article claims Thai air forces have struck targets as deep as 170 kilometers from the border despite ongoing General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat talks in Pailin/Chanthaburi. Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn has briefed French officials on the deteriorating humanitarian situation involving over 640,000 displaced persons.
title: Civilian toll rises as Thai assaults continue despite ceasefire talks

summary: Front-page news reports that Cambodia is ignoring the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, choosing to continue heavy shelling even as secretariat talks began. The report highlights the emotional story of a Thai soldier who lost his leg but had to hide the news from his bedridden mother. It also features academics urging Cambodians to stop believing government propaganda aimed at inciting hatred toward Thailand.
title: เดลินิวส์ 26 ธ.ค. กัมพูชาเมิน GBC ยิงถล่มต่อ ชายแดนเดือด-ทหารเสียขาที่ 9
titleEn: Daily News Dec 26: Cambodia Ignores GBC, Shelling Continues; Border Intense as 9th Soldier Loses Leg

summary: Officials at the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting in Chanthaburi have drafted a ceasefire agreement set for December 27, 2025. Both sides will monitor the situation for 72 hours while waiting for a final decision from the Thai National Security Council.
title: คาดหยุดยิง 27 ธ.ค.68 ไทยจับตาสถานการณ์ 72 ชั่วโมง รอ สมช.เคาะเย็นนี้
titleEn: Ceasefire expected Dec 27; Thailand monitors for 72 hours awaiting NSC decision

summary: A ceasefire agreement is expected to be signed on December 27 following three days of intense negotiations at the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting at the Ban Phakkat/Prom border crossing. Despite ongoing reports of heavy shelling and airstrikes killing 31 civilians so far, Thai Prime Minister Anutin expressed optimism that the defense ministers of both nations will sign the document tomorrow. The agreement reportedly involves mine-clearing and the withdrawal of heavy weapons.
title: Cambodia–Thailand Ceasefire Set for December 27 After Border Talks

summary: ACM Prapas Sornjaidee, director of the Joint Thai-Cambodian Situation Briefing Centre, stated that Thai military operations are 'strictly defensive' under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Thailand maintains it has no intention of occupying Cambodian territory. Meanwhile, the Army Chief of Staff noted that most military objectives have been achieved, but Thailand insists Cambodia must be the one to formally declare a ceasefire first as they initiated the conflict.
title: Border operations 'strictly defensive'

summary: According to a statement from Cambodia's Defence Ministry, the Thai military deployed F-16 fighter jets to drop as many as 40 bombs in the Chok Chey village area between 6:08 am and 7:15 am on Friday. This escalation occurred on the third day of bilateral talks aimed at ending the deadly clashes. Meanwhile, Thai media reported that Cambodian forces launched overnight attacks in Sa Kaeo province, damaging homes with shelling.
title: Cambodia says Thailand escalated strikes during border talks

summary: The Thai Army Region 2 announced that it has regained control over 90% of the disputed sovereign territory. It successfully seized 'Hill 225,' a strategic point near Prasat Ta Kwai that connects to Hill 350. However, a combat engineer sustained a serious injury, losing his left leg to a landmine near the temple, making him the 9th soldier to suffer such an injury in this conflict. The army accuses Cambodia of lacking the intent to stop the conflict, citing continued BM-21 rocket fire into Sa Kaeo.
title: ทัพไทยคุมพื้นที่อธิปไตยแล้ว90% ยึดเนิน225สำเร็จ ทหารช่างเหยียบบึ้มขาขาดรายที่9
titleEn: Thai Military Controls 90% of Territory, Successfully Seizes Hill 225; Combat Engineer Loses Leg in 9th Landmine Incident

summary: As GBC Secretariat talks continue, Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence has officially rejected Thai media reports claiming Cambodia requested a ceasefire, labeling it a misinterpretation. On the night of December 25, PM Hun Manet spoke with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio via phone to discuss facilitating a rapid ceasefire and adhering to peace agreements.
title: Border talks underway as Phnom Penh rejects ceasefire claims

summary: On the night of December 25, 2025, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a telephone conversation with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet. Rubio conveyed President Donald Trump's desire for peace and stated that the United States is ready to facilitate talks to end the weeks-long border clashes and restore stability. The call follows reports of nearly 100 deaths and hundreds of thousands of displaced civilians since fighting reignited on December 7.
title: លោក Rubio៖ អាមេរិកត្រៀមសម្របសម្រួលក្នុងកិច្ចចរចាសន្តិភាពរវាងកម្ពុជា និងថៃ
titleEn: Rubio: US ready to facilitate peace talks between Cambodia and Thailand

summary: The Cambodia-Thailand General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat met for a third day in Chanthaburi to negotiate a path toward stability. Amidst these talks, at 9:46 AM on December 26, the Thai military reportedly fired two 155mm artillery shells into the Stung Bot area of Poipet, Banteay Meanchey. The article also mentions diplomatic mediation signals from Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim.
title: ក្រុមលេខាធិការ គណៈកម្មាធិការព្រំដែន ទូទៅកម្ពុជា-ថៃ (GBC) បន្ដកិច្ចប្រជុំថ្ងៃទី3 ដើម្បីឱ្យមាន ស្ថិរភាពឡើងវិញ រវាងប្រទេសទាំងពីរ
titleEn: GBC Secretariat continues Day 3 meeting to restore stability between both countries

summary: The 2nd Army Region reported that the situation at the Thai-Cambodian border remains tense on December 25-26. Cambodian forces have been using artillery and BM-21 rockets to pressure Thai positions, particularly at Chong Sai Taku in Buriram. Thai forces have responded with proportional artillery fire. Despite the attacks, the military confirms that Thailand maintains full control over all primary strategic areas.
title: ชายแดน ยังตึงเครียดหลายจุด ยิงตอบโต้กันต่อเนื่อง แต่ไทยยังคุมพื้นที่หลักได้ทั้งหมด
titleEn: Border remains tense in many spots, continuous fire exchange, but Thailand still controls all main areas

summary: First Lady Pich Chanmony met with families displaced by the border conflict at Koh Pich in Phnom Penh. She expressed sympathy and provided aid to those affected by the ongoing military situation at the border.
title: លោកជំទាវបណ្ឌិត ពេជ ចន្ទមុន្នី ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត អញ្ជើញសំណេះសំណាលសួរសុខទុក្ខ និងផ្ដល់អំណោយជូនប្រជាជនភៀសសឹក ដោយសារការឈ្លានពានរបស់កងទ័ពថៃ នៅកោះពេជ្រ
titleEn: Dr. Pich Chanmony Hun Manet visits and provides gifts to people displaced by Thai military invasion at Koh Pich

summary: As of December 26, the third day of General Border Committee (GBC) secretariat talks in Chanthaburi ended without a consensus. Cambodia continues to reject Thailand's three core proposals: a prior formal declaration of ceasefire by Cambodia, a genuine and continuous cessation of fire, and cooperation on demining. The atmosphere is described as very tense, while an ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) from Malaysia continues to monitor the situation.
title: GBC day three: Cambodia still rejects Thai ceasefire terms

summary: Officials from the Ministry of Information and the state news agency AKP delivered aid and school supplies to approximately 300 families displaced from Koh Kong province. These families fled to Srae Ambel district following Thai military aggression that began on December 13. While some families have started returning home, many remain in temporary shelters at local pagodas (such as Wat Sala Mnang) due to the unstable security situation.
title: មន្រ្តីក្រសួងព័ត៌មាននាំយកអំណោយចែកជូនជនភៀសសឹកនៅស្រុកស្រែអំបិល
titleEn: Information Ministry officials bring aid to displaced persons in Srae Ambel

summary: Reporting on the deep distrust between the neighbors, this article highlights that Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet spoke with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about securing a ceasefire. Despite diplomatic interventions from the US, China, and Malaysia, the conflict over the 800km frontier and temple ruins has intensified. Cambodia claims a heavy bombardment occurred between 6:08 AM and 7:15 AM on Friday even as technical officials were meeting at a border checkpoint for the third consecutive day.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of launching strikes during border peace talks

summary: First Lady Dr. Pich Chanmony met with displaced families in border provinces on Friday to deliver humanitarian aid and encouragement. She conveyed support from Hun Sen, Bun Rany, and PM Hun Manet, emphasizing 'Khmer helping Khmer' while the government defends the nation and assists the hundreds of thousands forced to flee their homes.
title: Pich Chanmony provides support to civilians displaced by the Cambodia–Thailand border conflict

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a field report detailing Thai military actions on December 26. It reported that at 5:40 AM, Thai forces shelled Ta Krabey Temple, followed by artillery fire at Ta Moan Temple and Preah Vihear Temple. Most significantly, between 6:08 AM and 7:15 AM, Thai F-16 jets reportedly dropped 40 bombs on Chok Chey village, causing significant destruction. The ministry stated that Cambodian forces are fighting back with 'high vigilance.'
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ ធ្វើបច្ចុប្បន្នភាពពីស្ថានពាក់ព័ន្ធករណីយោធាថៃ បន្តការបាញ់ប្រហារឈ្លានពានមកលើដែនអធិបតេយ្យកម្ពុជា រយៈពេល20ថ្ងៃ
titleEn: Ministry of National Defense updates on Thai military aggression over 20 days

summary: At approximately 1:00 PM on December 26, Thai fighter jets dropped 10 bombs in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province. This area is located roughly 80km from the Thai border, marking a significant escalation and deep penetration into Cambodian territory. The report frames this as an attempt to invade Cambodian sovereignty beyond the disputed border zones.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 14.30 26/12/25: Thai F-16s bomb 80km inside Cambodian border

summary: Cambodia has accused Thai forces of conducting 'ruthless' aerial attacks on Friday morning, specifically targeting the village of Chouk Chey with dozens of bombs. The Cambodian Defence Ministry described the strikes as 'grave acts of aggression' that damaged civilian property and infrastructure. The violence occurred while both nations were engaged in talks intended to de-escalate the border conflict that has killed 96 people since December 8.
title: Cambodia blames Thailand for ‘ruthless’ bombardment amid border talks

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation briefed representatives from 21 diplomatic missions on the latest border developments. Secretary of State Kung Phoak emphasized Cambodia's commitment to an immediate ceasefire and the peaceful resolution of disputes through existing bilateral mechanisms, while highlighting the impact of Thai military incursions on civilians.
title: Cambodia briefs foreign diplomats on developments in border tensions with Thailand

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet spoke by phone with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss ways to secure a ceasefire. He emphasized Cambodia's commitment to the Kuala Lumpur Joint Statement and the July 28 truce framework to build long-term peace.
title: សម្តេចមហាបវរធិបតី ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត ជួបរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសអាមេរិក តាមទូរស័ព្ទ បញ្ជាក់ជំហរគោរពសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍រួមកូឡាឡាំពួរលើការដោះស្រាយជម្លោះព្រំដែនជាមួយថៃ
titleEn: PM Hun Manet meets US Secretary of State via phone to confirm stance on Kuala Lumpur Statement for resolving border conflict with Thailand

summary: Army Region 2 summarized border tension on December 26, noting that Cambodian forces fired BM-21 multiple rocket launchers from the Preah Vihear temple area into Thailand's Phu Ma Khuea. One Thai soldier was injured during artillery exchanges in the Phu Ma Khuea–Don Ao area. Additionally, two soldiers were injured by PMN-2 anti-personnel landmines during clearing operations at Prasat Ta Kwai. Cambodian forces also shelled near Prasat Ta Muen Thom and Chong Sai Taku.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปสถานการณ์ ยังมีปะทะหลายจุด เขมรยิง BM-21 จากเขาพระวิหารใส่ภูมะเขือ ยิงปืนใหญ่เข้าประสาทตาเมือนธม
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summary: Clashes Continue in Multiple Areas; Cambodia Fires BM-21 from Preah Vihear to Phu Ma Khuea

summary: The Government Savings Bank (GSB) has announced special measures to assist those affected by the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Debt will be cancelled for soldiers and border patrol police killed in action since December 7, 2025. Additionally, civilians forced to evacuate or who have lost income due to the fighting are eligible for a 3-month debt moratorium with no interest charged.
title: ออมสิน ยกหนี้ทหาร-ตชด. เสียชีวิตเหตุชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พักหนี้ผู้อพยพที่ขาดรายได้ 3 งวด
titleEn: GSB cancels debt for soldiers killed in border conflict, offers 3-month holiday for affected civilians

summary: The Department of Foreign Trade reported that border trade between Thailand and Cambodia has suffered a loss of approximately 72 billion baht over the first 11 months of 2025. This decline is largely attributed to the persistent border conflict and restricted movement at various checkpoints. Trade with Myanmar is also facing significant challenges due to regional instability.
title: เผยยอด 11 เดือน ค้าชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา เสียหายแล้ว 7.2 หมื่นล้าน
titleEn: 11-month trade figures show 72 billion baht loss in Thai-Cambodian border trade

summary: Thai military units discovered several improvised explosive devices (IEDs) made from RPG heads and C4 explosives in the Ta Kwai area of Surin province. The 2nd Army Area stated this is evidence that Cambodian forces are targeting the lives of personnel moving to assist in the area. Clashes with BM-21 rockets and drones continue in the sector.
title: ทภ.2 พบ “กับระเบิด” แสวงเครื่องอานุภาพทำลายสูงในพื้นที่ตาควาย
titleEn: Army Region 2 Finds High-Explosive IEDs in Ta Kwai Area

summary: Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodia's Defense Minister Tea Seiha are expected to hold high-level talks in Thailand's Chanthaburi province on Saturday. The meeting follows three days of technical negotiations. The death toll from recent clashes has reached 99. Thailand has proposed a 72-hour ceasefire and offered the release of 18 Cambodian prisoners of war if terms are met.
title: Thailand, Cambodia move towards final ceasefire talks over weekend

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that the Thai military fired approximately 360 shells into Sok Sang and Prey Chan villages in Banteay Meanchey province between 7:00 am and 2:30 pm on December 26. The ministry described the actions as brutal and indiscriminate attacks violating international humanitarian law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15.20 26/12/25: 360 shells fired by Thai aggressors at 2 Cambodian villages today
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:20 26/12/25: 360 shells fired by Thai aggressors at 2 Cambodian villages today

summary: A detailed report from Thai Rath describes the escalation of fighting in Sa Kaeo on December 26, just one day before the planned ceasefire. Surapha Task Force soldiers moved to secure 3 strategic points, resulting in a fierce battle. Cambodia reportedly used BM-21 rockets and heavy artillery. The report emphasizes the sacrifice of 3 Thai soldiers and the skepticism regarding Cambodia's sincerity despite their proposal of the '6th draft' at the GBC talks.
title: ตึงเครียดตลอดแนวรบ ก่อนเจรจา “หยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง” หวังเริ่มต้น 27 ธ.ค.68
titleEn: Tension Across the Frontline Before '72-Hour Ceasefire' Negotiations Hoped to Start Dec 27, 2025

summary: Secretarial-level talks for the Thailand–Cambodia General Border Committee (GBC) concluded in Chanthaburi on December 26. The two sides have reached a '6th draft' agreement which is now being reviewed by the Thai National Security Council (NSC). If approved, a formal signing ceremony between Thai Defense Minister Gen Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian Defense Minister Gen Tea Seiha is expected on December 27, aimed at initiating a 72-hour ceasefire.
title: GBC talks conclude with 6th draft; NSC decision key to Dec 27 ceasefire

summary: The First Army Region reported that three Thai soldiers from the 2nd Infantry Regiment, 2nd Infantry Battalion, were killed on the evening of December 26 during a Cambodian BM-21 rocket attack at Ban Nong Chan, Khok Sung District, Sa Kaeo province. The deceased were identified as Sgt. Maj. 1st Class Pongsakorn Nakthongdee, Pvt. Patipat Sornpradit, and Pvt. Thiwatawan Phonyiam. The military continues to hold three key positions despite the attacks.
title: ทหารไทยพลีชีพ 3 นายปกป้องอธิปไตยชายแดนบ้านหนองจาน สระแก้ว
titleEn: 3 Thai soldiers killed defending sovereignty at Ban Nong Chan border, Sa Kaeo

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated on Friday that the country's Defence Minister will join border talks on Saturday, December 27, in an attempt to reach a truce. The potential agreement is expected to follow the framework of a previous deal brokered by the US and Malaysia in July. The PM urged both sides to adhere to their promises and reduce hostilities to allow displaced civilians to return home.
title: Thai defence minister to attend truce talks with Cambodia, PM says

summary: Army Region 1 reported that 3 Thai soldiers were killed on December 26 during a strategic operation to secure territory in Sa Kaeo province. The fallen soldiers were identified as Sergeant First Class Pongsakorn Nakthongdee, Private Patiphat Sornpradit, and Private Tiwtawan Phonyiam. Fighting was most intense at Ban Nong Chan, where Cambodian forces used heavy artillery. Currently, 18,188 Thai civilians are taking refuge in 40 temporary shelters across four districts in Sa Kaeo.
title: ด่วน! ทหารเสียชีวิต สมรภูมิบ้านหนองจาน 3 นาย หลังดำเนินกลยุทธ์ เพื่อยึดครอง 3 พื้นที่ จ.สระแก้ว
titleEn: Urgent! 3 Soldiers Killed in Ban Nong Chan Battlefield After Operation to Secure 3 Areas in Sa Kaeo

summary: An urgent request for clear passage on Mittraphap and Phahonyothin roads was issued for ambulances transporting three soldiers injured in border clashes in Surin province. The soldiers are being moved to Phramongkutklao Hospital in Bangkok, which has the highest capability for treating war-related injuries.
title: ขอทางด่วน ส่ง 3 ทหารกล้าเหยื่อปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา เข้ากรุงเทพฯ
titleEn: Expressway requested for ambulance moving 3 brave soldiers from border clashes to Bangkok

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the National Security Council has authorized the Defense Minister to sign a ceasefire agreement in Chanthaburi on Saturday. However, hostilities continued late Friday as a Cambodian rocket attack in Surin province killed three Thai soldiers and injured 17 others. Anutin emphasized that while Thailand agrees to the truce, it will not accept returning to pre-conflict positions in secured areas, stating Thailand 'cannot retreat'.
title: Hopes rise for ceasefire
titleEn: Hopes rise for ceasefire despite late Friday casualties

summary: Following three days of negotiations in Chanthaburi, the GBC secretariat teams have reached a consensus on a draft joint statement and ceasefire terms. The agreement is set to take effect on December 27. Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Thai Defense Minister will attend the meeting today to finalize the statement under the Kuala Lumpur Agreement framework.
title: Thailand and Cambodia agree on the terms of the initial ceasefire

summary: Authorities in Ubon Ratchathani, Surin, and Sa Kaeo have issued urgent warnings for residents to remain in bunkers or evacuation centers until a projected ceasefire at 12:00 PM on Saturday, Dec 27. Officials fear that Cambodian forces may launch heavy attacks or long-range artillery strikes in the final hours leading up to the truce in an attempt to regain lost strategic positions. Local defense volunteers have been told to dim lights and watch for unidentified drones.
title: Border districts urge residents to stay in bunkers ahead of expected noon ceasefire on December 27

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the National Security Council has authorized the Defence Minister to meet his Cambodian counterpart on Saturday, December 27. The goal is to reach a deal based on a previous October pact, which includes mine-clearing, withdrawing heavy weapons, and allowing ceasefire monitors. Anutin mentioned that if a 72-hour ceasefire is maintained, Thailand will consider releasing 18 Cambodian prisoners of war captured in previous clashes.
title: Thailand's PM expresses hope for ceasefire with Cambodia by Dec 27

summary: Following the GBC Joint Statement, the Thai military (Army Regions 1 and 2) reported successful reclamation and control of key strategic border areas. In Sa Kaeo, Thai forces secured Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. In Surin and Sisaket, troops established control over Hill 225 and areas near Preah Vihear before the 12:00 PM ceasefire took effect on Dec 27. The 72-hour window is now being used to verify sincerity before the potential return of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
title: เช็กพื้นที่ล่าสุด ไทยยึดคืนได้ หลังเจรจาหยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง
titleEn: Checking Latest Areas Reclaimed by Thailand After 72-Hour Ceasefire Negotiation

summary: Cambodia accused the Thai military of dropping as many as 40 bombs using F-16 fighter jets on Chok Chey village in Banteay Meanchey province on Friday morning. Meanwhile, Thai media reported that Cambodian forces launched heavy attacks overnight in Sa Kaeo province, damaging several homes. Despite the escalation, the defense ministers of both countries are scheduled to meet on Saturday, December 27, to negotiate an end to the fighting, which has killed over 40 people and displaced around 1 million civilians.
title: Thailand escalating strikes: Cambodia

summary: Hostilities between Thailand and Cambodia have continued for a third week, with at least 98 people killed and over 500,000 displaced since the ceasefire broke down in early December. International pressure from China, the US, and ASEAN has intensified, leading to a high-level meeting scheduled for Saturday between the defense ministers of both nations to restore a previous peace pact.
title: Thai Defence Minister to attend truce talks with Cambodia, PM says

summary: The Election Commission (EC) of Thailand has published special guidelines in the Royal Gazette to ensure the upcoming general election can proceed in Chanthaburi, Trat, Buri Ram, Si Sa Ket, Sa Kaeo, Surin, and Ubon Ratchathani. Due to the border conflict and evacuations, officials are authorized to use electronic systems for voter list notifications if physical delivery is unsafe, and to adapt polling procedures to prioritize voter safety without disenfranchising citizens in conflict zones.
title: Election safeguards extend to border areas
titleEn: Election Commission issues special voting measures for 7 border provinces

summary: Thai and Cambodian General Border Committee (GBC) secretariats have finalized a draft ceasefire agreement after three days of tense negotiations in Chanthaburi. The deal, which includes a 72-hour halt to hostilities, is scheduled for signing by the defense ministers of both nations on Saturday, Dec 27. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand will not trade territory for business interests and that the military has successfully established sovereignty over contested areas.
title: เจรจา GBC ไทย-เขมรจบแล้ว หยุดยิง 72 ชม. กห. 2 ฝ่ายลงนาม 27 ธ.ค.
titleEn: GBC talks concluded: 72-hour ceasefire agreed, Defense Ministers to sign Dec 27

summary: The Second Army Region of Thailand reports that it has successfully gained 100% control over the Ban Nong Chan area. Troops are currently fortifying positions at Phu Ma Khua and Ta Kwai due to a high risk of Cambodian forces attempting to retake lost ground. The report notes recent heavy clashes involving Cambodian BM-21 rocket launchers striking civilian areas and confirmed that Thai F-16s conducted airstrikes against Cambodian weapon depots in Siem Reap province, more than 60km from the border.
title: ยึดหนองจาน100% ทภ.2ตรึงกำลังภูมะเขือ-ตาควาย เสี่ยงสูงกัมพูชาจ้องโจมตีเอาคืน
titleEn: Ban Nong Chan 100% secured; Army Region 2 on high alert at Phu Ma Khua and Ta Kwai for potential counter-attacks

summary: At 7:31 AM on December 27, 2025, Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly dropped four bombs on Cambodian civilian areas in Kampong Svay commune, Serei Saophoan City, Banteay Meanchey province. The Ministry of Defense stated that Cambodian forces remain on high alert and vigilant to defend territorial integrity and national dignity.
title: យោធាថៃ បានប្រើយន្តហោះចម្បាំង F-16 ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់ បែកចំនួន 4គ្រាប់ ចូលទីតាំងប្រជាជនស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា ក្នុងក្រុងសិរីសោភ័ណ នៅម៉ោង 7:31នាទីព្រឹក
titleEn: Thai military uses F-16 fighter jets to drop 4 bombs on Cambodian civilian locations in Serei Saophoan at 7:31 AM

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of December 26 evening, Thai military shelling and bombardment has resulted in a total of 31 deaths and 91 injuries among Cambodian civilians since December 7. The latest casualties include one death in Siem Reap and one injury in Banteay Meanchey. The report highlights severe impacts on civilian areas across multiple border provinces.
title: ក្រសួងមហាផ្ទៃ ៖ អំពើឈ្លានរបស់ថៃ លើដែនអធិបតេយ្យកម្ពុជា បណ្ដាលឱ្យពលរដ្ឋកម្ពុជាស្លាប់កើនឡើង 31នាក់ និងរបួស 91នាក់
titleEn: Ministry of Interior: Thai aggression on Cambodian sovereignty leads to 31 deaths and 91 injuries

summary: Between 7:31 AM and 8:00 AM on December 27, Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly violated Cambodian airspace and dropped 16 bombs in Banteay Meanchey province. This incident occurred just hours before the scheduled 12:00 PM ceasefire. The report reflects the high tension and continued military activity leading up to the diplomatic agreement.
title: យោធាថៃ ប្រើ F-16 បាញ់16គ្រាប់ ចូលបន្ទាយមានជ័យ
titleEn: Thai military uses F-16s to drop 16 bombs in Banteay Meanchey

summary: As of the morning of December 27, the 2nd Army Area reported that the situation along the Northeastern border remains tense. Clashes involving heavy weaponry continued through December 26 in Si Sa Ket province. Thai forces maintain control of strategic high grounds despite constant pressure.
title: ในประเทศ - ทภ 2 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทยกัมพูชา ศรีสะเกษปะทะหนัก หลายพื้นที่ยังตึงเครียด
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summary: Heavy Clashes in Si Sa Ket, Tensions Remain High

summary: The 1st Army Area released a tribute to three soldiers (one Master Sergeant and two Privates) who were killed on December 26 while defending Ban Nong Chan in Sa Kaeo. Cambodian forces reportedly used heavy artillery and mortars to attack the position after Thai troops successfully secured the area.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สดุดีทหารกล้า 3 นาย สังกัด ร.2 พัน.2 รอ. สละชีพปกป้องอธิปไตยของไทย
titleEn: 1st Army Area Honors 3 Fallen Soldiers from 2nd Infantry Regiment

summary: Reports indicate that despite a consensus reached on ceasefire terms, the Thai military launched at least three F-16 bombing raids on December 27. At 7:00 AM, strikes targeted Anlong Veng district; at 7:30 AM and 7:31 AM, bombs were dropped on Serei Sophon city and Kampong Svay Sangkat in Banteay Meanchey province, specifically hitting civilian residential areas.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.30 27/12/25: Despite apparent ceasefire agreement, Thailand launches multiple F-16 bombing raids on Cambodia this morning

summary: Thailand deployed F-16 fighter jets to drop approximately 40 bombs on a village in the Cambodian province of Banteay Meanchey on Saturday morning. The Thai military confirmed the operation, stating it was a necessary self-defense measure to protect Sa Kaeo province. This escalation occurred while both nations were holding working-level talks to negotiate a ceasefire following weeks of intense border fighting.
title: Thailand bombs village in Cambodia amid border talks

summary: Thai fighter jets dropped dozens of bombs near the northwestern Cambodian village of Chouk Chey on Friday morning, according to reports from Cambodia's state news agency. The strikes caused 'extensive destruction' to civilian homes and infrastructure even as officials were in the third day of talks. Thailand has previously demanded that Cambodia announce a truce first and cooperate in demining efforts.
title: Thailand bombs a village in Cambodia even as both nations hold border talks to end armed clashes

summary: The 1st Army Area clarified that social media reports claiming the death of Private Nithikorn Somtum are false. The soldier was injured in the line of duty at Ban Nong Chan and underwent successful surgery; he is currently in safe condition under medical supervision.
title: ทภ 1 แจ้ง พลทหารนิธิกร ไม่ได้เสียชีวิต แค่ได้รับบาดเจ็บ อยู่ระหว่างแพทย์ดูแลใกล้ชิด
titleEn: Army Confirms Private Nithikorn is Not Dead, Only Injured

summary: The Club of Cambodian Journalists (CCJ) distributed protective vests and helmets to 57 journalists from 36 media organizations to ensure their safety while reporting from high-risk zones along the Cambodia-Thailand border. This move comes as security risks remain elevated despite ongoing diplomatic talks.
title: Club of Cambodian Journalists distributes protective gear to border reporters

summary: A 16-point joint statement was signed by defense ministers to halt a 21-day clash. The agreement focuses on preventing escalation by freezing military positions along the Dangrek mountains and enabling the return of nearly one million displaced civilians. The dispute remains rooted in colonial-era maps and territory around ancient temple sites.
title: Thailand, Cambodia sign ceasefire agreement; to freeze troop positions, allow affected civilians to return home

summary: Thailand and Cambodia agreed on Saturday to halt weeks of fierce border clashes, the worst in years. The joint statement, signed by Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian counterpart Tea Seiha, went into effect at noon. Both sides committed to maintaining current troop deployments without further movement to avoid heightening tensions. The fighting, which included fighter jet sorties and artillery exchanges, has killed at least 101 people and displaced over half a million since early December.
title: Thailand and Cambodia agree to ‘immediate’ ceasefire: joint statement

summary: Details of the 3rd Special General Border Committee (GBC) meeting report a 16-point agreement. Key points include an immediate ceasefire starting at 12:00 PM on Dec 27 covering all weapons, freezing troop movements/patrols, and allowing civilians to return home. The agreement explicitly states it does not affect border demarcation, which remains the responsibility of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).
title: เปิดรายละเอียดไทย-กัมพูชาหยุดยิง 16 ข้อ งดโจมตีทุกประเภท คงทหารไว้ตำแหน่งปัจจุบัน ไม่เกี่ยวเรื่องเขตแดน-โยนกลับเป็นหน้าที่ JBC
titleEn: Full 16-Point Thai-Cambodian Ceasefire Details: End All Attacks, Maintain Current Troop Positions, Border Issues Referred to JBC

summary: Thai and Cambodian defense ministers signed a Joint Statement in Chanthaburi to end hostilities. The deal includes a 72-hour 'danger zone' period to prove sincerity before returning 18 Cambodian POWs. Cooperation on humanitarian demining and cybercrime suppression was also highlighted as urgent agendas to build trust.
