title: Thailand and Cambodia Firm Up Ceasefire in China

summary: Cambodian Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn stated that if conditions remain stable, 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand since July 2025 are expected to be released at 12:00 PM on December 30. The release follows the 72-hour ceasefire agreement period. Thailand has reportedly notified the International Red Cross to coordinate the process.
title: รองนายกฯกัมพูชารอลุ้น คาด 18 ทหารเชลยศึกจะถูกปล่อยตัวพรุ่งนี้ ลั่นจะไม่มีปัญหาใดๆ
titleEn: Cambodian DPM Expects Release of 18 Prisoners of War Tomorrow, Vows No Issues

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi hosted a two-day meeting in Yunnan ending Dec 29 with the foreign ministers of Thailand and Cambodia. The talks aimed to consolidate the Dec 27 ceasefire. A key milestone is the expected return of 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand since July, scheduled for Dec 30, provided the 72-hour truce holds. China pledged support for de-mining and the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT).
title: China pushes Cambodia and Thailand to consolidate ceasefire as 18 Cambodian soldiers expected home on Dec 30

summary: While diplomatic talks proceed in China, Thailand has raised concerns regarding fresh ceasefire violations allegedly committed by Cambodian forces. The ceasefire, signed Dec 27, was intended to end 20 days of fighting that killed dozens and displaced nearly one million people. The 72-hour observation window concludes at noon on Tuesday (Dec 30), which is the deadline for the promised return of Cambodian prisoners of war.
title: Thailand, Cambodia engage in rebuilding ties, mutual trust as Bangkok claims ceasefire violation

summary: The Thai Army reported detecting numerous Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace, totaling over 250 incursions. Consequently, the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners of war, originally scheduled for noon on December 30 after a 72-hour ceasefire, has been postponed. The Thai military views these drone activities as a violation of the de-escalation measures agreed upon during the recent GBC meeting.
title: ทบ.พบโดรนเขมรรุกล้ำอธิปไตย เลื่อนส่งคืน 18 เชลย
titleEn: Thai Army Finds Cambodian Drones Violating Sovereignty, Postpones Return of 18 Prisoners

summary: Families in Pailin province are still waiting for the return of 18 soldiers held by Thailand for 154 days. Although a 16-point agreement was signed on December 27, Thai Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura indicated that security agencies detected drone encroachments, which has complicated the scheduled release. Cambodia has urged immediate repatriation as per the terms.
title: The 12 PM Deadline Has Passed, But 18 Cambodian Soldiers Remain in Thai Custody

summary: Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence, Lt. Gen. Mali Socheata, denied Thai claims that over 250 drones from Cambodia violated Thai airspace on December 29. She stated that Cambodia is strictly adhering to the GBC joint statement and the ceasefire, and has issued strict bans on any drone flights in border provinces.
title: កម្ពុជា ពុំបានបង្ហោះយានគ្មានមនុស្សបើកជាង 250គ្រឿង ចូលរំលោភដែនអធិបតេយ្យរបស់ថៃទេ
titleEn: Cambodia did not launch more than 250 UAVs to violate Thailand's sovereignty

summary: Phnom Penh has proposed an urgent special meeting with Thailand to resume the work of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). The goal is to address stalled border survey and demarcation work following the recent ceasefire agreement. This move is seen as an effort to resolve underlying territorial disputes that triggered the recent armed conflict.
title: Cambodia seeks meeting with Thailand to resume demarcation

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi hosted an urgent trilateral meeting with his Thai and Cambodian counterparts in Yuxi on December 29. The meeting resulted in a three-point consensus focused on looking ahead, making steady incremental progress, and rebuilding mutual trust following the December 27 ceasefire. Wang Yi emphasized that both Southeast Asian nations are committed to de-escalating and improving relations after weeks of deadly border clashes.
title: China-Cambodia-Thailand FMs' meeting held in China's Yunnan Province

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized in a national message that the ceasefire is not a surrender or cession of territory. He stated that the decision was made to protect the lives of civilians, noting that 32 civilians have been killed and 93 injured in the conflict so far. He highlighted that the international boundary remains governed by existing treaties and the ceasefire allows half a million displaced people to return home.
title: Cambodia agreed to ceasefire to protect its people from the pain of conflict, says Prime Minister

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokesperson for the Cambodian Ministry of National Defense, issued a statement on December 29 categorically denying Thai claims that 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai territory. She emphasized that Cambodia remains committed to the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement from December 27 and has strict orders prohibiting any UAV launches in border areas.
title: ‘มาลี’ โต้ไทย เขมรยึดมั่นในสันติภาพ ไม่ได้ส่งโดรนกว่า 250 ลำล้ำแดน
titleEn: Maly Rebuts Thailand: Cambodia Committed to Peace, Denies Sending 250 Drones Across Border

summary: Border Patrol Police and Humanitarian Mine Action Unit 1 are inspecting and disposing of unexploded ordnance, including BM-21 rocket remnants and artillery shells, in border villages of Sa Kaeo Province. Residents returning home are warned not to touch suspicious objects and to report them to authorities immediately via hotlines 191 or 1599.
title: Thai authorities clear unexploded ordnance along Thailand–Cambodia border to ensure civilian safety

summary: The Ministry of National Defence of Cambodia has categorically rejected Thailand's claim that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai airspace on December 29. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata called the allegations unfounded and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the December 27 ceasefire. She noted that strict instructions have been issued to provincial authorities to prohibit all drone launches.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Claim of Drone Incursions, Reaffirms Commitment to Ceasefire

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has categorically rejected claims made by the Thai side on Dec 29 that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai territory. A spokesperson stated that strict orders are in place prohibiting the launch of any UAVs and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the Dec 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: เขมรปฏิเสธข้อกล่าวหาไทย โดรน 250 ลำรุกล้ำน่านฟ้า
titleEn: Cambodia denies Thai allegations of 250 drones violating airspace

summary: In the wake of a brokered ceasefire, China hosted trilateral talks in Yunnan province on December 29. While Beijing positions itself as a peacemaker, tension remains as the Thai army reports drone violations by Cambodia. Thailand is reportedly 'reconsidering' the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners due to these fresh violations of the ceasefire agreement.
title: China steps out of diplomatic shadows to take credit for efforts on Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire

summary: The Thai military has officially accused Cambodia of violating the newly signed December 27 ceasefire by flying more than 250 drones over Thai territory on Monday. This development threatens the stability of the truce, which was intended to end weeks of intense conflict. The accusations coincided with diplomatic talks in China aimed at solidifying the peace agreement.
title: Thai army accuses Cambodia of violating truce with over 250 drones

summary: Local reporters in Surin noted that residents who returned home during the 72-hour ceasefire (expiring noon, Dec 30) are on high alert. Cambodian sources claimed their military has not allowed Cambodian civilians back into the O'Smach area, contrasting with Thai authorities allowing Thais to return. Vendors at Chong Chom market expressed a lack of trust in the ceasefire and readiness to flee immediately if fighting erupts.
title: ลุ้นเที่ยงนี้! ครบ 72 ชม. ไทย-กัมพูชา ลงนามหยุดยิง แม่ค้าชายแดนช่องจอมไม่กลัว พร้อมอพยพทุกเมื่อ
titleEn: Tension at noon! 72-hour ceasefire ends; Chong Chom border vendors ready to evacuate if war resumes

summary: Army Region 2 reported the border situation as of Dec 29, noting no heavy weapon clashes during the 72-hour ceasefire. However, they detected Cambodian military movements, including about 30 trucks transporting logistics from Ban Char to Ban Kon Prambei in Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket, and drones patrolling Thai positions.
title: นับถอยหลังหยุดยิงครบ 72 ชม. ทภ.2 แจ้งยังไร้เหตุปะทะชายแดนกัมพูชา
titleEn: Countdown to end of 72-hour ceasefire; Army Region 2 reports no clashes on Cambodian border

summary: The Ministry of Interior held a meeting on Dec 29 with governors from 7 border provinces to coordinate the implementation of the GBC joint statement. Officials emphasized monitoring the 72-hour ceasefire expiration at noon on Dec 30 and ensuring the safety of civilians returning home, under the 'Safe and Dignified' return principle.
title: ก.มหาดไทย ประชุมผู้ว่าฯ ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ถกเข้มแนวทางปฏิบัติข้อตกลง GBC
titleEn: Interior Ministry meets border governors to discuss GBC agreement implementation

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the 72-hour ceasefire observation period officially ends at 12:00 PM today (Dec 30). Security agencies report the situation is normal, but the PM warned that the military cannot yet be fully complacent. He emphasized the need for continued vigilance despite the current lack of clashes.
title: ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชายังสงบ "อนุทิน" จับตาครบ 72 ชม. หยุดยิง 12.00 น. วันนี้
titleEn: Thai-Cambodia border remains calm; Anutin monitors completion of 72-hour ceasefire at noon today

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated on December 30 that the 72-hour deadline for full ceasefire implementation has been reached. She reported that the situation along the Cambodia-Thailand border remains calm and stable. This follows the agreement reached during the GBC meeting on December 27.
title: គ្រប់3ថ្ងៃ នៃការអនុវត្ត បទឈប់បាញ់ពេញលេញ សភាពការណ៍ នៅព្រំដែន មានលក្ខណៈស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ល្អ
titleEn: After 3 days of full ceasefire implementation, the border situation remains calm

summary: Following weeks of intense fighting that killed over 100 people and displaced 440,000 Cambodians, Caritas Cambodia has launched an emergency appeal to support 5,000 families in 20 priority camps. The aid includes food, shelter kits, solar lights, and psychosocial support for children traumatized by artillery fire and air strikes. Over 315,000 people are currently sheltering in 200 government evacuation sites facing overcrowding and poor sanitation.
title: Caritas Cambodia steps up aid for displaced families along the Thailand–Cambodia border

summary: Thailand has officially postponed the scheduled release of 18 Cambodian soldiers (originally set for Dec 30) after security agencies detected Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace. This action is considered a breach of the GBC joint statement which prohibits provocations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura stated the landmine incidents are also a serious concern for the Thai side.
title: สีหศักดิ์แจงคณะทูต ไทยเลื่อนปล่อย 18 ทหารกัมพูชา หลังพบโดรนรุกล้ำ
titleEn: Sihasak briefs diplomats: Thailand postpones release of 18 Cambodian troops due to drone violations

summary: The Thai Cabinet acknowledged the Ministry of Commerce's measures to help citizens and businesses affected by the border conflict. Key actions include controlling commodity prices, finding new markets for exporters, and providing free space for small vendors and OTOP producers to sell products outside the conflict zones.
title: ครม.รับทราบมาตรการบรรเทาผลกระทบชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Cabinet acknowledges measures to mitigate impact on Thai-Cambodian border

summary: The National Mine Action Center (NMAC) reported that on Dec 29, a Thai soldier from the 1st Cavalry Division lost his left leg and suffered eye injuries after stepping on a landmine while clearing an area in Kantharalak, Sisaket. This is the 11th Thai soldier to suffer such a loss since the conflict began. NMAC condemned the use of mines as a violation of the Ottawa Convention.
title: ศทช.แถลงทุ่นระเบิดสังหารเขมร ทําทหารไทยสูญเสียรายที่ 11 ภัยเงียบละเมิดออตตาวา
titleEn: NMAC announces Cambodian landmine claims 11th Thai soldier casualty, calling it a violation of Ottawa Treaty

summary: Thai PBS summarizes the Army Region 2 report, highlighting specific drone incursions near Prasat Ta Muen Thom (31 drones) and sightings of Cambodian patrols. While heavy artillery has ceased, the military suspects these movements are for assessing Thai deployments. Residents are urged to report suspicious objects to EOD teams.
title: ทภ.2 ยันชายแดนไร้ปะทะ พบกัมพูชาขนกำลัง-โดรนสอดแนม
titleEn: Army Region 2: Border quiet but Cambodian troop movement and drones detected

summary: The ceasefire reached its 72-hour benchmark on Tuesday, December 30, but the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers remains unconfirmed. Thailand has expressed concerns over alleged drone incursions, while Cambodia has issued a nationwide drone ban to protect the truce. The conflict has reportedly killed 101 people and displaced over 500,000 civilians since it reignited earlier this month.
title: Thailand–Cambodia truce holds after 72 hours amid tensions over detainees

summary: Foreign ministers from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met on December 29 to discuss the border crisis. The priority is to ensure the ceasefire remains effective. They agreed to support the Joint Border Committee (JBC) to demarcate the border according to international law and the UN Charter. China is ready to help with humanitarian demining through the Joint Coordination Task Force (JCTF) and support ASEAN Observers (AOT).
title: ចិន កម្ពុជា ថៃ គាំទ្រដល់គណៈកម្មការចម្រុះខ័ណ្ឌសីមាព្រំដែន និងច្បាប់ UN ដើម្បីបញ្ចប់វិវិវាទកម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: China, Cambodia, Thailand support Joint Border Committee and UN Law to end Cambodia-Thailand dispute

summary: During a trilateral meeting in Yunnan, China, Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn emphasized that Cambodia and Thailand are permanent neighbors and must ensure peace. He thanked China for its role in facilitating the December 27 ceasefire. China announced 20 million RMB in humanitarian aid for Cambodian IDPs. Sokhonn also held bilateral talks with Thai FM Sihasak Phuangketkeow to reaffirm commitment to the ceasefire and the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement.
title: DPM Prak Sokhonn: Cambodia and Thailand Share Responsibility to Ensure Regional Peace and Stability

summary: The Thai Border Joint Situation News Center announced response plans for potential violations after the ceasefire expired at noon. Thailand has established a 'Red Line' (prohibiting sovereignty violation, civilian attacks, or threats). Responses will be proportionate to the level of provocation. Decisions on the 18 prisoners depend on humanitarian and safety assessments.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: วัดใจกัมพูชาหลังครบ 72 ชม.หยุดยิง ไทยยกระดับเฝ้าระวัง-เตือนภัยเชิงรุก
titleEn: Thai-Cambodia: Testing Cambodia's sincerity after 72-hour ceasefire; Thailand elevates proactive surveillance

summary: International travel advisories remain in effect for areas within 50 km of the Thailand-Cambodia border. Access to the Preah Vihear and Banteay Chhmar areas is officially suspended until at least March 31, 2026. While major tourist hubs like Siem Reap and Bangkok remain safe, land border crossings are currently restricted.
title: Thailand–Cambodia Border Issues: Travel Advisory Update

summary: Lt. Gen. Weerayut Raksilp, Commander of the 2nd Army Area, visited 19 soldiers currently hospitalized in Surin for injuries sustained during recent border clashes. He assured the troops and their families that the army would provide full medical care and welfare benefits throughout the New Year period.
title: 'แม่ทัพเติ่ง' เยี่ยม 19 ทหารบาดเจ็บเหตุปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Army Region 2 Commander visits 19 soldiers injured in Thai-Cambodian border clashes

summary: As of 5:10 PM on December 30, the 72-hour ceasefire deadline for the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers has passed without their return. Families and provincial governors, including Pailin Governor Ban Sreymom, reported having no information on the release. The situation is complicated by Thai allegations of 250 Cambodian drone incursions and a landmine incident, which Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense has refuted. Over 590,000 Cambodians remain in displacement shelters.
title: First 72-hours of Ceasefire Expires As Families Await Release of 18 Captured Soldiers

summary: Experts and social observers warn that while physical fighting has stopped, a 'Digitalization War' continues online. They claim Thailand is using fake news and AI-generated content to poison the information environment and cause confusion among Cambodians. The Ministry of Information urged citizens to only follow official government sources to avoid falling into psychological traps.
title: សង្គ្រាមនៅលើសមរភូមិស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ហើយ នៅឡើយតែសង្គ្រាមព័ត៌មាន តើពលរដ្ឋគួរធ្វើដូចម្តេច ដើម្បីកុំឱ្យចាញ់សង្គ្រាមចិត្តសាស្ត្រ?
titleEn: War on the battlefield is quiet, but information war remains; what should citizens do to avoid losing the psychological war?

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held since July 2025. The release occurred at 10:00 AM on December 31, 2025, following a 72-hour ceasefire. The ministry emphasized that the soldiers were treated in accordance with the 1949 Geneva Convention and international humanitarian laws. The ICRC and ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) witnessed the handover, which Thailand hopes will build trust and lead to lasting peace.
title: แถลงการณ์กระทรวงการต่างประเทศเรื่องการส่งทหารกัมพูชา 18 คน กลับกัมพูชา
titleEn: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Statement on the Repatriation of 18 Cambodian Soldiers to Cambodia

summary: Soldiers were repatriated at a border checkpoint between Thailand's Chanthaburi and Cambodia's Pailin province. Thai authorities monitored drone activity (claiming 250 Cambodian drones) before proceeding with the release. The AP notes that the conflict since early December has resulted in 26 Thai military deaths and a total of over 101 casualties across both sides. Families greeted the returning soldiers in Phnom Penh after they were flown in by helicopter.
title: Thailand releases 18 Cambodian prisoners of war as part of ceasefire agreement

summary: The Thai-Cambodian Border Situation Joint Information Center clarified the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers at the Ban Phakkad checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The move follows the General Border Committee (GBC) agreement, reflecting Thailand's stance on peaceful resolution and international humanitarian principles. The military emphasized that this does not compromise national sovereignty, as Thai forces remain on 24-hour high alert.
title: ศูนย์แถลงข่าวร่วมฯ แจงปมปล่อยตัว 18 ทหารกัมพูชา ยันไม่กระทบอธิปไตย-ความมั่นคง
titleEn: Joint Information Center clarifies release of 18 Cambodian soldiers, insists no impact on sovereignty or security

summary: Following their release at the border, the 18 soldiers were flown to Phnom Penh and greeted by hundreds of cheering citizens and family members. The returnees are expected to meet Prime Minister Hun Manet. Residents in the border province of Pailin described the homecoming as a New Year's gift for the nation.
title: Thailand releases 18 Cambodian soldiers held since July

summary: Coordinated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Thailand repatriated 18 soldiers captured in July as a 'goodwill' gesture. ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric stated the move is a critical step for building confidence toward lasting peace. The soldiers arrived in Pailin province before being moved to Phnom Penh.
title: Thailand releases 18 Cambodian soldiers as ceasefire holds

summary: The 18 Cambodian soldiers captured in July 2025 were released at the Prum-Ban Pak Kard border crossing. They were transported to Phnom Penh where thousands of citizens lined the streets to welcome them. The article frames their detention as 'illegal' and highlights their meeting with Prime Minister Hun Manet. International observers like the ICRC and EU welcomed the move as a step toward rebuilding trust.
title: 18 soldiers illegally detained in Thailand for five months come home to a hero's welcome

summary: A highly critical analysis accusing the Thai military of transforming a border row into an 'undeclared war.' The article claims the conflict displaced over 640,000 Cambodians and damaged UNESCO-listed sites like Preah Vihear. Experts quoted in the piece describe Thailand's actions as reflecting 'expansionist ambitions' and a refusal to respect historical treaties (1904/1907) and ICJ rulings.
title: How a border dispute turned into a full-scale invasion of Cambodia

summary: The National Bank of Cambodia (NBC) has issued an urgent announcement to all banking and financial institutions to prioritize debt relief and credit restructuring for soldiers and veterans. This comes after a significant surge in applications for financial assistance from military personnel following the border conflict. The central bank aim to prevent logistical bottlenecks and ensure support for those who served on the frontlines.
title: National Bank Urges Debt Relief Priority for Frontline Soldiers

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that conditions are not yet suitable for a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting proposed by Cambodia for January in Siem Reap. Thailand cited its caretaker government status and the extensive presence of landmines as obstacles to survey and demarcation work. Cambodia had previously sent a diplomatic note to initiate these talks.
title: Conditions not yet met for border meeting with Cambodia: Thai FM spokesperson

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona reaffirmed that Cambodia strictly adheres to the December 27 Joint Statement and will not recognize any border adjustments made through military force. He emphasized that the current deployment of troops does not affect official boundary demarcation.
title: អ្នកនាំពាក្យរាជរដ្ឋាភិបាលបញ្ជាក់ឡើងវិញថា កម្ពុជាមិនទទួលស្គាល់ការកែប្រែព្រំដែន ដោយការប្រើកម្លាំងនោះទេ
titleEn: Government Spokesperson Reaffirms: Cambodia will not recognize boundary changes by force

summary: Senate President Hun Sen expressed his deep sympathy for the 18 soldiers who returned after 155 days of separation from their families. He compared their experience to his own struggles and highlighted the government's commitment to 'leaving no soldier behind.' The government has also established a task force to restore infrastructure and livelihoods damaged during the conflict.
title: សម្តេចតេជោ យល់ទុក្ខលំបាករបស់វីរយុទ្ធជនកម្ពុជា18រូបបែកបាក់ពីគ្រួសារ
titleEn: Samdech Techo understands the hardships of the 18 Cambodian heroic soldiers separated from their families

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) issued a statement welcoming the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held for 155 days. The soldiers were repatriated via the Prum International Point of Entry in Pailin province on December 31. The ministry stated that this move will contribute to building mutual trust and creating an environment for normalizing relations. The process was observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
title: Release of 18 Cambodian Soldiers Seen as Step Toward Restoring Peace and Trust

summary: Thai authorities oversaw the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers at the Ban Phak Kat checkpoint in Chanthaburi on December 31. The move followed a successful 72-hour ceasefire monitoring period agreed upon during the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The process was observed by the ICRC and ASEAN teams to ensure it met international humanitarian standards and the Geneva Conventions.
title: Thailand repatriates 18 Cambodian soldiers after 72-hour border ceasefire

summary: Thailand released 18 Cambodian soldiers on Wednesday (Dec 31) following a ceasefire agreement signed on Dec 27. The soldiers, held for 155 days since July, were repatriated at a border checkpoint after a 72-hour ceasefire observation period. The deal ended 20 days of heavy fighting that killed at least 101 people and displaced over 500,000. The handover was briefly delayed as Thailand investigated alleged drone violations by Cambodia.
title: Thailand frees 18 Cambodian soldiers under new ceasefire deal

summary: The Second Army Region reports that the situation is under control with no heavy weaponry exchanges since the 72-hour ceasefire expired. However, Cambodian drone activity was spotted near Prasat Ta Kwai for reconnaissance, and troop reinforcements continue near Preah Vihear.
title: All is quiet on Cambodia border front

summary: King Norodom Sihamoni and the Queen Mother received the 18 recently released Cambodian soldiers at the Royal Palace. The soldiers, who were held by Thai authorities since fighting began in July 2025, were presented with royal gifts. This high-profile reception followed earlier meetings with Prime Minister Hun Manet and Senate President Hun Sen, underscoring the soldiers' status as national heroes in Cambodia.
title: King Sihamoni, Queen Mother Grant Royal Audience to Freed Cambodian Soldiers
